drills.coaching_notes: Best for poor rebound security, low outlet awareness, weak pivot control, or high turnover risk after rebounds. Assign if the player rebounds and immediately drops, travels, or throws wild passes. Practice rebound and secure without outlet first; ages 7-8 can do no-jump catches and very short outlets.
drills.statistic: A rebound should end with possession, not panic. This teaches secure first, then outlet safely.
drills.safety: No swinging elbows. Outlet distance must match strength.

drills.name: Rebound Land Wide
drills.reps_target: 6-8 reps
drills.instructions: A coach tosses the ball gently. Catch it with two hands and land with feet about shoulder-width apart. Freeze for 2 seconds after landing while the coach checks balance. Start with no jump or small jump only. Do 6-8 reps.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for poor landing control, narrow base, low balance, or rebound instability. Assign if the player catches rebounds and falls, stumbles, or lands with feet too close. Use no-jump catches if landing control is poor; ages 7 should use no-jump catches.
drills.statistic: Rebounding includes landing safely. Young players need landing control before competitive rebounding.
drills.safety: No high tosses. Stop if knee or ankle pain appears.

drills.name: Backboard Track and Catch
drills.reps_target: 6-8 reps both sides
drills.instructions: A coach stands close and tosses the ball softly off the backboard. Watch the ball, step to it, catch with two hands, and secure it. The toss should be easy and predictable at first. Do 6-8 reps from both sides of the hoop.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for poor ball tracking, weak rebound timing, low catching confidence, or missed rebounds. Assign if the player loses the ball off the backboard or mistimes easy rebounds. Use straight-up tosses before backboard tosses if tracking is poor; ages 7 can use soft tosses without jumping.
drills.statistic: Rebounds come off the rim and backboard at different angles. Beginners need simple tracking reps before competitive rebounding.
drills.safety: One player at a time. No crowded rebounding.

drills.name: Rebound Tip to Self
drills.reps_target: 5-6 clean reps
drills.instructions: Stand close to the basket or in open space. The coach tosses the ball softly. Tip it lightly upward once, then catch it with two hands and secure it. Start with very low tosses and no jumping if needed. Do 5-6 clean reps.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for low rebound touch, weak hand control, poor tracking, or low coordination. Assign if the player bats rebounds away instead of controlling them. Use two-hand rebound catch first if the player cannot control the tip; ages 8-9 only with no-jump soft tosses.
drills.statistic: Some rebounds are not caught cleanly right away. A light tip-to-self teaches control, but only after basic catching is safe.
drills.safety: No high jumping, no crowds, no tipping over other players.

drills.name: Loose Ball Stop and Secure
drills.reps_target: 6-8 reps from different angles
drills.instructions: A coach gently rolls the ball a short distance. Move to the ball, stop it with two hands, pick it up, and secure it at the chest. Then pass it back to the coach. Do 6-8 reps from different short angles.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for poor loose-ball awareness, low ball security, weak pickup control, or panic around loose balls. Assign if the player kicks at loose balls, dives unsafely, or cannot secure the ball. Roll the ball slower or closer for younger players.
drills.statistic: Loose balls often lead to chaos. This teaches a safe, controlled pickup before adding speed or competition.
drills.safety: No diving. No sliding on the floor. Secure with two hands.

drills.name: Defensive Rebound Call "Mine"
drills.reps_target: 6-8 reps
drills.instructions: A coach tosses the ball softly. Track the ball, call "mine," catch with two hands, and secure it. Start with one player. Add a second nearby teammate only after the player can communicate safely. Do 6-8 reps.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for low communication, poor rebound ownership, weak ball tracking, or team confusion. Assign if players watch each other and let rebounds drop. Use one player only for younger athletes.
drills.statistic: Communication helps finish possessions. Calling the ball builds ownership and reduces hesitation.
drills.safety: No two-player collisions. Add teammates slowly.

drills.name: Box-Out Then Rebound Toss
drills.reps_target: reps, cone version for young players
drills.instructions: A defender stands in front of a cone or passive partner. The coach calls "shot." The defender turns, gets into a safe box-out position for 1 second, then the coach tosses the ball softly nearby. The defender releases, gets the ball with two hands, and secures it. Use cones instead of partners for younger players.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for poor box-out habit, weak rebound pursuit, low ball security, or low possession finish skill. Assign if the player boxes out but does not go get the ball, or watches the ball without making contact first. Use the no-contact cone version for younger or contact-averse players; ages 8-9 use cone box-outs with no contact.
drills.statistic: Rebounding has two parts: make space and secure the ball. This teaches both without making it a live battle.
drills.safety: No pushing or wrestling. Toss must be soft and close.

drills.name: Chair Height Stance Check
drills.reps_target: 6 reps
drills.instructions: A chair or cone is placed behind the player as a height guide. Drop into a comfortable stance until the hips lightly match the guide height, hold 2 seconds, then stand and reset. Do 6 reps.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for stance depth, leg strength, and posture control. Assign if the player squats too deep, stands too tall, or bends at the waist. Remove the chair and use coach feedback if the player leans back.
drills.statistic: Teaches the athlete to find a stance that is low enough to defend but not so deep that their legs fail.
drills.safety: Keep the rep controlled. Remove speed, contact, or jumping if the athlete loses balance, shows fear, or reports pain.

drills.name: Toe-Heel Balance Stance
drills.reps_target: 8 slow reps
drills.instructions: Get into a stance. The coach says 'toes,' 'heels,' or 'middle.' Gently feel the weight shift, then return to the middle balanced position. Do 8 slow reps.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for balance, foot pressure, and stance control. Assign if the player falls forward, leans back, or cannot freeze in stance. Use standing balance first if stance is too hard.
drills.statistic: Teaches the player to feel balance through the whole foot instead of rocking onto the toes or heels.
drills.safety: Keep the rep controlled. Remove speed, contact, or jumping if the athlete loses balance, shows fear, or reports pain.

drills.name: Defensive Step Stop
drills.reps_target: reps with 1s freeze
drills.instructions: Start in stance, take one short step right, freeze, then return to the middle. Repeat left, forward, and backward. Each rep ends with a 1-second freeze.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for stop control, body control, and foot discipline. Assign if the player drifts, hops, or loses balance after one step. Hold a taller stance for younger athletes.
drills.statistic: Teaches the player to take one defensive step and stop without drifting.
drills.safety: Keep the rep controlled. Remove speed, contact, or jumping if the athlete loses balance, shows fear, or reports pain.

drills.name: Lane Line Shuffle Walk
drills.reps_target: shuffle 6 ft and back
drills.instructions: Start on a lane line in a comfortable stance. Shuffle-walk 6 feet, freeze, then come back. The coach watches for crossed feet and tall posture.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for lateral control, footwork, and balance. Assign if the player crosses feet or cannot keep the body controlled. Shorten distance for ages 7-9.
drills.statistic: Teaches side movement along a court line at a pace the player can control.
drills.safety: Keep the rep controlled. Remove speed, contact, or jumping if the athlete loses balance, shows fear, or reports pain.

drills.name: Corner Close Step
drills.reps_target: both sides
drills.instructions: A cone is placed at the corner and another on the wing. Walk from corner cone to wing cone, slow down, and land in stance with hands up. Do both sides.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for angle movement, stop balance, and hand discipline. Assign if the player runs straight, overshoots, or closes with hands down. Walk only if the player cannot stop safely.
drills.statistic: Teaches the player to close a small angle from corner to wing without running past the spot.
drills.safety: Keep the rep controlled. Remove speed, contact, or jumping if the athlete loses balance, shows fear, or reports pain.

drills.name: Backpedal to Stance
drills.reps_target: 6 reps
drills.instructions: Backpedal 3 slow steps, then drop into a comfortable stance and freeze. Reset and repeat 6 times, keeping eyes forward.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for backpedal control, balance, and stance reset. Assign if the player trips, crosses feet, or leans backward. Use two steps only for younger athletes; ages 7-8 use walking steps.
drills.statistic: Teaches the player to move backward and sit into stance without falling.
drills.safety: Keep the rep controlled. Remove speed, contact, or jumping if the athlete loses balance, shows fear, or reports pain.

drills.name: Diagonal Slide Reset
drills.reps_target: both diagonal directions
drills.instructions: Start at a cone, slide diagonally to a second cone, freeze, then return to the start. Do both diagonal directions slowly.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for diagonal control, balance, and defensive footwork. Assign if the player can slide sideways but loses control diagonally. Walk the pattern first.
drills.statistic: Teaches the player to move diagonally while staying balanced.
drills.safety: Keep the rep controlled. Remove speed, contact, or jumping if the athlete loses balance, shows fear, or reports pain.

drills.name: Hands Up Backpedal
drills.reps_target: reps
drills.instructions: Start near a coach, take 3 controlled backpedal steps with hands up, then freeze. Reset and repeat. No ball pressure is used.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for recovery control, hand activity, and balance. Assign if the player drops hands or falls backward while recovering. Keep hands lower if shoulder fatigue appears.
drills.statistic: Teaches the player to recover with hands high without running into the shooter.
drills.safety: Keep the rep controlled. Remove speed, contact, or jumping if the athlete loses balance, shows fear, or reports pain.

drills.name: Stance Clock Steps
drills.reps_target: short reps
drills.instructions: The coach calls 12, 3, 6, or 9. Take one short step in that direction and reset to the middle. Use slow calls and short reps.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for directional control, reaction, and stance balance. Assign if the player steps the wrong way or cannot reset. Use only two directions first.
drills.statistic: Teaches the player to move to different directions like a clock while staying in control.
drills.safety: Keep the rep controlled. Remove speed, contact, or jumping if the athlete loses balance, shows fear, or reports pain.

drills.name: No-Reach Hip Pocket Defense
drills.reps_target: 15s, switch
drills.instructions: An offensive partner walks slowly in a straight line without a ball. Walk beside them, staying near the hip pocket with hands out but no reaching. Switch after 15 seconds.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for containment, body position, and reach discipline. Assign if the defender reaches or trails behind the offensive player. Use a cone walking path for younger players.
drills.statistic: Teaches the defender to stay near an offensive player's hip without reaching.
drills.safety: Keep the rep controlled. Remove speed, contact, or jumping if the athlete loses balance, shows fear, or reports pain.

drills.name: Shadow Zig-Zag Walk
drills.reps_target: reps, switch roles
drills.instructions: Use cones in a wide zig-zag. The offensive player walks from cone to cone. The defender shadows the path, staying in front without contact. Switch roles.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for change direction, containment, and balance. Assign if the player loses position when direction changes. Use 2 cones only for younger athletes.
drills.statistic: Teaches the player to change direction on defense at walking speed.
drills.safety: Keep the rep controlled. Remove speed, contact, or jumping if the athlete loses balance, shows fear, or reports pain.

drills.name: Stance Talk Drill
drills.reps_target: 10 short calls
drills.instructions: Get into stance. The coach points left, right, ball, or help. Call the word out loud while staying balanced. Do 10 short calls.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for communication, stance control, and focus. Assign if the player stays silent or loses stance while talking. Use simple words for younger players.
drills.statistic: Teaches the player to communicate while holding a defensive position.
drills.safety: Keep the rep controlled. Remove speed, contact, or jumping if the athlete loses balance, shows fear, or reports pain.

drills.name: High-Hand Low-Hand Contest
drills.reps_target: hold 1s, reset
drills.instructions: A coach holds the ball high or low. If high, show one high hand. If low, show one low hand without reaching. Hold 1 second and reset.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for hand discipline, no-foul contest, and visual reaction. Assign if the player reaches, swipes, or uses the wrong hand position. Use no ball first if the player swipes.
drills.statistic: Teaches the defender to choose a high hand for a shot and a low hand for a dribble without swiping.
drills.safety: Keep the rep controlled. Remove speed, contact, or jumping if the athlete loses balance, shows fear, or reports pain.

drills.name: Closeout Brake Steps
drills.reps_target: reps
drills.instructions: Start 8 feet away. Approach a coach with quick but short steps, then use three tiny brake steps and stop with hands up. Reset and repeat.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for braking, closeout control, and balance. Assign if the player cannot slow down or crowds the shooter. Shorten distance if stopping is unsafe; ages 7-8 walk only.
drills.statistic: Teaches the player to use short brake steps at the end of a closeout.
drills.safety: Keep the rep controlled. Remove speed, contact, or jumping if the athlete loses balance, shows fear, or reports pain.

drills.name: Closeout Voice Call
drills.reps_target: reps
drills.instructions: Start near the lane. Coach holds the ball on the wing. Close out slowly, call 'ball,' raise hands, and freeze. If coach raises the ball, say 'shot.'
drills.coaching_notes: Best for communication, closeout control, and focus. Assign if the player closes out silently or loses hand position. Walk speed for younger players.
drills.statistic: Teaches the player to call 'ball' or 'shot' while closing out under control.
drills.safety: Keep the rep controlled. Remove speed, contact, or jumping if the athlete loses balance, shows fear, or reports pain.

drills.name: Help Foot In Paint
drills.reps_target: reps
drills.instructions: Place one cone in the paint and one cone at the defender's player. Step one foot toward the paint cone, point to ball, then recover to the player cone.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for help positioning, recovery, and spacing. Assign if the player never helps or leaves too far. Point only before stepping.
drills.statistic: Teaches the defender where a basic help position can be without overhelping.
drills.safety: Keep the rep controlled. Remove speed, contact, or jumping if the athlete loses balance, shows fear, or reports pain.

drills.name: Corner Ball Deny Hands
drills.reps_target: hold 2s, switch sides
drills.instructions: A receiver stands in the corner. Stand nearby with one hand in the passing lane and one hand toward the receiver. Hold 2 seconds, reset, switch sides.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for deny position, hand control, and spacing. Assign if the player grabs, face-guards, or loses the receiver. Use no live pass at first; younger players use a cone receiver.
drills.statistic: Teaches the player to show one hand in the passing lane without grabbing.
drills.safety: Keep the rep controlled. Remove speed, contact, or jumping if the athlete loses balance, shows fear, or reports pain.

drills.name: Wing Deny Step
drills.reps_target: both sides
drills.instructions: A coach holds the ball at the top. Receiver cone is on the wing. Take one step toward the passing lane, show a hand, then return to neutral. Do both sides.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for deny step, recovery control, and hand discipline. Assign if the player lunges too far or cannot recover. Use a shorter step for younger players.
drills.statistic: Teaches the defender to take one safe step into the passing lane, then recover.
drills.safety: Keep the rep controlled. Remove speed, contact, or jumping if the athlete loses balance, shows fear, or reports pain.

drills.name: Paint Help Hands Wall
drills.reps_target: hold 2s, reset
drills.instructions: Stand in the paint in a comfortable stance. On cue, show both hands wide like a wall, hold 2 seconds, then reset. Add a coach with a ball only if safe.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for help stance, hand activity, and no-foul positioning. Assign if the player reaches down or turns sideways. Lower hands if shoulder fatigue appears.
drills.statistic: Teaches the player to make the body wide in the paint without fouling.
drills.safety: Keep the rep controlled. Remove speed, contact, or jumping if the athlete loses balance, shows fear, or reports pain.

drills.name: Baseline Cut-Off Step
drills.reps_target: freeze, reset, repeat
drills.instructions: A cone marks the baseline drive path. Start inside the lane and step to block the path with body position, not hands. Freeze, reset, repeat.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for baseline containment, body control, and angle awareness. Assign if the player opens the baseline or reaches instead of moving feet. Walk only for younger players.
drills.statistic: Teaches the defender to take one step to cut off the baseline without contact.
drills.safety: Keep the rep controlled. Remove speed, contact, or jumping if the athlete loses balance, shows fear, or reports pain.

drills.name: Shot Hand Switch Contest
drills.reps_target: hold 1s, reset
drills.instructions: Coach holds the ball on the right or left side. Raise the near hand, keep the other hand wide, hold 1 second, then reset. No jumping.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for contest hand choice, hand control, and foul risk. Assign if the player reaches across the body or jumps at the ball. Use no ball if the player swipes.
drills.statistic: Teaches the defender to contest with the hand closest to the ball without crossing the body wildly.
drills.safety: Keep the rep controlled. Remove speed, contact, or jumping if the athlete loses balance, shows fear, or reports pain.

drills.name: Closeout Chop and Turn
drills.reps_target: both directions
drills.instructions: Close out to a coach, chop the feet, then the coach points to a cone. Turn and walk back to that cone. Do both directions.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for closeout recovery, stop control, and direction change. Assign if the player closes out but cannot recover safely. Remove the turn if stopping is unsafe; ages 8-9 walk only.
drills.statistic: Teaches the player to close out, then turn and recover to a new spot under control.
drills.safety: Keep the rep controlled. Remove speed, contact, or jumping if the athlete loses balance, shows fear, or reports pain.

drills.name: Help Tag Step
drills.reps_target: reps
drills.instructions: A cone represents a cutter moving through the lane. Take one controlled step toward the cone, say 'tag,' then recover to the original cone.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for help timing, recovery, and communication. Assign if the player overhelps or never helps. No live cutter at first; younger players use pointing only.
drills.statistic: Teaches a small help step toward a cutter without contact.
drills.safety: Keep the rep controlled. Remove speed, contact, or jumping if the athlete loses balance, shows fear, or reports pain.

drills.name: Skip Ball Point Recover
drills.reps_target: reps
drills.instructions: Coach moves a ball from one side to the other. Point to the new ball spot, take one recovery step, and reset in stance.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for ball awareness, recovery step, and focus. Assign if the player loses the ball when it changes sides. Use slow ball movement.
drills.statistic: Teaches the player to point to a skipped ball and recover stance.
drills.safety: Keep the rep controlled. Remove speed, contact, or jumping if the athlete loses balance, shows fear, or reports pain.

drills.name: Talk Touch Help Cone
drills.reps_target: both sides
drills.instructions: A cone is placed in help position. Say 'help,' walk to touch the cone with a foot, then recover to the start. Do both sides.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for communication, help positioning, and recovery. Assign if the player does not talk or forgets the help spot. Use pointing only for ages 7-8.
drills.statistic: Teaches the player to communicate help while moving to a safe help spot.
drills.safety: Keep the rep controlled. Remove speed, contact, or jumping if the athlete loses balance, shows fear, or reports pain.

drills.name: See Both Shoulder Check
drills.reps_target: reps
drills.instructions: Stand between a ball coach and receiver cone. Coach says 'check.' Glance to the receiver cone, then back to the ball, keeping stance.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for vision, shoulder check, and focus. Assign if the player stares only at the ball or only at the player. Stand tall if the stance hold is tiring.
drills.statistic: Teaches the defender to check over the shoulder without losing stance.
drills.safety: Keep the rep controlled. Remove speed, contact, or jumping if the athlete loses balance, shows fear, or reports pain.

drills.name: No-Swipe Ball Shadow
drills.instructions: Coach holds the ball and slowly moves it side to side. Follow with the hands but never touch the ball. Hold a safe distance for 10 seconds.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for hand discipline, focus, and foul risk. Assign if the player slaps or grabs at the ball. Increase distance if the player reaches.
drills.statistic: Teaches the defender to mirror the ball without trying to steal it.
drills.safety: Keep the rep controlled. Remove speed, contact, or jumping if the athlete loses balance, shows fear, or reports pain.

drills.name: Lane Plug Step
drills.reps_target: reps
drills.instructions: Coach points to the lane. Take one step to the lane line, show hands, say 'help,' then reset. Use cones for location.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for paint help, body position, and communication. Assign if the player stands out of position on drives. No live offense.
drills.statistic: Teaches the player to step into the lane line area to stop a drive path without contact.
drills.safety: Keep the rep controlled. Remove speed, contact, or jumping if the athlete loses balance, shows fear, or reports pain.

drills.name: Recover to Corner Cone
drills.reps_target: reps
drills.instructions: Start near the paint help cone. Coach calls 'corner.' Walk or slide to the corner cone, show hands, and freeze.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for help recovery, closeout angle, and balance. Assign if the player helps but cannot get back under control. Shorten the distance.
drills.statistic: Teaches the player to recover from help position back to the corner safely.
drills.safety: Keep the rep controlled. Remove speed, contact, or jumping if the athlete loses balance, shows fear, or reports pain.

drills.name: Defensive Seatbelt Hands
drills.reps_target: 10s, switch
drills.instructions: Walk beside a partner with hands lightly across the chest like a seatbelt. The goal is foot movement only. Switch roles after 10 seconds.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for foul prevention, foot movement, and body control. Assign if the player uses hands to steer the opponent. Use a cone instead of a partner if contact risk.
drills.statistic: Teaches the player to keep hands safe when moving beside an offensive player.
drills.safety: Keep the rep controlled. Remove speed, contact, or jumping if the athlete loses balance, shows fear, or reports pain.

drills.name: Cut-Off Cone Gate
drills.reps_target: freeze
drills.instructions: Two cones make a gate. Start beside the gate, step into position between the offensive cone and the basket cone, and freeze. No partner needed.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for containment angle, positioning, and body control. Assign if the player does not understand getting between player and basket. Use a larger gate for younger players.
drills.statistic: Teaches the defender to close a gate with body position.
drills.safety: Keep the rep controlled. Remove speed, contact, or jumping if the athlete loses balance, shows fear, or reports pain.

drills.name: Hands High Walk-Through Contest
drills.reps_target: reps from angles
drills.instructions: Walk from one cone to a coach with the ball, lift hands high, hold, back out, and repeat from another angle.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for contest habit, hand activity, and balance. Assign if the player contests with hands low. Lower hands if shoulder fatigue appears.
drills.statistic: Teaches the player to arrive with hands high without jumping.
drills.safety: Keep the rep controlled. Remove speed, contact, or jumping if the athlete loses balance, shows fear, or reports pain.

drills.name: Corner Closeout No Middle
drills.reps_target: freeze
drills.instructions: Coach stands in the corner. Close out slowly with the inside foot shading the middle, hands high, and freeze. No live drive.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for closeout angle, no-middle stance, and balance. Assign if the player gives up the middle immediately. No live offense; younger players use a walk-through.
drills.statistic: Teaches the defender to close out in a way that keeps the ball away from the middle.
drills.safety: Keep the rep controlled. Remove speed, contact, or jumping if the athlete loses balance, shows fear, or reports pain.

drills.name: Help Side Step Line
drills.reps_target: reps
drills.instructions: Use a line from ball to basket as a visual. Walk to the help-side cone, point to ball and player, then reset.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for help-side awareness, positioning, and vision. Assign if the player stands too high, too low, or loses the ball. Use two spots only.
drills.statistic: Teaches the defender to stand on the correct help-side line.
drills.safety: Keep the rep controlled. Remove speed, contact, or jumping if the athlete loses balance, shows fear, or reports pain.

drills.name: Ball Pressure Distance Check
drills.reps_target: freeze
drills.instructions: Coach holds the ball. Step in until one arm could reach space near the ball, then step back to a safe distance and freeze. No reaching.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for ball-pressure distance, balance, and foul risk. Assign if the player crowds or stands too far away. No live dribble.
drills.statistic: Teaches the player to guard at a safe arm-length distance without crowding.
drills.safety: Keep the rep controlled. Remove speed, contact, or jumping if the athlete loses balance, shows fear, or reports pain.

drills.name: Defensive Call and Point
drills.reps_target: 10 calls
drills.instructions: Coach says 'ball,' 'help,' or 'player.' Call it out, point correctly, then reset stance. Do 10 quick but calm calls.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for communication, awareness, and focus. Assign if the player is quiet or confused on defense. Use fewer words for young players.
drills.statistic: Teaches the player to call their job and point to the ball or player.
drills.safety: Keep the rep controlled. Remove speed, contact, or jumping if the athlete loses balance, shows fear, or reports pain.

drills.name: Closeout Feet Under Hips
drills.reps_target: hold 1s, 3 angles
drills.instructions: Close to a cone, stop with feet under the hips, hands up, and hold 1 second. Coach checks for no lunge. Repeat from three angles.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for closeout balance, foot position, and lunge risk. Assign if the player lands too wide, too narrow, or leaning. Walk-through first.
drills.statistic: Teaches the player to finish closeouts with feet under the hips instead of lunging.
drills.safety: Keep the rep controlled. Remove speed, contact, or jumping if the athlete loses balance, shows fear, or reports pain.

drills.name: Help Recover Name Call
drills.reps_target: reps
drills.instructions: Start at the help cone. Coach says 'recover.' Call 'corner' or a teammate name and move back to the cone under control.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for communication, recovery, and team awareness. Assign if the player recovers silently or to the wrong spot. Use spot names before teammate names.
drills.statistic: Teaches the player to recover while naming the teammate or spot they are returning to.
drills.safety: Keep the rep controlled. Remove speed, contact, or jumping if the athlete loses balance, shows fear, or reports pain.

drills.name: No-Middle Foot Angle Hold
drills.reps_target: hold 2s, both sides
drills.instructions: Stand on the wing in stance. Coach checks the top foot and baseline foot. Hold a no-middle angle for 2 seconds, reset, repeat both sides.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for foot angle, no-middle positioning, and stance control. Assign if the player stands square and gives up the middle. Use visual floor tape.
drills.safety: Keep the rep controlled. Remove speed, contact, or jumping if the athlete loses balance, shows fear, or reports pain.

drills.name: Closeout to Contest Voice
drills.reps_target: reps
drills.instructions: Close from 6 feet, say 'contest,' raise hands, and freeze. The coach can pump fake but the defender stays down.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for contest discipline, communication, and pump-fake control. Assign if the player jumps on pump fakes or stays silent. Remove the pump fake for younger players.
drills.statistic: Teaches the player to finish a closeout by saying 'contest' and showing hands without jumping.
drills.safety: Keep the rep controlled. Remove speed, contact, or jumping if the athlete loses balance, shows fear, or reports pain.

drills.name: Box-Out Cone Spin
drills.reps_target: hold 1s, both directions
drills.instructions: Face away from a cone. Coach says 'shot.' Turn, place hips between the cone and basket, hold 1 second, then reset. Do both directions.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for box-out turn, positioning, and balance. Assign if the player turns the wrong way or forgets to get between cone and basket. Use a larger cone target for younger players.
drills.statistic: Teaches the player to turn around a cone and create safe rebounding position without contact.
drills.safety: Keep the rep controlled. Remove speed, contact, or jumping if the athlete loses balance, shows fear, or reports pain.

drills.name: Find Cone Then Ball
drills.reps_target: reps
drills.instructions: A cone represents the opponent. On 'shot,' find the cone, then the coach tosses the ball softly. Get the ball with two hands and secure it.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for find-first habit, tracking, and a secure catch. Assign if the player watches the ball and skips the box-out location. Remove the toss first.
drills.statistic: Teaches the player to locate a player or object first, then track the ball.
drills.safety: Keep the rep controlled. Remove speed, contact, or jumping if the athlete loses balance, shows fear, or reports pain.

drills.name: Hit Air Hold
drills.reps_target: hold 2s, reset
drills.instructions: Turn as if boxing out, take a safe wide base, and hold arms in a safe frame for 2 seconds. No partner. Reset and repeat.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for box-out shape, base control, and arm safety. Assign if the player needs box-out shape before partner contact. Keep arms lower if shoulders tire.
drills.statistic: Teaches box-out contact shape without actually hitting anyone.
drills.safety: Keep the rep controlled. Remove speed, contact, or jumping if the athlete loses balance, shows fear, or reports pain.

drills.name: Rebound Squeeze Hold
drills.reps_target: squeeze 2s
drills.instructions: Start with the ball at the chest, squeeze with two hands for 2 seconds, pivot slightly, then reset. Add a soft toss only if secure.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for ball security, grip strength, and rebound control. Assign if the ball gets knocked loose or slips after the catch. Use a smaller ball for weak hands.
drills.statistic: Teaches the player to squeeze and secure the ball after a rebound.
drills.safety: Keep the rep controlled. Remove speed, contact, or jumping if the athlete loses balance, shows fear, or reports pain.

drills.name: Low Toss Rebound Catch
drills.reps_target: 8 reps
drills.instructions: Coach tosses the ball gently just above chest height. Track it, catch with two hands, land or stand balanced, and secure. Do 8 reps.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for tracking, two-hand catch, and confidence. Assign if the player cannot yet handle backboard or high tosses. Use a foam ball if fear appears.
drills.statistic: Teaches catching a rebound from a low safe toss without jumping.
drills.safety: Keep the rep controlled. Remove speed, contact, or jumping if the athlete loses balance, shows fear, or reports pain.

drills.name: Overhead Secure Walk
drills.reps_target: walk 5 steps
drills.instructions: Hold the ball overhead with two hands, walk 5 steps, bring it to the chest, and reset. Use a smaller ball if needed.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for overhead control, shoulder endurance, and ball security. Assign if the player drops rebounds or brings the ball down too soon. Avoid if shoulder pain appears.
drills.statistic: Teaches the player to hold a rebound strong overhead while walking slowly.
drills.safety: Keep the rep controlled. Remove speed, contact, or jumping if the athlete loses balance, shows fear, or reports pain.

drills.name: Rebound Pivot Square
drills.reps_target: 4 each side
drills.instructions: Start with the ball at the chest, pivot 90 degrees to each side, keep the ball tight, then return square. Do 4 each side.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for pivot control, ball security, and travel risk. Assign if the player rebounds and travels or turns into pressure. No pivot for younger players; use turns only.
drills.statistic: Teaches the player to pivot after securing a rebound without traveling or exposing the ball.
drills.safety: Keep the rep controlled. Remove speed, contact, or jumping if the athlete loses balance, shows fear, or reports pain.

drills.name: Backboard Bounce Read
drills.reps_target: reps
drills.instructions: Coach tosses the ball softly off the backboard to one side. Call 'left' or 'right,' move one step, catch, and secure.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for backboard read, tracking, and reaction. Assign if the player loses the ball after it hits the board. Use a straight toss if reading is poor.
drills.statistic: Teaches the player to read a predictable bounce off the backboard.
drills.safety: Keep the rep controlled. Remove speed, contact, or jumping if the athlete loses balance, shows fear, or reports pain.

drills.name: Rim Bounce Drop Catch
drills.reps_target: reps
drills.instructions: Coach softly bounces the ball off the rim or tosses near the rim. Track, wait, catch with two hands, and secure. Keep tosses easy.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for timing, patience, and catch security. Assign if the player jumps early or slaps at the ball. No crowded rim area; ages 8-9 use coach toss only.
drills.statistic: Teaches the player to wait for the ball to come down instead of grabbing early or swiping.
drills.safety: Keep the rep controlled. Remove speed, contact, or jumping if the athlete loses balance, shows fear, or reports pain.

drills.name: Two-Step Go Get It
drills.reps_target: reps
drills.instructions: Coach tosses the ball softly a short distance away. Take two controlled steps, catch with two hands, and secure.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for pursuit, tracking, and body control. Assign if the player waits for the ball to come to them. Shorter toss for younger players.
drills.statistic: Teaches the player to move two steps to a rebound instead of waiting.
drills.safety: Keep the rep controlled. Remove speed, contact, or jumping if the athlete loses balance, shows fear, or reports pain.

drills.name: Rebound Outside Foot Step
drills.reps_target: reps
drills.instructions: Start in the lane. Coach tosses to the right or left. Step with the outside foot first, gather the ball, and secure.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for first step, rebound range, and tracking. Assign if the player turns awkwardly or steps across the body. Walk-through without the ball first.
drills.statistic: Teaches the player to step with the outside foot toward a rebound angle.
drills.safety: Keep the rep controlled. Remove speed, contact, or jumping if the athlete loses balance, shows fear, or reports pain.

drills.name: Box-Out to Outlet Name
drills.reps_target: reps
drills.instructions: Turn to a cone box-out, coach tosses the ball, secure it and call the outlet teammate's name before a short pass.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for box-out habit, communication, and outlet awareness. Assign if the player rebounds silently or outlets blindly. Short outlet only; younger players use no outlet pass.
drills.statistic: Teaches the player to rebound and call the outlet target by name.
drills.safety: Keep the rep controlled. Remove speed, contact, or jumping if the athlete loses balance, shows fear, or reports pain.

drills.name: Rebound Elbows Safe Check
drills.reps_target: reps
drills.instructions: Hold the ball at the chin. Coach says 'check.' Turn the shoulders slightly left and right while elbows stay controlled, then freeze.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for elbow safety, ball security, and body control. Assign if the player clears space with elbows unsafely. Slow only; no partner contact.
drills.statistic: Teaches the player to secure the ball without swinging elbows.
drills.safety: Keep the rep controlled. Remove speed, contact, or jumping if the athlete loses balance, shows fear, or reports pain.

drills.name: Block-Out Step Back
drills.reps_target: reps
drills.instructions: Face the coach. On 'shot,' turn and take one short step back into box-out space, hold, then get a soft toss.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for box-out space, balance, and rebound timing. Assign if the player runs straight to the rim without making space. Use a cone instead of a partner.
drills.statistic: Teaches the player to step back into space before going to the ball.
drills.safety: Keep the rep controlled. Remove speed, contact, or jumping if the athlete loses balance, shows fear, or reports pain.

drills.name: Rebound Wall Cushion Catch
drills.reps_target: reps
drills.instructions: Coach tosses the ball softly. Catch quietly with two hands and bring it in. Coach listens for loud slaps and cues soft hands.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for soft hands, catch security, and tracking. Assign if the ball pops out of the hands on rebounds. Use a foam ball if nervous.
drills.statistic: Teaches the player to cushion the ball into the hands instead of slapping it.
drills.safety: Keep the rep controlled. Remove speed, contact, or jumping if the athlete loses balance, shows fear, or reports pain.

drills.name: Outlet Fake Secure
drills.reps_target: reps
drills.instructions: Secure the ball. Coach shows hands or keeps hands down. If hands show, outlet. If not, keep the ball tight and pivot.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for decision-making, outlet safety, and ball security. Assign if the player throws the outlet even when the target is not ready. No pressure defender; younger players use one cue only.
drills.statistic: Teaches the player to hold the rebound when the outlet is not open.
drills.safety: Keep the rep controlled. Remove speed, contact, or jumping if the athlete loses balance, shows fear, or reports pain.

drills.name: Rebound Step Through Traffic Cones
drills.reps_target: reps
drills.instructions: Cones make a small lane. Secure a soft toss, then walk through the lane with the ball protected at the chest. Reset and repeat.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for rebound exit, ball protection, and body control. Assign if the player catches but freezes under the rim. Make the lane wider.
drills.statistic: Teaches the player to move out of rebounding traffic after securing the ball.
drills.safety: Keep the rep controlled. Remove speed, contact, or jumping if the athlete loses balance, shows fear, or reports pain.

drills.name: Weak-Side Cone Crash
drills.reps_target: reps
drills.instructions: Start at the weak-side cone. Coach says 'shot' and tosses the ball to the middle. Step in, catch, and secure.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for weak-side rebounding, pursuit, and tracking. Assign if the player stays on the weak side and watches. Walk-in only for young athletes.
drills.statistic: Teaches the player to move from the weak-side cone toward rebound space.
drills.safety: Keep the rep controlled. Remove speed, contact, or jumping if the athlete loses balance, shows fear, or reports pain.

drills.name: Box-Out Call Shot Partner
drills.reps_target: hold 1s, reset
drills.instructions: A partner stands behind. Coach says shot. Say 'shot,' turn, create safe space, hold 1 second, and reset.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for communication, box-out reaction, and contact readiness. Assign if the player forgets to call or turn. No pushing; ages 8-9 use a cone partner.
drills.statistic: Teaches the player to call 'shot' and turn to box out a passive partner.
drills.safety: Keep the rep controlled. Remove speed, contact, or jumping if the athlete loses balance, shows fear, or reports pain.

drills.name: Rebound High-Low Secure
drills.reps_target: reps
drills.instructions: Coach alternates a soft high toss and a chest-height toss. Catch with two hands and secure each one. Keep the high toss safe.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for catch range, tracking, and hand strength. Assign if the player handles one height but not another. No high toss for younger players.
drills.statistic: Teaches the player to secure rebounds from different heights.
drills.safety: Keep the rep controlled. Remove speed, contact, or jumping if the athlete loses balance, shows fear, or reports pain.

drills.name: Tip Check No Chase
drills.reps_target: reps
drills.instructions: Coach tosses the ball. Only tip if you can control it; otherwise catch or let the coach reset. The goal is a good decision, not chaos.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for tip decision, control, and safety awareness. Assign if the player tips every ball wildly. Use catch-only for younger players.
drills.statistic: Teaches the player not to chase uncontrolled tips.
drills.safety: Keep the rep controlled. Remove speed, contact, or jumping if the athlete loses balance, shows fear, or reports pain.

drills.name: Board Touch Land Freeze
drills.reps_target: freeze 2s
drills.instructions: Reach or lightly jump to touch a low target, land, and freeze for 2 seconds. Coach checks knees and balance.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for landing control, rebound timing, and balance. Assign if the player lands narrow or stumbles. Reach-only if landing is poor; ages 7-8 reach only.
drills.statistic: Teaches the player to land and freeze after a rebound-style reach.
drills.safety: Keep the rep controlled. Remove speed, contact, or jumping if the athlete loses balance, shows fear, or reports pain.

drills.name: Rebound Turn and Face Coach
drills.reps_target: both sides
drills.instructions: Catch a soft toss, secure the ball, turn under control, and face the coach without passing. Do both sides.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for post-rebound awareness, ball security, and pivot control. Assign if the player catches and looks down or turns blindly. No pass until control improves.
drills.statistic: Teaches the player to secure the ball and find the coach/outlet with the eyes.
drills.safety: Keep the rep controlled. Remove speed, contact, or jumping if the athlete loses balance, shows fear, or reports pain.

drills.name: Box-Out Seat Position
drills.reps_target: hold 2s, reset
drills.instructions: Face away from a cone, drop the hips slightly like sitting into space, hold 2 seconds, then reset. No partner.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for box-out base, hip position, and balance. Assign if the player stands tall or bends at the waist. Do not squat deeply.
drills.statistic: Teaches the player to sit the hips back into a safe box-out base without contact.
drills.safety: Keep the rep controlled. Remove speed, contact, or jumping if the athlete loses balance, shows fear, or reports pain.

drills.name: Rebound Catch Above Eyes
drills.reps_target: reps
drills.instructions: Coach tosses the ball gently above the forehead. Catch with two hands above the eyes, then bring it down safely to the chest.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for high catch, hand strength, and tracking. Assign if the player catches everything low or lets the ball drop. Use a smaller ball if strength is low; younger players use a lower toss.
drills.statistic: Teaches the player to catch the ball above eye level when possible.
drills.safety: Keep the rep controlled. Remove speed, contact, or jumping if the athlete loses balance, shows fear, or reports pain.

drills.name: Loose Ball Foot Stop
drills.reps_target: reps
drills.instructions: Coach rolls the ball slowly. Step beside it, stop it lightly with the foot, then bend and secure with two hands.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for loose-ball control, body control, and pickup safety. Assign if the player kicks wildly or dives. Use a hands-only pickup if the foot stop is unsafe.
drills.statistic: Teaches the player to stop a rolling ball safely before picking it up.
drills.safety: Keep the rep controlled. Remove speed, contact, or jumping if the athlete loses balance, shows fear, or reports pain.

drills.name: Loose Ball Turn Away Secure
drills.reps_target: reps
drills.instructions: Coach places the ball on the floor. Pick it up with two hands, turn away from cone pressure, and hold tight.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for loose-ball security, turn control, and protection. Assign if the player picks up the ball and exposes it. No live defender.
drills.statistic: Teaches the player to secure a loose ball and turn away from pressure.
drills.safety: Keep the rep controlled. Remove speed, contact, or jumping if the athlete loses balance, shows fear, or reports pain.

drills.name: Rebound Outlet Walk Lane
drills.reps_target: reps
drills.instructions: Catch a soft toss, take two controlled steps toward a sideline cone, then pass to an outlet partner. Keep the pass short.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for outlet lane, ball security, and pass control. Assign if the player outlets from a bad angle or rushes. Remove the pass for younger athletes.
drills.statistic: Teaches the player to rebound, walk to a safe outlet lane, and pass short.
drills.safety: Keep the rep controlled. Remove speed, contact, or jumping if the athlete loses balance, shows fear, or reports pain.

drills.name: Box-Out Voice Check
drills.reps_target: reps
drills.instructions: Coach says 'shot.' Say 'find,' turn to a cone/partner, hold a box-out shape, then say 'ball.' No rebound needed.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for communication, sequence memory, and box-out habit. Assign if the player forgets the order after a shot. Use one cue for ages 7-8.
drills.statistic: Teaches players to say the box-out cue before moving.
drills.safety: Keep the rep controlled. Remove speed, contact, or jumping if the athlete loses balance, shows fear, or reports pain.

drills.name: Rebound Secure Under Chin
drills.reps_target: hold 2s
drills.instructions: Catch a coach toss, bring the ball under the chin/chest, elbows safe, and hold 2 seconds. Coach checks for strong hands.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for ball protection, hand strength, and rebound security. Assign if the player brings the rebound to the waist or exposes it. Smaller ball if hands are weak.
drills.statistic: Teaches the player to hold the ball strong under the chin after a rebound.
drills.safety: Keep the rep controlled. Remove speed, contact, or jumping if the athlete loses balance, shows fear, or reports pain.

drills.name: Guard-Rebound Switch Cue
drills.reps_target: reps
drills.instructions: Start in stance. Coach calls 'guard' for 3 seconds, then 'shot.' Turn to a cone, hold box-out shape, then secure a soft toss.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for the transition from defense to board, reaction, and box-out habit. Assign if the player keeps guarding and forgets the rebound. Cone only for younger players.
drills.statistic: Teaches the player to switch from guarding to rebounding when the coach calls shot.
drills.safety: Keep the rep controlled. Remove speed, contact, or jumping if the athlete loses balance, shows fear, or reports pain.

drills.name: Deny to Rebound Turn
drills.reps_target: reps
drills.instructions: Start denying a cone receiver. Coach says 'shot.' Turn to the box-out cone, hold, then reset. Add a ball toss only if safe.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for deny-to-rebound, reaction, and position change. Assign if the player denies but never finds a body on the shot. No partner contact first.
drills.statistic: Teaches the player to move from denial position into rebound position.
drills.safety: Keep the rep controlled. Remove speed, contact, or jumping if the athlete loses balance, shows fear, or reports pain.

drills.name: Help to Hit to Get
drills.reps_target: reps
drills.instructions: Start at the help cone. Coach says 'shot.' Find the box-out cone, hold 1 second, then get a soft toss and secure.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for help position, box-out habit, and possession finish. Assign if the player helps but does not finish the possession. Remove the toss if the sequence is hard; younger players use first two parts only.
drills.statistic: Teaches help position, box-out shape, and ball secure in a simple sequence.
drills.safety: Keep the rep controlled. Remove speed, contact, or jumping if the athlete loses balance, shows fear, or reports pain.

drills.name: Closeout Rebound Callout
drills.reps_target: reps
drills.instructions: Close out to a coach. Coach raises the ball. Say 'shot,' turn to a cone, say 'find,' then hold box-out shape.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for communication, closeout, and rebound reaction. Assign if the player is quiet or stops after the contest. Walk speed only.
drills.statistic: Teaches the defender to close out, call shot, then communicate rebound.
drills.safety: Keep the rep controlled. Remove speed, contact, or jumping if the athlete loses balance, shows fear, or reports pain.

drills.name: Two-Player Safe Board Share
drills.reps_target: reps
drills.instructions: Two players stand apart. Coach tosses the ball softly between them and calls one name. The called player secures; the other stops and boxes out air.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for communication, safety, and rebound ownership. Assign if players collide or both grab blindly. One player only if safety is poor; younger players use wider spacing.
drills.statistic: Teaches two teammates to avoid colliding when going for the same ball.
drills.safety: Keep the rep controlled. Remove speed, contact, or jumping if the athlete loses balance, shows fear, or reports pain.

drills.name: Find Ball Find Outlet
drills.reps_target: reps
drills.instructions: Catch a soft toss, secure it, then point to the outlet coach before passing or resetting. Start without a pass.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for tracking, outlet awareness, and decision. Assign if the player catches and looks down or panics. Remove the pass if needed.
drills.statistic: Teaches the player to track the rebound and immediately find a safe outlet target.
drills.safety: Keep the rep controlled. Remove speed, contact, or jumping if the athlete loses balance, shows fear, or reports pain.

drills.name: Defensive Slide to Loose Ball
drills.reps_target: reps
drills.instructions: Slide two short steps to a cone. Coach rolls the ball nearby. Stop, bend the knees, secure the ball with two hands.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for slide control, loose-ball pickup, and body control. Assign if the player rushes from a slide into an unsafe pickup. No speed, no diving; ages 7-8 walk only.
drills.statistic: Teaches the player to slide, stop, then secure a loose ball safely.
drills.safety: Keep the rep controlled. Remove speed, contact, or jumping if the athlete loses balance, shows fear, or reports pain.

drills.name: Closeout to Loose Ball Secure
drills.reps_target: reps
drills.instructions: Close to a cone, freeze, then the coach rolls the ball to the side. Move under control and secure with two hands.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for closeout stop, loose-ball control, and balance. Assign if the player cannot stop before chasing the ball. Walk the closeout first.
drills.statistic: Teaches the player to close out, stop, then pick up a loose ball safely.
drills.safety: Keep the rep controlled. Remove speed, contact, or jumping if the athlete loses balance, shows fear, or reports pain.

drills.name: Rebound Escape Pivot No Pass
drills.reps_target: reps
drills.instructions: Catch a soft toss, secure it, coach points left or right. Pivot away and hold. No outlet pass.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for pivot protection, ball security, and decision patience. Assign if the player catches and throws blindly. No pivot for younger players.
drills.statistic: Teaches the player to pivot out of pressure after a rebound without forcing a pass.
drills.safety: Keep the rep controlled. Remove speed, contact, or jumping if the athlete loses balance, shows fear, or reports pain.

drills.name: Box-Out Balance Push Test
drills.reps_target: reps
drills.instructions: Set a no-contact box-out shape. Coach gives a light shoulder-level air tap or tiny pad pressure. Hold balance. No pushing back.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for balance, contact readiness, and base strength. Assign if the player falls from small pressure or pushes back. Avoid for contact-averse or younger players.
drills.statistic: Teaches the player to hold a box-out base against a very light coach check.
drills.safety: Keep the rep controlled. Remove speed, contact, or jumping if the athlete loses balance, shows fear, or reports pain.

drills.name: Wall Rebound Hand Tap
drills.reps_target: 8 reps
drills.instructions: Face the wall, reach to tap a safe target with both hands, then bring hands to the chest. Do 8 reps. No ball needed.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for reach pattern, hand speed, and shoulder control. Assign if the player struggles reaching safely overhead. Lower the target if shoulder fatigue.
drills.statistic: Teaches the player to tap a wall target with two hands like reaching for a rebound.
drills.safety: Keep the rep controlled. Remove speed, contact, or jumping if the athlete loses balance, shows fear, or reports pain.

drills.name: Rebound Count the Bounce
drills.reps_target: reps
drills.instructions: Coach bounces the ball off the floor or board. Count 'one' when it bounces, then catch with two hands and secure.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for tracking focus, timing, and catch security. Assign if the player loses sight of the ball after the bounce. Use a soft floor bounce first.
drills.statistic: Teaches the player to track ball flight and bounce before securing it.
drills.safety: Keep the rep controlled. Remove speed, contact, or jumping if the athlete loses balance, shows fear, or reports pain.

drills.name: Shot Fake Stay Down Board
drills.reps_target: reps
drills.instructions: Coach holds the ball and gives a slow shot fake. Keep the feet down. Coach then says shot; turn to a cone box-out shape.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for discipline, contest control, and rebound reaction. Assign if the player jumps on the fake or forgets the rebound. Slow fake only; younger players no fake.
drills.statistic: Teaches the defender to stay down on a shot fake, then rebound on cue.
drills.safety: Keep the rep controlled. Remove speed, contact, or jumping if the athlete loses balance, shows fear, or reports pain.

drills.name: Paint Wall to Board
drills.reps_target: reps
drills.instructions: Start in a paint wall stance with hands wide. Coach says 'shot.' Turn to a cone and secure a soft toss.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for help stance, rebound reaction, and a secure catch. Assign if the player helps but watches the shot. Remove the toss for young athletes.
drills.statistic: Teaches the player to show help in the paint, then turn for a rebound.
drills.safety: Keep the rep controlled. Remove speed, contact, or jumping if the athlete loses balance, shows fear, or reports pain.

drills.name: Corner Box-Out Cone Pair
drills.reps_target: hold
drills.instructions: Two cones mark the shooter and basket line in the corner. Turn from the shooter cone, place the body between the cone and basket, and hold.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for corner rebound angle, box-out position, and balance. Assign if the player boxes out in the wrong direction from the corner. Walk-through only.
drills.statistic: Teaches box-out positioning from the corner area without contact.
drills.safety: Keep the rep controlled. Remove speed, contact, or jumping if the athlete loses balance, shows fear, or reports pain.

drills.name: Wing Shot Long Board Read
drills.reps_target: reps
drills.instructions: Coach stands on the wing and tosses the ball toward the free throw area. Start in the lane, step to the ball, and secure. Keep the toss soft.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for rebound angle, long board awareness, and tracking. Assign if the player expects every rebound under the rim. Short toss only if tracking is poor; younger players use a shorter toss.
drills.statistic: Teaches the player that wing shots can create longer rebounds.
drills.safety: Keep the rep controlled. Remove speed, contact, or jumping if the athlete loses balance, shows fear, or reports pain.

drills.name: Baseline Miss Track
drills.reps_target: reps
drills.instructions: Coach tosses from the baseline side to the backboard or air. Track the angle, move one or two steps, catch, and secure.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for angle tracking, movement, and catch security. Assign if the player misreads baseline misses. No high toss.
drills.statistic: Teaches the player to track a rebound coming from a baseline angle.
drills.safety: Keep the rep controlled. Remove speed, contact, or jumping if the athlete loses balance, shows fear, or reports pain.

drills.name: Free Throw Rebound Spot Walk
drills.reps_target: reps
drills.instructions: Start on a marked lane spot. Coach says 'shot.' Step into a safe rebounding position and freeze. Add a soft toss later.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for free throw position, step timing, and balance. Assign if the player stands in the wrong spot or steps early. No contact or live free throw.
drills.statistic: Teaches the player where to stand and how to step during a free throw rebound without contact.
drills.safety: Keep the rep controlled. Remove speed, contact, or jumping if the athlete loses balance, shows fear, or reports pain.

drills.name: Rebound and Tuck Walk
drills.reps_target: reps
drills.instructions: Catch a soft toss, tuck the ball safely to the chest/side, walk three steps to an outlet cone, freeze. No pass needed.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for ball security, movement control, and outlet prep. Assign if the player drops the ball while moving after a rebound. Shorter walk for younger athletes.
drills.statistic: Teaches the player to secure the ball and walk out safely without exposing it.
drills.safety: Keep the rep controlled. Remove speed, contact, or jumping if the athlete loses balance, shows fear, or reports pain.

drills.name: Two Hands Above Traffic
drills.reps_target: reps
drills.instructions: Coach tosses the ball overhead. Reach with two hands, catch, and bring it tight. No jumping unless landing is safe.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for two-hand catch, overhead control, and security. Assign if the player uses one hand or waits too low. Smaller ball if strength is low; younger players use a lower toss.
drills.statistic: Teaches the player to catch with two hands above imaginary traffic, then secure safely.
drills.safety: Keep the rep controlled. Remove speed, contact, or jumping if the athlete loses balance, shows fear, or reports pain.

drills.name: Outlet Target Look First
drills.reps_target: reps
drills.instructions: Catch a soft toss, secure, turn the head to the outlet target, say the target name, then pass short or reset.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for outlet vision, decision, and pass safety. Assign if the player throws the outlet without looking. No pass if the target is not ready.
drills.statistic: Teaches the player to look at the outlet before passing after a rebound.
drills.safety: Keep the rep controlled. Remove speed, contact, or jumping if the athlete loses balance, shows fear, or reports pain.

drills.name: Rebound Protect Against Cone
drills.reps_target: hold 2s
drills.instructions: Secure the ball. A cone represents a defender. Pivot so the back/side protects the ball from the cone, hold 2 seconds.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for rebound protection, pivot control, and ball security. Assign if the player exposes the ball toward pressure. Turn only, no pivot for young players.
drills.statistic: Teaches the player to keep the body between ball and imaginary defender after securing a rebound.
drills.safety: Keep the rep controlled. Remove speed, contact, or jumping if the athlete loses balance, shows fear, or reports pain.

drills.name: Defensive Turn Find Rim
drills.reps_target: reps
drills.instructions: Start facing away from the hoop. Coach says shot. Turn, point to the rim, then get in rebounding position. Add a ball later.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for rim awareness, turn control, and rebound orientation. Assign if the player turns and loses rim location. No ball first.
drills.statistic: Teaches the player to know where the rim is after turning for a rebound.
drills.safety: Keep the rep controlled. Remove speed, contact, or jumping if the athlete loses balance, shows fear, or reports pain.

drills.name: Miss Direction Call
drills.reps_target: reps
drills.instructions: Coach calls 'short,' 'long,' 'left,' or 'right.' Take one step that direction and get into rebound-ready hands. Add a toss if safe.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for reaction, rebound language, and first step. Assign if the player does not understand miss directions. Use two directions first.
drills.statistic: Teaches the player to react to the coach's call for where the miss goes.
drills.safety: Keep the rep controlled. Remove speed, contact, or jumping if the athlete loses balance, shows fear, or reports pain.

drills.name: Safe Box-Out Release
drills.reps_target: reps
drills.instructions: Hold a box-out shape on a cone. Coach says 'release.' Step to a soft ball toss and secure. Reset.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for box-out timing, release, and ball secure. Assign if the player never goes to the ball after boxing out. No partner contact; younger players cone only.
drills.statistic: Teaches the player when to release the box-out and go to the ball.
drills.safety: Keep the rep controlled. Remove speed, contact, or jumping if the athlete loses balance, shows fear, or reports pain.

drills.name: Deflect Stance Hands Only
drills.reps_target: reps
drills.instructions: Coach gently tosses a soft or foam ball through a lane. Reach one hand into the lane to tap it softly down, then reset.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for hand activity, timing, and no-contact defense. Assign if the player swings hard or reaches across the body. Younger players use a balloon or foam only. Avoid with finger pain.
drills.statistic: Teaches the player to use quick hands in a safe lane without body contact.
drills.safety: Keep the rep controlled. Remove speed, contact, or jumping if the athlete loses balance, shows fear, or reports pain.

drills.name: No-Jump Rebound Contest
drills.reps_target: reps
drills.instructions: Coach tosses the ball chest-high between the player and open space. Step to position, catch with two hands, and secure without jumping.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for position, two-hand catch, and low-impact rebound. Assign if the player jumps unnecessarily or loses balance. Keep the toss chest high.
drills.statistic: Teaches the player to win position and catch without jumping.
drills.safety: Keep the rep controlled. Remove speed, contact, or jumping if the athlete loses balance, shows fear, or reports pain.

drills.name: Board Tap Count Hold
drills.reps_target: freeze
drills.instructions: Reach to touch a low backboard or target twice, then freeze in a balanced stance. Use reach-only unless jumping is safe.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for reach control, landing if used, and shoulder control. Assign if the player cannot reach safely or lands poorly. Stop if shoulder or knee pain; ages 7-8 reach a lower target.
drills.statistic: Teaches safe repeated reach without high jump volume.
drills.safety: Keep the rep controlled. Remove speed, contact, or jumping if the athlete loses balance, shows fear, or reports pain.

drills.name: Rebound Footwork Square-Up
drills.reps_target: reps
drills.instructions: Catch a soft toss, land or stand wide, pivot to square the shoulders to the coach, and hold the ball secure.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for square-up, pivot control, and ball security. Assign if the player catches but stays turned or off balance. No outlet pass until stable.
drills.statistic: Teaches the player to square the body after a rebound before making the next play.
drills.safety: Keep the rep controlled. Remove speed, contact, or jumping if the athlete loses balance, shows fear, or reports pain.

drills.name: Loose Ball Call and Cover
drills.reps_target: reps
drills.instructions: Coach rolls the ball slowly. Say 'ball,' move to it, cover with two hands, pick up, and secure.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for communication, loose-ball control, and security. Assign if the player is silent or swipes at the ball. No diving.
drills.statistic: Teaches the player to call the loose ball and cover it safely with two hands.
drills.safety: Keep the rep controlled. Remove speed, contact, or jumping if the athlete loses balance, shows fear, or reports pain.

drills.name: Early Pick-Up Two-Step Finish
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: The player starts at the wing with one dribble available. The player takes one controlled dribble, picks the ball up earlier than normal, takes two clean steps, and finishes softly off the glass. The coach should mark the pick-up spot with a cone. Work both sides.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players who rush the last step near the rim. Triggers: Assign if the player picks the ball up too late or gets trapped under the rim. Avoid/modify: Use beginner two-step gather work first if the athlete cannot control basic layup footwork. Focus: Best for gather timing, stride control, rim spacing, and finish balance.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the player to pick the ball up earlier before the rim so the finish is calm instead of rushed. It helps players who take the ball too deep and get stuck under the basket.
drills.safety: No full-speed drives at first. The player must land balanced before the drill progresses.

drills.name: Late Pick-Up Extension Finish
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: The player starts outside the lane. The player takes one controlled dribble toward the rim, keeps the ball low and protected, picks it up on the last safe step, and extends for a controlled finish. Work both hands and both sides.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players who show the ball too early on drives. Triggers: Assign if the player gets stripped before finishing or picks the ball up too soon. Avoid/modify: Remove speed if the player loses the ball on the gather. Focus: Best for ball protection, gather timing, extension control, and weak-hand confidence.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the player to delay the pick-up just enough to protect the ball and extend near the rim. It helps players who expose the ball too early.
drills.safety: Keep the drive controlled. No reaching defender until the player controls the gather safely.

drills.name: Outside-Foot Veer Finish
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: Place a cone on the lane line as imaginary help. The player drives from the wing, steps with the outside foot to slightly veer away from the cone, and finishes with the outside hand. Keep the veer small. Work both sides.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players who drive straight into help. Triggers: Assign if the player finishes straight into the defender's chest or loses angle control. Avoid/modify: Use a walk-through version if the player jumps sideways or lands poorly. Focus: Best for angle creation, body control, outside-hand finishing, and help awareness.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the player to step slightly away from the defender's line while still finishing at the rim. It helps the athlete create a clean angle without jumping sideways out of control.
drills.safety: The veer should be small. No sideways jumping into another player.

drills.name: Inside-Shoulder Shield Finish
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: A cone or pad sits near the block. The player drives from the wing, keeps the inside shoulder between the cone and the ball, and finishes with the outside hand. The player should not swing the shoulder or create contact. Work both sides.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players who expose the ball on finishes. Triggers: Assign if the player brings the ball across the body or gets stripped near the rim. Avoid/modify: Use no obstacle if the athlete turns the shoulder into contact. Focus: Best for ball protection, shoulder alignment, outside-hand finishing, and rim confidence.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the player to use the inside shoulder as a shield while finishing with the outside hand. It helps the player protect the ball from imaginary help.
drills.safety: No shoulder checking. The shoulder is a shield, not a hit.

drills.name: Two-Hand Gather High Finish
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: The player starts near the lane line. On the drive, the player gathers with two hands, brings the ball high near the chest or shoulder, and finishes softly. The coach cues "catch it high, keep it high." Work both sides.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players who drop the ball before finishing. Triggers: Assign if the player lowers the ball near traffic before finishing. Avoid/modify: Lower the speed if the player cannot gather cleanly. Focus: Best for two-hand gather, ball security, high finish control, and rim protection.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the player to gather the ball with two hands, keep it high, and finish before bringing it down. It helps players who lower the ball and get stripped.
drills.safety: No defender reaching at first. The athlete must control the ball before pressure is added.

drills.name: Gather Outside the Paint Finish
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: Place a cone just outside the paint. The player must gather before or at the cone, then take controlled steps into the finish. The player finishes off the glass or at the front of the rim. Work both sides.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players who drive too far under the basket. Triggers: Assign if the player ends up behind the backboard or under the rim. Avoid/modify: Use a closer starting point if the player overstrides. Focus: Best for paint spacing, gather timing, finish balance, and rim awareness.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the player to gather before entering a crowded paint area. It helps players who drive too deep and lose space to finish.
drills.safety: No long lunging steps. The player should stay balanced through the gather.

drills.name: High-Low Ball Pocket Finish
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: The player starts on the wing and drives slowly. The ball stays low and protected during the first step, then moves high on the second step into the finish. The coach watches that the ball path is tight, not wide.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players who swing the ball wide on finishes. Triggers: Assign if the ball gets loose or exposed during the gather. Avoid/modify: Use a stationary ball-path rehearsal before driving. Focus: Best for ball path, protection, gather control, and finishing hand strength.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the player to move the ball from low protection to a high finish without exposing it. It helps with protected finishes near defenders.
drills.safety: Keep the ball close to the body. No wide swinging motion.

drills.name: Front-Rim Two-Foot Stop Finish
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: The player drives from the slot, takes one controlled dribble, jump-stops in front of the rim, and finishes softly. The player must land balanced before the ball goes up. Work straight-on and slight-angle approaches.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players who rush into the rim. Triggers: Assign if the player charges into the rim area or loses balance before finishing. Avoid/modify: Use no-dribble footwork first if stop control is poor. Focus: Best for stop control, two-foot balance, paint patience, and finish touch.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the player to stop on two feet in front of the rim and finish under control. It helps players who cannot slow down in the paint.
drills.safety: No hard jump stops from full speed. Control comes before speed.

drills.name: Side-Rim Window Finish
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: Place a cone at the side of the rim area. The player drives from the wing and must finish before crossing behind the cone. The finish should be soft and controlled off the side window of the backboard.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players who drive too far past the rim. Triggers: Assign if the player ends behind the backboard or loses the finishing window. Avoid/modify: Move the cone closer to teach a wider safe window first. Focus: Best for rim angle, backboard touch, body control, and timing.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the player to finish through a small side-rim window without going behind the basket. It helps with angle control on drives from the wing.
drills.safety: Do not jump under or behind the backboard. Stay clear of the support.

drills.name: Far-Corner Glass Finish
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: The player starts near the short wing. The player attacks at a 45-degree angle and aims for a higher far-corner glass target. The finish should be soft, not a hard throw. Do both sides with both hands when safe.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players who miss angled layups long or flat. Triggers: Assign if the player uses the same backboard target from every angle. Avoid/modify: Move closer if the player cannot control the touch. Focus: Best for glass touch, angle finishing, release control, and hand selection.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the player to use the far corner of the glass on an angled finish. It helps with touch when the player is not directly square to the rim.
drills.safety: No fast approach until touch is consistent.

drills.name: Same-Side High Glass Finish
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: The player starts near the lane line and drives under control. The player finishes high on the same-side glass with a soft release. The coach should cue "high and soft," not "hard." Work both sides.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players who finish too low on the glass. Triggers: Assign if the player hits the bottom of the rim or throws flat layups. Avoid/modify: Start closer if the player lacks strength or touch. Focus: Best for release height, backboard touch, arc control, and soft hands.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the player to finish softly high on the same side of the glass. It helps players avoid throwing the ball too low into the rim or defender.
drills.safety: No contact. Keep the approach short.

drills.name: Rim Side Change Finish
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: The player starts under control on one side of the lane, takes two steps, and finishes on the opposite side of the rim with a soft release. The player should stay close to the floor and avoid twisting wildly. Work both directions.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players learning controlled side changes near the rim. Triggers: Assign if the player has basic finishing but cannot adjust around the rim. Avoid/modify: Avoid if the player twists in the air or lands off balance. Focus: Best for rim adjustment, body control, release timing, and landing safety.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the player to approach one side of the rim and finish on the other side without making it acrobatic. It helps players learn simple rim-side adjustment.
drills.safety: No wild mid-air twist. Land balanced or remove the drill.

drills.name: Baseline Window Reverse Touch
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: The player starts on the baseline short corner. The player takes one controlled dribble, steps under control, and finishes on the near side of the rim using soft touch. The player must stay clear of the backboard support.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players who need better tight-angle finishing. Triggers: Assign if the player drives baseline and gets stuck behind the hoop. Avoid/modify: Avoid if the court has limited baseline safety space. Focus: Best for baseline angle, touch, body control, and rim awareness.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the player to use a controlled baseline window without drifting behind the basket. It helps with touch and timing from tight angles.
drills.safety: Check the baseline space first. No jumping into the wall, padding, or support.

drills.name: Short-Corner One-Dribble Finish
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: The player starts in the short corner. The player takes one strong but controlled dribble toward the lane, gathers, and finishes with the proper hand. Work both sides. The coach should watch the gather spot.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players learning short-corner finishing angles. Triggers: Assign if the player catches short corner and has no controlled finishing option. Avoid/modify: Use no-dribble short-corner finishing first if the athlete cannot control the step. Focus: Best for short-corner attack, gather location, hand choice, and rim spacing.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the player to attack from the short corner with one controlled dribble and finish before drifting too far under the rim.
