drills.safety: No baseline sprinting. Keep the attack short and controlled.

drills.name: Elbow Dive Finish
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: The player starts at the elbow. The coach passes or hands the ball to the player. The player takes one controlled step toward the rim, gathers, and finishes. Work both elbows and both hands when safe.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players who catch at the elbow and need a simple rim attack. Triggers: Assign if the player catches at the elbow and rushes or freezes. Avoid/modify: Use a self-start version if catching and moving is too hard. Focus: Best for elbow attack, first step, gather control, and finish timing.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the player to dive from the elbow area into a controlled finish. It helps with finishing after catching near the high post or elbow.
drills.safety: No full-speed dive. The player must keep the gather clean.

drills.name: Slot Angle Finish
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: The player starts at the slot. The player drives at a slight angle, gathers before the paint, and finishes off the correct side of the glass. Work both slots. The coach should cue "angle first, speed second."
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players learning slot-drive finishing. Triggers: Assign if the player drives from the slot with no angle or poor finish balance. Avoid/modify: Start closer if the player overstrides. Focus: Best for slot attack, angle control, gather timing, and backboard touch.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the player to finish from the slot with a better angle and controlled steps. It helps players who drive from the slot and run straight into the rim.
drills.safety: No overstriding. Keep the drive at controlled speed.

drills.name: Wing-to-Middle Finish
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: The player starts on the wing. A cone blocks the outside lane. The player takes one controlled dribble toward the middle, gathers, and finishes through the middle side of the rim. Work both wings.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players who need a middle finishing option. Triggers: Assign if the player only attacks the baseline or outside lane. Avoid/modify: Walk through the lane change before adding the dribble. Focus: Best for lane change, gather control, middle finish timing, and body balance.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the player to start from the wing and finish through the middle lane under control. It helps with finishing when the outside lane is closed.
drills.safety: Do not cut sharply at full speed. Control the lane change.

drills.name: Middle-to-Wing Finish
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: The player starts near the top or slot. The player drives middle, then takes a controlled angle step toward the wing-side rim window and finishes with the outside hand. Work both directions.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players who drive directly into help. Triggers: Assign if the player drives middle and gets swallowed by help. Avoid/modify: Use cones to show the angle if the player cannot visualize it. Focus: Best for lane exit, outside-hand finish, body control, and help awareness.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the player to start middle and finish slightly outside the rim line. It helps the player avoid help defenders waiting in the paint.
drills.safety: No hard sideways jump. Step to angle, then finish.

drills.name: Narrow Lane Finish
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: Place two cone lines leading to the rim. The player drives between the cones, keeps the ball tight, gathers, and finishes. The cones should be wide enough for safety. Work both hands.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players who lose control in tight spaces. Triggers: Assign if the player drifts, bumps cones, or exposes the ball in traffic. Avoid/modify: Widen the lane if the athlete cannot move safely. Focus: Best for tight-space control, ball security, straight-line balance, and finish accuracy.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the player to finish inside a narrow lane without losing balance or swinging the ball. It helps with tight paint control.
drills.safety: Do not make the cone lane too tight. Safety space matters.

drills.name: Wide Lane Finish
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: The player starts wide outside the lane. The player attacks the rim on a controlled angle and finishes before drifting past the backboard. Use a cone to mark the finish window. Work both sides.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players who drive too wide and lose the rim. Triggers: Assign if the player floats away from the rim or loses the glass angle. Avoid/modify: Move the start closer to the lane if the player cannot control the angle. Focus: Best for wide-angle control, rim path, gather timing, and backboard touch.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the player to finish from a wider angle without drifting away from the rim. It helps players who avoid contact by floating too wide.
drills.safety: No drifting into walls, supports, or other players.

drills.name: Inside-Hand High Reach Finish
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: The player starts near the wing. The player drives at a controlled angle and finishes with the inside hand high off the glass. The coach should check that the release is high and soft, not forced. Work both sides.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players who need more hand options. Triggers: Assign if the player always uses the outside hand even when the inside hand is cleaner. Avoid/modify: Use closer reps if the player lacks inside-hand touch. Focus: Best for hand selection, release height, angle finishing, and touch.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the player to use the inside hand with a higher release when the angle calls for it. It helps with hand choice near help defenders.
drills.safety: No defender at first. Add pressure only after clean touch.

drills.name: Outside-Hand Low Reach Finish
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: The player starts on the wing. The ball stays protected near the outside hip during the approach. The player extends late with the outside hand and finishes softly. The finish should be controlled, not thrown.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players learning protected extension finishes. Triggers: Assign if the player brings the ball high too early and gets stripped. Avoid/modify: Use walk-through reps if the player loses the ball low. Focus: Best for outside-hand control, ball protection, extension timing, and touch.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the player to extend with the outside hand from a lower protected path. It helps players finish around help without exposing the ball high too early.
drills.safety: Keep the ball controlled. No off-balance reach across the body.

drills.name: Weak-Hand High Window Finish
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: The player starts close to the lane on the weak-hand side. The player takes a controlled approach and finishes with the weak hand high off the glass. Start close, then move out only if the player makes clean reps.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players with basic weak-hand layup ability who need better touch. Triggers: Assign if the player can make basic weak-hand layups but misses under pressure or angle. Avoid/modify: Return to beginner weak-hand layups if the player cannot make close reps. Focus: Best for weak-hand touch, release height, glass control, and confidence.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the player to finish with the weak hand on a higher glass target. It helps improve weak-hand touch and confidence.
drills.safety: Start close. Do not force range or speed.

drills.name: Weak-Hand Outside Step Finish
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: The player starts at the lane line. The player takes one controlled outside step, gathers, and finishes with the weak hand. Work from both sides if appropriate, but focus on the weaker side first.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players who need weak-hand finishing balance. Triggers: Assign if the player avoids weak-hand finishes or falls away on weak-hand attempts. Avoid/modify: Use no-dribble footwork first if the player cannot control the step. Focus: Best for weak-hand balance, outside step control, gather timing, and hand confidence.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the player to step outside and finish with the weak hand while staying balanced. It helps weak-hand finishing from a better angle.
drills.safety: No long outside step. Keep the base under control.

drills.name: Strong-to-Weak Hand Transfer Finish
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: The player starts with the ball on the strong side. On the approach, the player gathers with two hands, transfers to the weak hand, and finishes softly. Start close and slow. Work both directions.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players learning hand transfer near the rim. Triggers: Assign if the player gets stuck using the wrong hand at the rim. Avoid/modify: Use stationary hand-transfer reps first. Focus: Best for hand transfer, weak-hand finish, gather control, and touch.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the player to transfer the ball from the strong hand to the weak hand before finishing. It helps when the finishing angle changes late.
drills.safety: No mid-air hand switching at first. Transfer during the gather.

drills.name: Weak-to-Strong Hand Transfer Finish
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: The player starts on the weak-hand side with a controlled dribble. The player gathers with two hands, transfers to the strong hand, and finishes softly. Start slow and close. Work both sides only if safe.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players who need better hand-transfer control. Triggers: Assign if the player loses the ball while changing hands near the rim. Avoid/modify: Use stationary gather transfer before adding steps. Focus: Best for hand transfer, gather security, strong-hand finish, and rim read.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the player to start with the weak hand, gather safely, and transfer to the strong hand for the finish. It helps when the player begins on the weak side but has a stronger finishing window.
drills.safety: Keep the transfer low-risk and on the ground. No airborne switching.

drills.name: Chest-to-Outside Finish
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: The player starts near the block with the ball at the chest. The player takes one step, moves the ball to the outside shoulder, and finishes softly. Work both hands and sides. The ball path should stay tight.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players who swing the ball across the body. Triggers: Assign if the player exposes the ball while moving from chest to release. Avoid/modify: Use stationary reps first if the ball path is loose. Focus: Best for ball path, outside release, ball security, and touch.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the player to start the ball at the chest, move it outside the body, and finish without swinging wide. It helps with clean protected releases.
drills.safety: No wide swing. Keep elbows safe.

drills.name: Hip-to-High Finish
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: The player starts near the lane line with the ball at the outside hip. The player steps to the rim, lifts the ball from hip to high release, and finishes softly. Work both sides and both hands if safe.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players who need protected low-to-high finishing. Triggers: Assign if the player brings the ball through the middle of traffic. Avoid/modify: Use close-range reps if the player lacks strength. Focus: Best for low-to-high control, ball protection, release timing, and touch.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the player to protect the ball near the hip and lift it high into the finish. It helps with finishing through crowded lanes without contact.
drills.safety: No contact. Keep the ball path tight.

drills.name: Shoulder-to-Glass Finish
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: The player starts close to the rim on the right side. The player steps, points the finishing shoulder toward the glass target, and finishes softly. Repeat on the left side. Add a dribble only after the shoulder line is clean.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players who finish across the body. Triggers: Assign if the player twists away from the target during the finish. Avoid/modify: Use stationary reps first. Focus: Best for shoulder alignment, release control, backboard touch, and hand accuracy.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the player to align the shoulder, release hand, and glass target. It helps players who finish across their body.
drills.safety: No twisting through the knees or back.

drills.name: Inside-Foot Brake Finish
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: The player drives from the wing. The player plants the inside foot softly to slow down, gathers, and finishes under control. The plant should be quiet and balanced. Work both sides.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players who need better deceleration near the rim. Triggers: Assign if the player cannot slow down before the final step. Avoid/modify: Use no-dribble footwork first if the plant is loud or unstable. Focus: Best for deceleration, inside-foot control, balance, and finish timing.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the player to use the inside foot as a brake before finishing. It helps players slow down without losing the rim angle.
drills.safety: No hard plant. Stop if knee or ankle pain appears.

drills.name: Outside-Foot Brake Finish
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: The player starts wide on the wing. The player attacks at a controlled pace, plants the outside foot to slow the body, gathers, and finishes softly. Work both sides.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players who attack too fast from wide angles. Triggers: Assign if the player drifts wide or loses balance on angled finishes. Avoid/modify: Use shorter approaches if the athlete cannot plant quietly. Focus: Best for outside-foot control, wide-angle deceleration, body balance, and touch.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the player to use the outside foot to slow down and keep a finishing angle. It helps when the player is attacking from a wide lane.
drills.safety: No hard outside plant. Keep the knee aligned.

drills.name: Stride Length Change Finish
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: The player starts from the slot. The first step is longer and controlled. The second step is shorter and balanced before the finish. The coach cues "long, short, finish." Work both sides.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players with one-speed footwork. Triggers: Assign if the player takes the same stride length into every finish. Avoid/modify: Walk through the rhythm without a ball first. Focus: Best for stride rhythm, timing, body control, and rim touch.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the player to change from a long step to a short step before finishing. It helps with timing and control near the rim.
drills.safety: No overstriding. Keep the second step quiet.

drills.name: Short-Long Finish
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: The player starts near the lane line. The first step is short and controlled. The second step is longer toward the rim, then the player finishes softly. Work both sides and hands.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players who need better reach timing. Triggers: Assign if the player cannot extend to the rim without losing control. Avoid/modify: Shorten the second step if landing becomes unstable. Focus: Best for step rhythm, reach timing, balance, and release control.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the player to use a short step into a longer finishing step. It helps players create controlled reach without jumping wildly.
drills.safety: No long lunging step. Land balanced.

drills.name: Hop Step Soft Finish
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: The player starts close to the lane. The player takes one dribble, makes a small hop step into balance, and finishes softly off two feet. The hop should be short and quiet. Work both sides.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players ready for controlled two-foot gathers. Triggers: Assign if the player needs a two-foot gather option but jumps too far. Avoid/modify: Avoid if the player lands loudly or cannot control knees and hips. Focus: Best for hop gather, two-foot balance, finish touch, and body control.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches a small hop step into a soft finish without turning it into a power move. It helps the player gather under control when the lane changes.
drills.safety: Small hop only. Stop if landing is loud or unstable.

drills.name: Skip Step Gather Finish
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: The player starts near the wing. The player takes a controlled dribble, uses a small skip step into the gather, and finishes off the correct hand. The skip should be low and balanced. Work both sides.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players who need rhythm before finishing. Triggers: Assign if the player rushes the gather or finishes out of rhythm. Avoid/modify: Use walk-through rhythm steps before adding the dribble. Focus: Best for gather rhythm, body control, timing, and touch.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the player to use a light skip step to organize the gather before finishing. It helps players who need rhythm without extra speed.
drills.safety: Keep the skip low. No high hop or drifting.

drills.name: Dribble Stop Re-Attack Finish
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: The player starts on the wing, takes one dribble, stops under control, pauses for one second, then re-attacks with one dribble and finishes. Use cones to mark the stop and re-attack points.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players who need reset control before finishing. Triggers: Assign if the player gets stopped and then rushes the next move. Avoid/modify: Remove the re-attack if the player cannot stop safely. Focus: Best for stop control, re-attack timing, balance, and finish control.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the player to stop the dribble, reset balance, and re-attack the rim with control. It helps players who lose rhythm after being slowed down.
drills.safety: No explosive re-attack until the stop is safe.

drills.name: Bump Pad Gather Finish
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: A coach holds a soft pad near the lane. The player drives slowly, receives a light side pad touch before the gather, secures the ball, and finishes. The bump must be light and predictable. Work both sides.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players ready for controlled contact preparation. Triggers: Assign if the player loses the ball from light contact. Avoid/modify: Avoid if the player fears contact or loses landing control. Focus: Best for contact balance, gather security, finish strength, and body control.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the player to keep the gather secure after a light pad bump. It helps with contact preparation without making the drill a collision.
drills.safety: Light pad only. No body checking or surprise contact.

drills.name: Pad Brush Outside-Hand Finish
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: A coach holds a soft pad near the side of the lane. The player drives at controlled speed, brushes the pad lightly with the body, keeps the ball outside, and finishes. Work both sides.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players learning to finish away from contact. Triggers: Assign if the player brings the ball into contact instead of away from it. Avoid/modify: Use a cone instead of a pad if contact readiness is low. Focus: Best for outside-hand protection, contact balance, release control, and finishing confidence.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the player to brush past light contact while finishing with the outside hand. It helps the player keep the ball away from pressure.
drills.safety: Brush contact only. No hard bump.

drills.name: Pad Behind Finish
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: The player starts on the wing. A coach trails with a soft pad held away from the player. The player drives and finishes while the coach applies no hit, only visual trailing pressure. Add a very light pad brush only if safe.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players who panic with pressure behind them. Triggers: Assign if the player looks back or rushes when trailed. Avoid/modify: Use no pad contact if the player loses focus or balance. Focus: Best for chase pressure, finish focus, body control, and confidence.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the player to finish while feeling light pressure from behind without slowing down into panic. It helps with chase-down awareness.
drills.safety: No chasing into the player. Coach stays off the athlete's legs and back.

drills.name: Pad at Rim Finish
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: A coach stands near the rim with a soft pad. The player drives slowly, gathers, and finishes while the pad creates a safe visual contact area. The pad should not knock the player off balance. Work both sides.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players ready for controlled rim contact prep. Triggers: Assign if the player avoids the rim or loses balance near contact. Avoid/modify: Use cone pressure first if contact is not safe. Focus: Best for contact readiness, gather control, rim focus, and finish balance.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the player to finish with a soft pad near the rim while keeping the ball secure. It helps prepare for contact at the basket.
drills.safety: Pad pressure must stay light. No collisions.

drills.name: No-Contact Defender Trail Finish
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: A defender starts one step behind the driver. The driver attacks at controlled speed and finishes. The defender trails with hands up but cannot block, bump, or reach. Switch roles after a few reps.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players ready for visual pressure without contact. Triggers: Assign if the player rushes when someone trails the play. Avoid/modify: Use a cone or coach shadow first if the player panics. Focus: Best for pressure awareness, rim focus, body control, and finish timing.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the player to finish with a defender trailing nearby without contact. It helps the player stay focused on the rim.
drills.safety: Defender cannot reach, bump, or jump into the finisher.

drills.name: No-Contact Help Step Finish
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: A coach stands near the paint as help. The player drives from the wing. As the player enters the lane, the coach takes one step toward help but does not contact. The player chooses a safe angle and finishes.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players learning to read help before finishing. Triggers: Assign if the player drives straight into help without adjusting. Avoid/modify: Use a cone help defender first if the live coach cue is too much. Focus: Best for help read, angle choice, body control, and finish timing.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the player to finish while seeing help step toward the lane. It helps the player pick the finish angle without crashing into help.
drills.safety: Coach steps only. No collision or shot blocking.

drills.name: Defender Hands Up Finish
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: A coach or partner stands near the rim with hands up. The player drives from a short distance and finishes around the hands. The defender does not jump, reach, or move into the player. Work both sides.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players who need finishing reps against a safe contest. Triggers: Assign if the player struggles when a defender shows hands. Avoid/modify: Use a tall cone or pad if a live contest makes the player rush. Focus: Best for release height, contest awareness, angle finishing, and touch.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the player to finish around a defender with hands up but no contact. It helps the player learn release height and angle.
drills.safety: Defender stays still and vertical. No blocking or body contact.

drills.name: Vertical Wall Finish
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: A coach stands near the rim with both arms straight up like a vertical wall. The player approaches under control, stops or steps around slightly, and finishes without initiating contact. Work from both sides.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players learning to finish around verticality. Triggers: Assign if the player jumps into the defender instead of finding a safe release. Avoid/modify: Use a pad or cone instead of a person if the player cannot avoid contact. Focus: Best for verticality read, body control, release choice, and foul avoidance.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the player to finish against a vertical defender shape without jumping into the defender. It helps with body control and safe release choices.
drills.safety: No jumping into the defender. Defender stays still.

drills.name: Side Pad Floater-Lay Finish
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: A coach stands beside the lane with a soft pad. The player drives slowly, feels a light side brush, and releases a soft one-hand finish near the rim. The finish should be controlled and close to the basket.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players who lose touch after contact. Triggers: Assign if the player throws the ball hard after light contact. Avoid/modify: Remove pad if touch disappears or balance is poor. Focus: Best for contact touch, release control, body balance, and soft hands.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the player to keep touch after light side pressure. It is not a true floater drill; it is a soft finishing-touch drill with controlled side contact.
drills.safety: Light side brush only. No heavy bump.

drills.name: Hand Shield Underhand Finish
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: The player starts near the lane. The non-finishing arm stays bent and safe near the body as a shield. The player finishes underhand with the outside hand. The shield arm cannot extend or push. Work both sides.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players learning safe off-arm protection. Triggers: Assign if the player pushes off or exposes the ball. Avoid/modify: Use no shield cue if the athlete extends the off arm illegally. Focus: Best for off-arm discipline, underhand touch, protection, and body control.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the player to use the non-finishing arm as a safe shield while finishing underhand with the other hand. It helps protect the release without pushing off.
drills.safety: Shield arm stays bent. No pushing off.

drills.name: Elbow Tuck Finish
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: The player drives from a short distance. During the gather, the player keeps elbows tight, ball close, and finishes with a compact release. The coach cues "tight elbows, clean finish." Work both sides.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players with loose gathers. Triggers: Assign if the player flares elbows or swings the ball wide near the rim. Avoid/modify: Use stationary gather reps if the player cannot keep elbows tight while moving. Focus: Best for compact gather, ball security, release control, and strip prevention.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the player to keep elbows tight during the gather and release. It helps players who flare the ball out and get stripped.
drills.safety: No elbow swinging. Keep the gather tight and safe.

drills.name: Ball-Side Hip Seal Finish
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: The player drives from the wing. A cone sits near the lane as imaginary pressure. The player keeps the ball-side hip between cone and ball, then finishes softly. Work both sides.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players learning body positioning near the rim. Triggers: Assign if the player exposes the ball or turns too far away from the rim. Avoid/modify: Remove cone if the player over-rotates. Focus: Best for hip positioning, ball protection, angle control, and finish balance.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the player to use the ball-side hip to protect the finish angle. It helps the player finish without turning the whole body away from the rim.
drills.safety: No hip check into a defender. The cone is only a guide.

drills.name: Back-to-Rim Turn Finish
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: The player starts with back to the rim at the mid-paint. The coach hands or tosses the ball. The player turns over one shoulder, finds the rim, and finishes softly. Work both shoulders.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players learning rim orientation after turning. Triggers: Assign if the player catches near the paint and cannot find the rim. Avoid/modify: Use no-ball turns first if orientation is poor. Focus: Best for rim awareness, turn control, balance, and short finish touch.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the player to turn from a back-to-rim position and finish under control. It helps players who catch near the paint and lose rim awareness.
drills.safety: Turn slowly. No spinning through contact.

drills.name: Back-to-Rim Shoulder Check Finish
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: The player starts with back to the rim and ball at the chest. The player shoulder-checks one side, turns the other way or same way based on coach cue, and finishes softly. Keep it slow.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players learning awareness before finishing. Triggers: Assign if the player turns blindly into pressure. Avoid/modify: Use one turn direction until the player understands the cue. Focus: Best for shoulder check, rim awareness, turn decision, and finish balance.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the player to check over the shoulder before turning to finish. It helps with awareness and controlled rim reads.
drills.safety: No live defender at first. Keep the turn controlled.

drills.name: Short Roll One-Step Finish
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: The player starts near the free throw line or short-roll area. A coach passes the ball. The player catches, takes one controlled step to the rim, and finishes. Work both sides and hands.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players learning short-roll finishing. Triggers: Assign if the player catches in the lane and takes too many steps or rushes. Avoid/modify: Use stationary catch and hold before adding the step. Focus: Best for catch-to-finish timing, one-step control, hand choice, and rim touch.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the player to catch around the short-roll area and finish with one clean step. It helps with quick decisions after catching near the lane.
drills.safety: No rushing through the catch. Secure first.

drills.name: Short Roll Catch Pivot Finish
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: The player catches near the middle of the lane. The coach calls "left" or "right." The player pivots that direction and finishes softly. Work both pivot directions.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players who need short-roll pivot control. Triggers: Assign if the player catches in the lane and travels or turns blindly. Avoid/modify: Use no-shot pivot reps first. Focus: Best for pivot control, rim read, catch security, and finish touch.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the player to catch in the short-roll area, pivot under control, and finish. It helps players who catch facing away from the best rim angle.
drills.safety: Slow pivot. No swinging elbows.

drills.name: Catch Low Finish High
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: The coach gives a low but safe pass near the lane. The player catches with two hands, brings the ball up tight, and finishes high off the glass. Work both sides.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players learning to finish after imperfect catches. Triggers: Assign if the player loses low catches or finishes low after catching. Avoid/modify: Raise the pass if the athlete bends unsafely. Focus: Best for low-catch control, ball security, high finish, and release timing.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the player to catch a low pass, bring the ball up safely, and finish high. It helps with bad-pass recovery near the rim.
drills.safety: Pass should be low but safe. No passes near the feet at speed.

drills.name: Catch High Bring Down Finish
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: The coach throws a safe high pass near the lane. The player catches, brings the ball down only enough to secure, takes controlled steps, and finishes. Work both sides.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players learning to manage high catches near the rim. Triggers: Assign if the player travels, rushes, or drops high catches near the rim. Avoid/modify: Use chest passes if high catches are not safe. Focus: Best for high catch control, footwork timing, ball security, and finish balance.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the player to catch a high pass, bring it down under control, and finish without traveling. It helps with awkward catch-to-finish timing.
drills.safety: No high passes above safe reach. Avoid if shoulder discomfort appears.

drills.name: Catch Outside Shoulder Finish
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: The player starts near the lane. The coach passes to the outside shoulder. The player catches, keeps the ball outside, steps to the rim, and finishes. Work both sides.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players who need better catch angle control. Triggers: Assign if the player catches outside but brings the ball back into traffic. Avoid/modify: Use a stationary outside-shoulder catch first. Focus: Best for outside-shoulder catch, ball protection, footwork adjustment, and finish timing.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the player to catch a pass on the outside shoulder and turn it into a finish. It helps with passes that lead the player away from traffic.
drills.safety: Keep the pass controlled. Do not chase wide passes into unsafe space.

drills.name: Catch Inside Shoulder Finish
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: The coach passes to the inside shoulder near the lane. The player catches with two hands, turns the body slightly to protect, and finishes with the cleanest hand. Work both sides.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players learning to finish from inside-shoulder catches. Triggers: Assign if the player catches inside and exposes the ball to help. Avoid/modify: Use no defender or cone until catch control is strong. Focus: Best for catch protection, hand choice, body turn, and ball security.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the player to catch on the inside shoulder and still protect the ball before finishing. It helps with catches near traffic.
drills.safety: No twisting hard through the knees. Turn under control.

drills.name: Catch Behind Step Finish
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: The coach gives a controlled pass slightly behind the player near the lane. The player catches, gathers balance, takes one controlled step, and finishes. The pass should not be unsafe or too far behind.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players learning to adjust to late passes. Triggers: Assign if the player loses balance when the pass is not perfect. Avoid/modify: Use easier pass placement if the athlete twists or reaches dangerously. Focus: Best for catch adjustment, balance recovery, footwork timing, and finish touch.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the player to adjust when the pass is slightly behind them and still finish under control. It helps with balance after imperfect timing.
drills.safety: No unsafe reaching behind the body. Pass must stay catchable.

drills.name: Catch Ahead Stride Finish
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: The player starts near the lane line and moves slowly toward the rim. The coach leads the player with a pass. The player catches in stride, takes controlled steps, and finishes. Work both sides.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players learning to finish from lead passes. Triggers: Assign if the player bobbles lead passes or slows down too much after catching. Avoid/modify: Use shorter lead passes if the athlete overreaches. Focus: Best for lead catch, stride timing, catch security, and finish balance.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the player to catch a pass slightly ahead and finish in stride. It helps with timing on cuts and transition-style catches.
drills.safety: Pass must lead safely. No chasing the ball into traffic.

drills.name: Short Hop Catch Finish
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: The coach gives a controlled short-hop pass near the lane. The player catches with two hands, secures, and finishes softly. Start close and slow. The pass should be safe and predictable.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players learning to handle low bounce catches. Triggers: Assign if the player fumbles low bounce passes near the rim. Avoid/modify: Use regular chest passes if the player cannot catch safely. Focus: Best for low catch timing, hand strength, ball security, and finish control.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the player to handle a pass that arrives on a short hop or low bounce and still finish. It helps with imperfect passes near the rim.
drills.safety: Keep the pass predictable. No fast passes at the feet.

drills.name: Catch, Check Rim, Finish
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: The player catches a pass near the paint. Before moving, the player must briefly check the rim with the eyes, then take one controlled step and finish. The pause should be short but clear.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players who rush after catches near the rim. Triggers: Assign if the player catches and throws the ball up without seeing the rim. Avoid/modify: Use catch-and-hold before adding the finish. Focus: Best for rim vision, catch patience, finish timing, and body control.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the player to catch, see the rim, then finish instead of rushing blindly. It helps with patience near the basket.
drills.safety: No defender at first. Control the catch before moving.

drills.name: Catch, Shot Fake, One-Step Finish
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: The player catches near the lane, gives a short shot fake with the feet down, then takes one step to finish. The fake should be small. Work both sides and both hands.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players learning controlled shot-fake finishing. Triggers: Assign if the player travels or jumps on their own fake. Avoid/modify: Use no finish until the fake is legal and controlled. Focus: Best for fake discipline, one-step control, footwork timing, and finish balance.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the player to use a small shot fake and finish with one controlled step. It helps players avoid wild fakes and traveling.
drills.safety: No jumping on the fake. Keep the feet under control.

drills.name: Catch, Ball Fake, Outside Finish
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: The player catches near the block. The player gives a small ball fake toward the middle, steps outside, and finishes softly. The fake should be tight and controlled. Work both sides.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players learning ball-fake finishing. Triggers: Assign if the player gets stuck after catching near the block. Avoid/modify: Use no defender and no contact until the fake is clean. Focus: Best for ball fake control, outside step, angle creation, and touch.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the player to ball fake inside, then finish outside. It helps players create a better angle without using contact.
drills.safety: No wide ball swing. Keep the fake close to the body.

drills.name: Catch, Reverse Pivot Finish
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: The player catches near the mid-post or block. The player reverse pivots away from the imaginary pressure and finishes. The pivot must be slow and balanced at first. Work both directions.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players who need a controlled pivot finish. Triggers: Assign if the player catches and travels or turns into pressure. Avoid/modify: Use pivot-only reps first. Focus: Best for pivot control, pressure avoidance, balance, and short finish touch.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the player to use a reverse pivot after catching and finish under control. It helps when the player catches with pressure on one side.
drills.safety: No spinning fast. Pivot first, finish second.

drills.name: Catch, Front Pivot Finish
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: The player catches with back or side to the rim. The player front pivots, gets shoulders toward the basket, and finishes softly. Work both pivot feet and sides.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players learning to face the rim before finishing. Triggers: Assign if the player catches side-on and rushes without facing the rim. Avoid/modify: Use catch-pivot-hold before adding the finish. Focus: Best for front pivot, rim square-up, balance, and finish timing.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the player to catch, front pivot toward the rim, and finish with control. It helps players square the body before finishing.
drills.safety: Keep the pivot foot stable. No twisting through the knee.

drills.name: Catch, Split Step Finish
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: The player receives a pass near the lane and lands with one foot slightly ahead. From that split stance, the player takes one controlled step and finishes. Work both lead feet.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players who need better catch stance near the rim. Triggers: Assign if the player catches with feet too narrow or off balance. Avoid/modify: Use catch-and-freeze before adding the finish. Focus: Best for catch stance, split balance, first-step control, and finish touch.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the player to catch, land in a split stance, and finish with one clean move. It helps players who catch with narrow feet.
drills.safety: No wide split. Keep knees and hips comfortable.

drills.name: Catch, Pause, Powerless Finish
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: The player catches near the block, pauses for one second, then finishes softly without jumping hard. The coach cues "quiet finish." Work both sides.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players who overpower short finishes. Triggers: Assign if the player throws short finishes too hard or rushes the release. Avoid/modify: Move closer and remove the jump if touch is poor. Focus: Best for patience, soft touch, short finish control, and body calm.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the player to pause after the catch and finish with touch instead of force. It helps players who rush and throw the ball too hard.
drills.safety: No hard jump. Keep the finish soft.

drills.name: Catch, Step Across Finish
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: The player catches near the lane. The player steps across with the outside foot, keeps the ball tight, and finishes. The step must be controlled and not a travel. Work both sides.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players learning angle change after catching. Triggers: Assign if the player catches and cannot change angle without traveling. Avoid/modify: Practice step-across without a shot first. Focus: Best for step-across control, ball security, angle creation, and finish balance.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the player to step across the body under control and finish from a new angle. It helps players who need a simple angle change after catching.
drills.safety: No lunging step. Keep the ball tight.

drills.name: Catch, Drop Shoulder Avoid Finish
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: The player catches near the wing lane line. The player lowers the body slightly, keeps the shoulder controlled, and finishes through the open angle. There is no defender contact. Work both sides.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players learning body strength without offensive fouls. Triggers: Assign if the player is too upright or uses the shoulder illegally. Avoid/modify: Avoid if the athlete lowers the shoulder into people. Focus: Best for body control, shoulder discipline, finish strength, and balance.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the player to lower the shoulder slightly for balance without charging or hitting. It helps the player stay strong through the finish lane.
drills.safety: No contact. This is body position, not a hit.

drills.name: Catch, Step Back In Finish
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: The coach passes the ball slightly to one side. The player catches, takes a small step back into balance, then steps toward the rim and finishes. Keep the pass safe and controlled.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players learning to recover balance after a catch. Triggers: Assign if the player catches awkwardly and rushes into a bad finish. Avoid/modify: Use catch-balance-freeze before adding the finish. Focus: Best for balance recovery, catch adjustment, footwork control, and finish touch.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the player to catch slightly off balance, step back into control, and finish. It helps after awkward catches near the paint.
drills.safety: No reaching for bad passes. The pass must stay safe.

drills.name: Catch, One-Bounce Reset Finish
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: The player catches near the lane, takes one controlled pound or low bounce, gathers, and finishes. The bounce should reset rhythm, not become a dribble move. Work both sides.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players who need a rhythm reset after catching. Triggers: Assign if the player catches out of rhythm and rushes the finish. Avoid/modify: Avoid if the player double-dribbles or loses the ball. Focus: Best for rhythm reset, gather timing, ball control, and finish touch.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the player to use one controlled bounce after the catch to reset timing and finish. It helps when the catch rhythm is off.
drills.safety: One controlled bounce only. No speed or extra dribbles.

drills.name: Catch, No-Dribble Angle Finish
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: The player catches near the block or lane line. Without dribbling, the player uses one controlled step to create an angle and finishes. Work both sides and both pivot feet.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players learning quick no-dribble finishes. Triggers: Assign if the player always dribbles after catching near the rim. Avoid/modify: Use catch-pivot-hold if the player travels. Focus: Best for no-dribble footwork, angle creation, catch security, and finish timing.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the player to create a finishing angle without dribbling. It helps players score quickly after catching near the rim.
drills.safety: No traveling. Keep the step controlled.

drills.name: Catch, Inside Pivot Outside Finish
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: The player catches near the block. The player pivots inside to face the rim, then steps outside and finishes. The ball stays tight during the pivot. Work both sides.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players learning pivot-to-angle finishing. Triggers: Assign if the player pivots but cannot create a safe finish angle. Avoid/modify: Use pivot-only reps if the player travels. Focus: Best for pivot control, angle change, ball protection, and short finish touch.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the player to pivot inside, then finish outside away from pressure. It helps with controlled footwork near the block.
drills.safety: No fast spin. Pivot under control.

drills.name: Catch, Outside Pivot Inside Finish
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: The player catches near the block. The player outside pivots to create space, then steps inside toward the rim and finishes softly. Work both sides.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players learning pivot direction control. Triggers: Assign if the player cannot pivot and finish without losing balance. Avoid/modify: Use no-shot pivot reps first. Focus: Best for outside pivot, direction change, balance, and finish touch.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the player to pivot outside, then finish back inside. It helps players use footwork to change direction without traveling.
drills.safety: Keep the pivot foot stable. No twisting through pain.

drills.name: Catch, Reverse Step Finish
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: The player catches near the lane line. A cone blocks the first path. The player takes a controlled reverse step away from the cone, gathers, and finishes softly. Work both sides.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players learning a safe counter step. Triggers: Assign if the player forces the first lane even when it is closed. Avoid/modify: Walk the footwork first. Focus: Best for counter step, angle reset, ball security, and finish balance.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the player to step away from one side and finish back toward the rim. It helps with finishing after the first angle is cut off.
drills.safety: No sharp plant at speed. Step under control.

drills.name: One-Count Hang Finish
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: The player starts close to the rim. The player takes one controlled jump, holds the ball for a tiny one-count, and releases softly. This is not a high jump or acrobatic move. Work both sides.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players with safe jumping control who rush release timing. Triggers: Assign if the player releases too early or panics in the air. Avoid/modify: Avoid if the player cannot land safely. Focus: Best for air control, release timing, body balance, and soft touch.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the player to stay calm in the air for a short controlled count before releasing. It helps players who rush the ball up too early.
drills.safety: Small jump only. Stop if the landing is unstable.

drills.name: Quick Up Finish
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: The player starts close to the rim. The coach passes or hands the ball. The player catches and finishes immediately with a compact release. The feet should stay controlled and legal. Work both sides.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players who are slow getting the ball up. Triggers: Assign if the player catches near the rim but takes too long to release. Avoid/modify: Use slower catch-secure-finish if the player loses control. Focus: Best for quick release, catch-to-finish speed, compact mechanics, and ball security.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the player to get the ball up quickly after catching or gathering. It helps players who bring the ball down and lose time.
drills.safety: Quick does not mean rushed. Secure the ball first.

drills.name: Slow Up Finish
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: The player drives slowly from the lane line. At the gather, the player pauses the body for a half-count, then finishes softly. The ball should not stop long enough to travel. Work both sides.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players who need tempo control near the rim. Triggers: Assign if the player rushes every close finish. Avoid/modify: Use stationary soft-touch finishes first. Focus: Best for tempo control, soft touch, balance, and finish patience.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the player to slow the release when the body is moving too fast. It helps players who rush and miss easy finishes.
drills.safety: No travel. Keep the gather legal and controlled.

drills.name: High Arc Rim Finish
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: The player starts close to the rim and finishes with a soft, higher arc. The coach should cue the ball to rise and drop, not push flat. Work both hands and sides.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players who shoot flat finishes at the rim. Triggers: Assign if the player hits the front rim or throws flat finishes. Avoid/modify: Move closer if the player lacks strength. Focus: Best for arc control, soft touch, release height, and rim finish accuracy.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the player to use a higher arc near the rim. It helps when flat finishes hit the front rim or get blocked.
drills.safety: Do not force range. Stay close enough for clean touch.

drills.name: Soft Rim Drop Finish
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: The player starts near the front of the rim. The player takes one small step and releases the ball softly so it drops over the rim. The goal is a gentle finish. Work both hands.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players who overpower close finishes. Triggers: Assign if the player throws close finishes too hard. Avoid/modify: Lower the speed or start closer if the player misses long. Focus: Best for soft touch, release control, close finish accuracy, and hand feel.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the player to drop the ball softly over the front of the rim. It helps with close finishes that need touch instead of power.
drills.safety: No jumping into the rim area. Keep the step small.

drills.name: Back-Rim Kiss Finish
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: The player starts close to the rim, attacks with one controlled step, and releases the ball softly so it reaches the back rim area and drops. The coach should cue touch, not power.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players who need better distance control near the rim. Triggers: Assign if the player leaves finishes short or throws them long. Avoid/modify: Use a closer start if touch is inconsistent. Focus: Best for distance control, rim touch, release feel, and finish accuracy.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the player to use a soft touch that reaches the back rim area without throwing the ball hard. It helps players learn distance control near the basket.
drills.safety: No contact or speed. The goal is touch.

drills.name: Side Spin Glass Finish
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: The player starts at a 45-degree angle. The player finishes softly off the glass with slight side spin from the wrist and fingers. Keep the finish close and controlled. Work both sides.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players learning advanced touch off the glass. Triggers: Assign if the player misses angled finishes because the ball comes off the glass too hard. Avoid/modify: Use regular glass touch first if spin control is poor. Focus: Best for side-spin touch, glass angle, wrist control, and finish accuracy.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the player to use gentle side spin off the glass. It helps with angled finishes where a straight release does not sit on the backboard well.
drills.safety: Keep the approach slow. Do not force spin from distance.

drills.name: No-Glass Rim Finish
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: The player starts close and slightly in front of the rim. The player takes one controlled step and finishes directly over the rim without using the glass. The release should be soft and close.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players who rely on the glass from every angle. Triggers: Assign if the player uses the glass even when a direct finish is cleaner. Avoid/modify: Start very close if direct touch is weak. Focus: Best for direct touch, rim feel, release control, and finish selection.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the player to finish softly without using the backboard when the angle calls for it. It helps with touch right in front of the rim.
drills.safety: No jumping into the rim or under the basket support.

drills.name: Glass-or-Rim Coach Call
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: The player starts close to the rim. As the player approaches, the coach calls "glass" or "rim." The player finishes with the called target. Keep speed controlled and distance short.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players learning finishing target decisions. Triggers: Assign if the player uses the same target on every finish. Avoid/modify: Use one target at a time if the player gets confused. Focus: Best for finish decision, target control, touch, and reaction.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the player to choose between using the glass and finishing directly at the rim based on a coach cue. It builds simple finishing decision-making.
drills.safety: No late shout that causes panic. Cue early enough for safe control.

drills.name: Hand Call Finish
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: The player starts close to the basket. The coach calls "right" or "left" before the gather. The player finishes with that hand. Keep speed slow at first and work from both sides.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players learning hand choice under a simple cue. Triggers: Assign if the player always uses the strong hand no matter the angle. Avoid/modify: Use only weak-hand side reps if two-hand calls overwhelm the player. Focus: Best for hand selection, weak-hand confidence, reaction, and release control.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the player to finish with the hand the coach calls. It builds both-hand confidence and forces the player to think near the rim.
drills.safety: Call early. Do not force awkward late hand changes.

drills.name: Foot Call Finish
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: The player starts close to the lane. The coach calls "inside foot" or "outside foot" before the gather. The player uses that foot pattern and finishes softly. Start slow.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players learning conscious footwork control. Triggers: Assign if the player uses the same footwork every time and cannot adjust. Avoid/modify: Teach each foot pattern separately before using calls. Focus: Best for footwork decision, gather control, body balance, and timing.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the player to finish off the foot pattern the coach calls. It builds footwork awareness and reduces automatic finishing habits.
drills.safety: Call before the gather. No late cue that causes awkward steps.

drills.name: Color Cone Finish Choice
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: Place two colored cones near the lane, one for right-hand finish and one for left-hand finish. Coach calls a color during the approach. The player finishes with the matching hand or angle. Start close and slow.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players learning visual finishing decisions. Triggers: Assign if the player struggles to react while approaching the rim. Avoid/modify: Use one cue at a time if reaction is too hard. Focus: Best for visual reaction, hand choice, angle control, and finish timing.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the player to finish based on a simple visual cue. It builds decision-making while keeping the read safe and clear.
drills.safety: Cue early enough for safe footwork.

drills.name: Defender Cone Side Read
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: Place a cone on either the left or right side of the lane. The player attacks the rim and must finish away from the cone. Move the cone each rep. Keep speed controlled.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players learning to finish away from help. Triggers: Assign if the player drives into the same help spot every time. Avoid/modify: Use a fixed cone side first. Focus: Best for help read, angle choice, body control, and hand selection.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the player to read which side of the lane is blocked and finish away from it. It helps with simple help-defender awareness.
drills.safety: Do not cut sharply. Read early and finish under control.

drills.name: Coach Hand Up Finish Under
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: A coach stands near the rim and raises one hand high. The player approaches under control and finishes away from or under the raised hand. The coach does not jump or reach.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players learning to read a contest hand. Triggers: Assign if the player shoots straight into a raised hand. Avoid/modify: Use a pad or cone hand target first if the player rushes. Focus: Best for contest read, release choice, hand selection, and touch.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the player to finish under or around a high hand without forcing the ball into the contest. It helps with release selection.
drills.safety: Coach stays still. No contact or blocks.

drills.name: Coach Low Hand Finish Over
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: A coach stands near the rim with a low hand or pad near the ball path. The player approaches and finishes over the low hand with a higher release. The coach does not swipe.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players who release too low near help. Triggers: Assign if the player brings the ball into low hands or gets stripped. Avoid/modify: Use a cone or soft pad instead of a hand if the player is nervous. Focus: Best for release height, contest awareness, touch, and ball protection.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the player to raise the release when a low hand is in the way. It helps players stop finishing too low.
drills.safety: No swiping. Coach hand is a visual cue only.

drills.name: Read Pad Left Finish Right
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: A coach holds a soft pad on the left side of the lane. The player drives under control, reads the pad, and finishes to the right side. Switch sides after several reps.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players learning to finish away from contact. Triggers: Assign if the player drives directly into pad pressure. Avoid/modify: Use cone pressure if the player is not contact-ready. Focus: Best for contact read, angle choice, body control, and release timing.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the player to read pad pressure on one side and finish to the other side. It helps with safe contact avoidance.
drills.safety: Pad is a cue, not a hit. No collisions.

drills.name: Read Pad High Finish Low
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: A coach holds a pad high near the rim. The player approaches and finishes with a controlled lower release under the pad line. The player must stay balanced and avoid contact.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players learning release-level decisions. Triggers: Assign if the player always shoots into high contests. Avoid/modify: Use no pad first if the player ducks or twists unsafely. Focus: Best for release decision, body control, touch, and contest awareness.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the player to read a high pad and choose a lower controlled finish. It helps with finishing under raised contests.
drills.safety: No ducking under bodies. Pad stays still.

drills.name: Read Pad Low Finish High
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: A coach holds a pad low near the ball path. The player attacks slowly, raises the ball above the pad line, and finishes softly. The player should not swing the ball wide.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players who finish too low against pressure. Triggers: Assign if the player brings the ball low into help pressure. Avoid/modify: Use a stationary high-release drill first. Focus: Best for release height, late extension, ball path, and touch.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the player to read low pressure and finish high. It helps with late extension and release control.
drills.safety: No pad swipe. Keep the pad still and soft.

drills.name: Finish After Shoulder Peek
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: The player starts on the wing. Before the gather, the player makes a quick shoulder peek, then returns eyes to the rim and finishes. A coach trails behind as visual pressure but does not contact.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players learning trail awareness. Triggers: Assign if the player gets surprised by trailing pressure. Avoid/modify: Use no trailer if the player loses rim focus. Focus: Best for shoulder awareness, trail pressure, rim focus, and finish timing.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the player to peek over the shoulder before finishing to sense trailing pressure. It helps players stay aware without looking away too long.
drills.safety: Peek quickly. Do not twist the head and body out of control.

drills.name: Finish After Rim Peek
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: The player starts near the slot. As the player takes the first dribble, they must peek at the rim, keep eyes up, gather, and finish. The coach can remind "rim early."
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players who look down on drives. Triggers: Assign if the player looks at the ball until the last second. Avoid/modify: Use slower dribble if eyes-up control is poor. Focus: Best for rim vision, eyes-up control, gather timing, and finish accuracy.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the player to find the rim early before releasing. It helps players who look down during the approach.
drills.safety: Slow the dribble if the player loses the ball.

drills.name: Rim-Line Stop and Finish
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: Place a tape line or cone even with the front of the rim. The player attacks and must gather before crossing that line, then finish. Work from the slot and wings.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players who get too deep under the rim. Triggers: Assign if the player constantly ends under or behind the rim. Avoid/modify: Move the line farther out for slower learning. Focus: Best for spatial control, gather location, finish balance, and rim awareness.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the player to stop before crossing the rim line and finish from a controlled spot. It helps avoid drifting too deep.
drills.safety: No sliding stop. Gather under control.

drills.name: Backboard Square Call Finish
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: The coach calls "high," "middle," or "soft" before the finish. The player drives from close range and uses the called backboard target. Work both sides.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players learning glass target control. Triggers: Assign if the player uses the same glass target from every angle. Avoid/modify: Use one target at a time before adding calls. Focus: Best for backboard target, reaction, touch, and finish accuracy.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the player to aim at the correct part of the backboard after a coach call. It helps improve target awareness.
drills.safety: Cue early. Do not make the player change target late in the air.

drills.name: Lane Line Drift Finish
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: The player starts on the lane line. The player drives along that line, gathers, and finishes without crossing far into the middle. Use cones to mark the lane if needed.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players who drift across the paint. Triggers: Assign if the player starts on one side and drifts into bad traffic. Avoid/modify: Slow the approach if the player cannot stay on path. Focus: Best for path control, lane discipline, gather balance, and finish accuracy.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the player to stay near a lane line path without drifting into traffic. It helps with straight but controlled finishing lanes.
drills.safety: No cutting across another player's path.

drills.name: Paint Dot Finish
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: Place a floor dot or cone in the paint. The player must gather at the dot, then finish. Change the dot location after a few makes. Work both sides and angles.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players learning paint finishing spots. Triggers: Assign if the player gathers randomly and loses finishing rhythm. Avoid/modify: Use one spot only until the player controls it. Focus: Best for gather spot, spatial control, finish timing, and touch.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the player to gather and finish from a specific paint spot. It helps players understand spacing and timing near the rim.
drills.safety: Use flat markers. No raised object in the landing area.

drills.name: One-More-Step Finish
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: The player starts slightly outside their normal finish range. The coach cues "one more." The player takes one extra controlled step, gathers, and finishes softly. Work both hands.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players who release too early. Triggers: Assign if the player shoots too far from the rim and leaves finishes short. Avoid/modify: Avoid if the extra step causes traveling or poor balance. Focus: Best for release distance, patience, step control, and touch.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the player to take one more controlled step before releasing instead of shooting too early. It helps players who leave finishes short.
drills.safety: No extra step if it becomes a travel. Keep it legal.

drills.name: One-Step-Early Finish
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: The player starts on the wing or slot. A cone marks the help defender near the rim. The player must release before reaching the cone area. The finish should be soft and controlled.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players who drive too deep before releasing. Triggers: Assign if the player waits too long and runs into help or under the rim. Avoid/modify: Move the cone farther from the rim if the player needs more space. Focus: Best for early release timing, help awareness, touch, and rim spacing.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the player to release one step earlier than usual when the rim window is open. It helps players avoid driving into help too deep.
drills.safety: No rushed throw. Early still has to be controlled.

drills.name: Sprint Stop Shot
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: The player starts at half court or a short sprint distance. On the coach's cue, the player sprints under control to a marked shooting spot, stops with balanced feet, catches or picks up a ball, and shoots. Start at midrange. Only move farther if the shot stays smooth.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players who rush shots after running. Triggers: Assign if the player's shot changes after sprinting into it. Avoid/modify: Use a jog instead of a sprint if the athlete cannot stop safely. Focus: Best for stop control, conditioning, shooting balance, and shot consistency after movement.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the player to run into a shot, slow down, and shoot with balance. It is harder than a basic catch-and-shoot because the player has to control the body before the release.
drills.safety: No full-speed sprint if the athlete cannot stop under control. Good balance comes before speed.

drills.name: Jog Curl Catch Shot
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: Place a cone near the wing. The player jogs around the cone on a curved path, receives a pass, gets the feet under the body, and shoots. The coach should cue "curl, catch, square." Work both sides.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players learning to shoot after curved movement. Triggers: Assign if the player curls into a shot but fades or turns sideways. Avoid/modify: Walk the curl first if the player cannot square up. Focus: Best for curved-path balance, catch timing, footwork, and body alignment.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the player to jog into a curved path, catch the ball, square the body, and shoot. It helps players who catch while drifting sideways.
drills.safety: No sharp turns at full speed. Keep the curl controlled.

drills.name: Jog Flare Catch Shot
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: The player starts near the lane, jogs out and slightly backward to a wing or slot spot, catches a pass, lands balanced, and shoots. The shooter should not fade away unless the drill is later progressed.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players learning to shoot after moving away from the passer. Triggers: Assign if the player catches on a flare and shoots while leaning. Avoid/modify: Shorten the flare distance if the player loses balance. Focus: Best for flare footwork, drift control, catch balance, and release consistency.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the player to move away from the ball, catch, and shoot with balance. It is harder than a simple flare spot shot because the player has to manage body drift.
drills.safety: Do not backpedal fast. Check space behind the shooter.

drills.name: Slot Sprint Catch Shot
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: The player starts near half court or the opposite slot. The player sprints to the slot, receives a pass, sets the feet quickly, and shoots. Start with midrange or safe range before moving out.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players learning transition spot-up shots. Triggers: Assign if the player arrives open but rushes or shoots off balance. Avoid/modify: Use a jog-in version if the player cannot stop safely. Focus: Best for transition conditioning, foot set speed, catch readiness, and shot balance.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the player to sprint into the slot, catch, and shoot without rushing the release. It helps with transition-style shooting.
drills.safety: No deep-range sprint shots if the player heaves or lands poorly.

drills.name: Corner Sprint Stop Shot
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: The player starts near the lane or wing, sprints to the corner, catches a pass, and shoots. The player must stop before drifting out of bounds. Work both corners.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players learning corner movement shooting. Triggers: Assign if the player catches in the corner and steps out or shoots while drifting. Avoid/modify: Use shorter movement if sideline control is poor. Focus: Best for corner footwork, sideline awareness, stop control, and catch-and-shoot balance.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the player to sprint into the corner, stop short of the sideline, and shoot with balance. It helps with spacing and corner shooting footwork.
drills.safety: Check sideline space. No drifting into walls, benches, or other players.

drills.name: Wing Back-Cut Pop Shot
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: The player starts on the wing, takes two steps toward the basket like a back cut, then pops back out to the wing spot. The passer delivers the ball as the player arrives. The player catches, sets, and shoots.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players learning simple off-ball shot creation. Triggers: Assign if the player stands still waiting for shots or cannot reset feet after moving. Avoid/modify: Walk the fake cut before adding speed. Focus: Best for relocation timing, footwork, catch balance, and shot prep.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the player to fake a back cut, pop back out, catch, and shoot. It helps players learn to create space before a shot.
drills.safety: No hard plant if the athlete cannot control the knees and ankles.

drills.name: Slot Shake Catch Shot
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: The player starts at the slot, slides or jogs a few feet into a new window, catches a pass, and shoots. The movement should be short and sharp but controlled. Work both slot directions.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players learning small relocation shots. Triggers: Assign if the player is open but does not move into a cleaner passing window. Avoid/modify: Use a walk-shake first if the athlete drifts. Focus: Best for relocation control, catch readiness, footwork, and shot speed.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the player to shake a few steps into open space and get ready to shoot. It helps players learn small off-ball movement instead of standing still.
drills.safety: Do not make the shake a hard cut until the athlete controls the stop.

drills.name: Wing Lift Behind Line Shot
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: The player starts low on the wing, lifts up toward the slot or higher wing, catches a pass, checks the feet, and shoots. The coach should watch that the player does not drift into the line or lose balance.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players learning spacing and shooting foot placement. Triggers: Assign if the player catches too low, steps on lines, or loses shot balance while lifting. Avoid/modify: Use midrange spacing first if the athlete is not strong enough for deeper shots. Focus: Best for spacing awareness, lift timing, foot placement, and shot balance.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the player to lift from the wing into open space and shoot without stepping on the line. It helps with spacing awareness and foot placement.
drills.safety: Range must fit strength. No heaving from deep space.

drills.name: Corner Drift Hold Shot
