drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: The player starts near the wing and drifts toward the corner. The player catches, holds the base for a half-count, then shoots. The hold should not be long; it is just enough to show balance.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players who drift into corner shots off balance. Triggers: Assign if the player catches while still sliding sideways. Avoid/modify: Shorten drift distance if the player cannot stop. Focus: Best for drift control, corner balance, catch timing, and release consistency.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the player to drift into the corner, stop, hold balance, and shoot. It helps players who move into the corner but cannot stop cleanly.
drills.safety: Do not drift into the sideline or corner wall.

drills.name: Trail Drag Catch Shot
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: The player starts behind the play, jogs or sprints to the top or slot, catches a pass, and shoots. The player should drag into the shot under control, not run through it.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players learning trail shooting rhythm. Triggers: Assign if the player trails into shots with heavy feet or poor balance. Avoid/modify: Jog instead of sprint if form breaks down. Focus: Best for trail timing, stop control, catch rhythm, and shot balance.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the player to arrive late as a trailer, slow down, and shoot in rhythm. It helps with transition trailing shots.
drills.safety: No fatigue heaves. Stop if legs or mechanics fail.

drills.name: Elbow Sprint Back Shot
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: The player starts under the rim, sprints out to the elbow, catches a pass, sets the feet, and shoots. Work both elbows. Keep the sprint short and controlled.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players learning to shoot after moving away from the basket. Triggers: Assign if the player fades backward or rushes elbow shots. Avoid/modify: Use jog speed if the athlete cannot plant safely. Focus: Best for elbow footwork, conditioning, catch balance, and midrange accuracy.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the player to sprint away from the rim, plant at the elbow, and shoot. It builds conditioning and footwork for midrange shots.
drills.safety: No hard backward plant. Keep the feet under control.

drills.name: Nail Step-Out Shot
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: The player starts at the nail or free throw line area. The player takes one controlled step to either side, catches or self-loads, and shoots. Work both directions.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players learning midrange shot windows. Triggers: Assign if the player shoots crowded nail shots without moving to space. Avoid/modify: Use shorter step if the athlete loses balance. Focus: Best for midrange spacing, side-step control, balance, and release consistency.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the player to step out from the nail area and shoot with balance. It helps players create a clear midrange shot window.
drills.safety: No wide lunge. Keep the step under the hips.

drills.name: Elbow-to-Wing Relocation Shot
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: The player starts at the elbow. On cue, the player relocates to the wing, catches a pass, squares the feet, and shoots. Work both sides.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players learning to move out of traffic for shots. Triggers: Assign if the player stays crowded at the elbow instead of moving to space. Avoid/modify: Walk the relocation first. Focus: Best for relocation, catch balance, footwork, and shot prep.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the player to move from the elbow to the wing, catch, and shoot. It builds relocation after leaving a crowded middle area.
drills.safety: No cutting through other players. Keep the path clear.

drills.name: Wing-to-Elbow Pull Shot
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: The player starts at the wing, jogs or cuts to the elbow, catches a pass, and shoots. The player should arrive with feet ready and shoulders square. Work both sides.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players learning wing-to-elbow shooting movement. Triggers: Assign if the player catches at the elbow with poor feet or rushed shoulders. Avoid/modify: Use walk-speed if the athlete cannot set the feet. Focus: Best for movement timing, elbow shooting, catch readiness, and balance.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the player to move from the wing into the elbow area and shoot on balance. It helps with controlled midrange rhythm.
drills.safety: Do not plant hard into the elbow. Stop under control.

drills.name: Dribble Drag Pull-Up
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: The player starts at the wing. The player takes two controlled dribbles, lets the last dribble slow the body, gathers, and shoots from midrange. Work both hands and sides.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players learning smoother off-dribble rhythm. Triggers: Assign if the player's pull-up is rushed or off balance. Avoid/modify: Use one slower dribble if the player loses control. Focus: Best for pull-up rhythm, dribble control, gather balance, and midrange shot consistency.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the player to drag the dribble into a balanced pull-up. It helps players who stop too suddenly or shoot off one foot.
drills.safety: No full-speed pull-ups until the landing and base are safe.

drills.name: Crossover Stop Jumper
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: The player starts at the slot. The player takes one crossover dribble, plants under control, gathers, and shoots from midrange. Work both directions.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players learning to shoot after a change of direction. Triggers: Assign if the player can dribble but cannot shoot after changing direction. Avoid/modify: Use a slower crossover or shorter distance if control breaks down. Focus: Best for crossover control, stop balance, gather timing, and shot accuracy.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the player to use a controlled crossover, stop, and shoot. It is harder than basic shooting because the player must control the ball and feet before release.
drills.safety: No hard plant if the knees or ankles are unstable.

drills.name: Inside-Out Pull-Up
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: The player starts at the wing or slot. The player uses one inside-out dribble, steps into balance, gathers, and shoots from safe range. Work both hands.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players ready to connect ball handling and shooting. Triggers: Assign if the player loses rhythm after a dribble move. Avoid/modify: Use no shot and just the gather if the move is uncontrolled. Focus: Best for inside-out control, pull-up rhythm, gather balance, and shot readiness.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the player to use an inside-out dribble into a pull-up shot. It helps with rhythm and shot balance after a ball-handling move.
drills.safety: Range must stay short enough that the athlete does not heave after the move.

drills.name: Behind-Back Gather Shot
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: The player starts at midrange. The player uses one controlled behind-the-back dribble, gathers with two hands, sets the feet, and shoots. Start slow and close.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players with safe intermediate ball control. Triggers: Assign if the player can dribble behind the back but cannot gather into a shot. Avoid/modify: Avoid if the behind-the-back dribble is loose or unsafe. Focus: Best for advanced gather control, foot set, ball handling, and shot balance.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the player to gather into a shot after a behind-the-back control dribble. It is for athletes who already control the move safely.
drills.safety: No speed until the dribble and gather are clean.

drills.name: Between-Legs Gather Shot
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: The player starts at the slot. The player uses one controlled between-the-legs dribble, gathers, sets the feet, and shoots from safe range. Work both directions.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players learning to shoot after intermediate dribble moves. Triggers: Assign if the player can do the move but shoots off balance afterward. Avoid/modify: Use a stationary gather first if the move breaks down. Focus: Best for dribble-to-shot control, foot set, balance, and release consistency.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the player to shoot after a between-the-legs dribble without losing the base. It helps connect intermediate ball control to shooting.
drills.safety: No deep shots after the move if the player throws the ball.

drills.name: In-and-Out Stop Shot
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: The player starts at the wing. The player uses one controlled in-and-out dribble, takes one step into balance, and shoots. Work both hands and both sides.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players learning pull-up rhythm after deception. Triggers: Assign if the player rushes after a fake dribble. Avoid/modify: Use a slower move if the ball gets loose. Focus: Best for change of pace, dribble control, stop balance, and shot rhythm.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the player to use an in-and-out dribble, stop, and shoot on balance. It helps with change-of-pace pull-up rhythm.
drills.safety: No hard plant. Keep the shot inside safe range.

drills.name: Hesitation Pull-Up Shot
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: The player dribbles toward the elbow or slot, gives a small hesitation, gathers, and shoots. The hesitation should slow the body, not make the player stand tall or lose the ball.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players learning to shoot out of change of speed. Triggers: Assign if the player hesitates well but cannot shoot afterward. Avoid/modify: Use a stationary hesitation gather before adding movement. Focus: Best for hesitation control, gather timing, body balance, and pull-up accuracy.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the player to hesitate, gather, and shoot without drifting. It helps players who stop defenders with rhythm but lose their shot base.
drills.safety: No deep pull-up if mechanics break down.

drills.name: Retreat Dribble Shot
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: The player starts at midrange. The player takes one retreat dribble backward, plants under control, gathers, and shoots. The shot should go up balanced, not leaning back.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players learning safe space-creation shooting. Triggers: Assign if the player steps back but fades or loses power. Avoid/modify: Use short retreat distance if the athlete lacks strength. Focus: Best for retreat control, balance, space creation, and release consistency.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the player to retreat one dribble, reset balance, and shoot. It helps players create space without turning the shot into a fadeaway.
drills.safety: Do not retreat into another player. Check space behind.

drills.name: Snatch Stop Jumper
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: The player dribbles forward, pulls the ball back with control, stops the feet, gathers, and shoots from midrange. Start slow. The stop should be clean, not a fall backward.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players learning to decelerate into shots. Triggers: Assign if the player cannot stop quickly without losing the ball. Avoid/modify: Use retreat dribble shot first if the snatch stop is unsafe. Focus: Best for deceleration, snatch control, foot stop, and shot balance.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the player to stop the ball quickly with a snatch dribble and shoot under control. It helps with deceleration and balance.
drills.safety: No violent stop. Protect knees and ankles.

drills.name: Side-Step Midrange Shot
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: The player starts at the elbow or wing. The player takes one controlled side step, sets the feet, and shoots. Work both directions. Keep the step short.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players learning simple space creation. Triggers: Assign if the player side-steps but shoots while leaning. Avoid/modify: Use a shorter step if the player loses balance. Focus: Best for side-step control, balance, shot window creation, and release consistency.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the player to move one step to the side and shoot without drifting. It helps create a clean shooting window.
drills.safety: No wide lunge. Keep the step controlled.

drills.name: Side-Step Three-Point Shot
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: The player starts behind the three-point line at a comfortable spot. The player takes one small side step, gathers, and shoots. The coach should watch for heaving, shoulder strain, or drifting. Work both directions.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Older players with clean three-point mechanics. Triggers: Assign if the player is ready for three-point range but loses balance on side steps. Avoid/modify: Use midrange side-step shots if the athlete heaves from three. Focus: Best for range strength, side-step balance, release consistency, and shot selection.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the player to side-step into a three-point shot only if their strength and form are ready. It is harder than midrange because range and footwork both matter.
drills.safety: No heaving. Move inside if the shot breaks down.

drills.name: Step-In Three-Point Shot
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: The player starts one step behind the line. The player steps in behind the line, catches or self-loads the ball, and shoots. The step should build rhythm, not extra speed.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players building safe three-point rhythm. Triggers: Assign if the player shoots threes flat or without leg rhythm. Avoid/modify: Use midrange step-in shots if form breaks down. Focus: Best for range rhythm, leg drive, footwork, and release consistency.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the player to step into a three-point shot from a shorter rhythm step. It helps players use their legs instead of throwing with the arms.
drills.safety: Move closer if the player uses arms more than legs.

drills.name: Range Hold Shot
drills.reps_target: 3 shots
drills.instructions: The player starts at midrange and shoots 3 shots. If all 3 look smooth, the player moves back one step. If the shot turns into a heave, the player moves in. The coach tracks the clean range.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players learning safe shooting range. Triggers: Assign if the player shoots from too far and breaks mechanics. Avoid/modify: Use fewer shots if fatigue changes mechanics. Focus: Best for range control, form consistency, leg strength, and shot selection.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the player to shoot from the farthest distance where their form still holds. It helps prevent unsafe range habits.
drills.safety: The clean range is the limit. Do not reward heaves.

drills.name: Range Step-Back Limit Shot
drills.reps_target: 2 shots
drills.instructions: The player finds a comfortable shooting spot. The player steps back one small step, shoots 2 shots, then returns to the original spot. If form breaks, stay at the original spot for the day.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players safely building range. Triggers: Assign if the player wants more range but loses mechanics. Avoid/modify: Do not use from three-point range unless the athlete is strong enough. Focus: Best for range development, form control, leg drive, and self-awareness.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the player to test one step back from their comfort range without letting the shot break down. It helps build range carefully.
drills.safety: Only one small step back. Stop if mechanics change.

drills.name: Three-Spot Range Check
drills.reps_target: 3 shots
drills.instructions: Pick three spots in a straight line: close midrange, deep midrange, and safe long range. The player shoots 3 shots at each spot. The coach watches form, not just makes. The player marks the farthest clean spot.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players learning range honesty. Triggers: Assign if the player takes shots beyond clean mechanics. Avoid/modify: Use two spots only for younger athletes. Focus: Best for range awareness, form consistency, shot selection, and lower-body strength.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the player to compare shooting form at three distances. It helps the athlete learn where their reliable range actually is.
drills.safety: Stop at the farthest clean range. No forced deep shots.

drills.name: Deep Midrange Balance Shot
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: The player shoots from deep midrange spots: wing, slot, and top. The player must make the shot look the same as shorter shots. If the shot is flat or forced, move in.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players building range before three-point work. Triggers: Assign if the player is not ready for threes but needs range development. Avoid/modify: Use closer midrange if the athlete heaves. Focus: Best for deep midrange range, balance, release consistency, and leg drive.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the player to shoot from deep midrange without changing mechanics. It builds range before three-point volume.
drills.safety: Move closer if the shot loses arc or smoothness.

drills.name: Arc Ladder Shot
drills.reps_target: 3 shots
drills.instructions: The player shoots 3 shots at the same spot. First shot is normal arc, second shot is slightly higher, third shot returns to normal. The coach checks that the player does not throw the ball.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players learning arc awareness. Triggers: Assign if the player shoots too flat or cannot feel shot arc. Avoid/modify: Use closer range if higher arc causes a heave. Focus: Best for arc control, release feel, touch, and shot smoothness.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the player to change arc slightly while keeping the shot smooth. It helps players who shoot too flat under fatigue or pressure.
drills.safety: Do not force high arc from far range. Keep it smooth.

drills.name: Flat-to-High Correction Shot
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: The player shoots from a safe spot. If the shot is flat, the next rep must focus on legs, lift, and soft release. The coach asks the player to say "flat" or "good arc" after each shot.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players learning shot self-correction. Triggers: Assign if the player repeats flat misses without adjusting. Avoid/modify: Move closer if flatness comes from lack of strength. Focus: Best for arc awareness, self-correction, leg drive, and release consistency.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the player to recognize a flat miss and correct the next shot with better lift. It builds self-correction.
drills.safety: Do not fix flat shots by throwing harder. Move closer first.

drills.name: Backspin Under Fatigue Shot
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: The player does a short controlled movement, such as 5 lane touches or 10 seconds of light slides. Then the player catches and shoots from safe range. The coach checks backspin and balance.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players whose mechanics break down when tired. Triggers: Assign if the player's shot loses spin after movement. Avoid/modify: Reduce conditioning if mechanics collapse. Focus: Best for fatigue shooting, backspin control, balance, and release consistency.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the player to keep clean backspin after a short conditioning action. It helps show whether the shot stays controlled when tired.
drills.safety: Fatigue should be mild. Stop if form breaks or the athlete feels dizzy.

drills.name: Smooth Finish Free Throw
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: The player takes normal free throws. The coach watches only the last part of the shot: lift, release, and follow-through. After each shot, the player says whether the finish felt smooth or forced.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players with inconsistent free throw release. Triggers: Assign if the player's free throw has a late jerk or push. Avoid/modify: Move closer if regulation distance causes a heave. Focus: Best for free throw release, shot smoothness, follow-through, and self-awareness.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the player to make the end of the free throw smooth and repeatable. It helps players who jerk or push the ball late.
drills.safety: No shoulder strain from regulation distance. Use an age-appropriate line if needed.

drills.name: Two-Free-Throw Pressure Set
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: The player shoots two free throws. After the first shot, the player must reset the routine and shoot the second. Track makes, but also track whether the routine stayed the same.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players learning game-style free throw rhythm. Triggers: Assign if the player rushes the second free throw or changes routine under pressure. Avoid/modify: Move closer if the player cannot shoot without heaving. Focus: Best for free throw routine, pressure control, reset ability, and consistency.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the player to shoot two free throws like a game trip. It helps with routine, reset, and pressure control.
drills.safety: Do not add running punishments if mechanics are breaking down.

drills.name: Miss-Response Free Throw
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: The player shoots a free throw. If the player misses, they must step back, take one breath, say one cue word, and repeat the routine before the next shot. Track routine quality.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players who spiral after misses. Triggers: Assign if the player rushes after missing or shows frustration. Avoid/modify: Use closer free throws if misses are caused by lack of strength. Focus: Best for emotional reset, routine consistency, free throw focus, and shot confidence.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the player to respond to a miss without rushing or getting emotional. It helps with free throw routine stability.
drills.safety: No negative punishment for misses. Keep the reset calm.

drills.name: Free Throw After Short Sprint
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: The player jogs or lightly sprints from the baseline to the free throw line, catches their breath for one routine breath, then shoots one free throw. Keep the movement short and repeat 4-6 times.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players whose free throws change when tired. Triggers: Assign if the player shoots free throws differently after running. Avoid/modify: Use a walk-up version if the athlete gets too tired or dizzy. Focus: Best for fatigue control, breathing, free throw routine, and release consistency.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the player to shoot a free throw after a small burst of movement. It helps players control breathing and routine when slightly tired.
drills.safety: No excessive conditioning. Stop if dizziness or form collapse appears.

drills.name: Free Throw Heartbeat Reset
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: The player does a short movement task, then stands at the line and waits until breathing is controlled. The player takes one full routine and shoots. The coach tracks whether the shot stayed smooth.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players who rush free throws when breathing hard. Triggers: Assign if the player shoots before resetting the body. Avoid/modify: Remove movement if the player cannot recover safely. Focus: Best for breathing control, routine timing, free throw smoothness, and focus.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the player to calm the body before shooting. It helps free throw rhythm after intense play.
drills.safety: Do not shoot while dizzy or gasping. Reset first.

drills.name: Three-Make Free Throw Ladder
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: The player must make three free throws total, not necessarily in a row. After every miss, the player resets the routine. The drill ends when three makes are completed with clean mechanics.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players building free throw consistency. Triggers: Assign if the player makes one but cannot repeat the same routine. Avoid/modify: Use two makes for younger athletes or low-strength players. Focus: Best for routine repeatability, free throw consistency, focus, and release control.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the player to build a short streak at the line without rushing. It helps with routine repeatability.
drills.safety: Do not extend the drill so long that fatigue ruins mechanics.

drills.name: Free Throw One-Cue Shot
drills.reps_target: 6-10 shots
drills.instructions: The player chooses one cue, such as "legs," "smooth," or "hold." Before each free throw, the player says the cue quietly, shoots, and holds the finish. Use 6-10 shots.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players who overthink free throws. Triggers: Assign if the player changes too many things between free throws. Avoid/modify: Use a closer line if the player's cue cannot fix strength breakdown. Focus: Best for focus, routine simplicity, release consistency, and confidence.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the player to use one simple cue before each free throw. It helps avoid overthinking.
drills.safety: One cue only. Do not stack too many corrections at once.

drills.name: Make-Miss-Make Routine
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: The player shoots a free throw and the coach records make or miss. No matter the result, the player must use the same routine on the next shot. Do 8 total shots and grade routine quality.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players whose routine changes after misses. Triggers: Assign if the player speeds up after a make or tightens after a miss. Avoid/modify: Use fewer shots if attention fades. Focus: Best for routine stability, emotional control, free throw confidence, and release repeatability.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the player to keep the same routine whether the last shot was a make or a miss. It builds consistency.
drills.safety: No punishment for misses. The goal is routine consistency.

drills.name: Corner 3 Clean Base
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: The player starts in the corner behind the line. The passer delivers the ball. The player catches, checks that both feet are balanced and inbounds, then shoots. If the shot is a heave, move inside.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Older players with safe corner three range. Triggers: Assign if the player is ready for corner threes but steps out or loses balance. Avoid/modify: Use long midrange corner shots if three-point form breaks down. Focus: Best for corner three readiness, foot placement, balance, and shot consistency.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the player to shoot a corner three with a clean base only if they have the strength for it. It helps with corner spacing and foot control.
drills.safety: No sideline drifting. Move in if the athlete heaves.

drills.name: Slot 3 Rhythm Catch
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: The player starts at the slot behind the line. The player receives a pass, steps or hops into balance, and shoots. The coach checks rhythm and smooth release, not just makes.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players ready for slot three-point rhythm. Triggers: Assign if the player rushes open slot threes or shoots flat. Avoid/modify: Move to deep midrange if the athlete's form breaks down. Focus: Best for slot three rhythm, catch timing, release smoothness, and lower-body power.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the player to catch a slot three in rhythm without rushing the release. It helps players who get open at the slot but shoot with poor timing.
drills.safety: Range must fit strength. No flat heaves.

drills.name: Wing 3 Foot Replace
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: The player starts at the wing with feet slightly messy on purpose. The passer delivers the ball. The player quickly replaces the feet into a balanced base and shoots. Keep the range safe.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players who need better foot replacement before shooting. Triggers: Assign if the player catches open but feet are not ready. Avoid/modify: Use midrange if wing three strength is not ready. Focus: Best for foot replacement, wing shooting, balance, and shot prep.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the player to replace the feet into a better base before a wing three. It helps players who catch with feet too narrow or crossed.
drills.safety: Do not rush the feet so much that knees twist.

drills.name: Three-Point One-More Pass Shot
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: The ball starts at the top. It is passed to the wing, then one more to the shooter. The shooter catches and shoots. Work both sides. Use deep midrange instead of three if needed.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players learning one-more shooting rhythm. Triggers: Assign if the player is late getting ready after ball movement. Avoid/modify: Use midrange one-more shots if range is not safe. Focus: Best for extra-pass rhythm, catch readiness, spacing, and shot selection.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the player to receive an extra pass and shoot in rhythm from three-point range only if ready. It builds spacing and shot prep.
drills.safety: No forced threes. Move inside when mechanics fail.

drills.name: Three-Point Shot Prep Sprint
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: The player starts inside the arc, sprints out to a three-point spot, catches, and shoots. The coach checks whether the shot looks the same as a normal shot. Work only from safe range.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Older players ready for movement threes. Triggers: Assign if the player can shoot stationary threes but struggles after movement. Avoid/modify: Use deep midrange if the athlete heaves. Focus: Best for movement three readiness, stop control, range strength, and form consistency.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the player to sprint into a three-point shot with form control. It is for older players who already have safe range.
drills.safety: Stop if legs fatigue and the shot turns into a heave.

drills.name: Two-Spot Three-Point Alternating
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: The player shoots from the wing, then moves to the slot, then back to the wing. Use 6-10 total shots. The player must keep the same form at both spots.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players ready for controlled three-point movement volume. Triggers: Assign if the player can shoot from one spot but loses form when moving. Avoid/modify: Use midrange if the three-point shot breaks down. Focus: Best for spot-to-spot rhythm, range consistency, conditioning, and shot repeatability.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the player to alternate between two three-point spots while keeping the shot consistent. It builds rhythm and conditioning.
drills.safety: Stop before fatigue changes mechanics.

drills.name: Corner-to-Wing Three Lift
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: The player starts in the corner, lifts to the wing, catches, and shoots. The coach checks foot placement, balance, and whether the player stays behind the line without drifting.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players ready for three-point lift shots. Triggers: Assign if the player lifts late or catches off balance. Avoid/modify: Use midrange lift shots if range is not ready. Focus: Best for lift timing, foot placement, three-point balance, and shot readiness.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the player to lift from the corner to the wing and shoot from behind the line. It helps older players learn movement spacing.
drills.safety: No forced deep range. Move inside if mechanics break.

drills.name: Trail Three Drag Stop
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: The player starts behind the play, jogs to the top, catches a pass, drags into a balanced base, and shoots. Start at deep midrange if three-point strength is not ready.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Older players learning trail three rhythm. Triggers: Assign if the player trails open but rushes or drifts into the shot. Avoid/modify: Use trail deep-midrange shots first. Focus: Best for trail rhythm, stop balance, transition shot prep, and range consistency.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the player to trail into a three-point shot, drag the feet into balance, and shoot. It helps transition shooters stop cleanly.
drills.safety: No fatigue heaves. Move closer if the shot changes.

drills.name: Shot Fake One-Dribble Side Shot
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: The player catches at the wing, gives a small shot fake, takes one side dribble, gathers, and shoots from midrange. The fake must stay legal and controlled.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players learning a simple closeout counter. Triggers: Assign if the player shot fakes but travels or rushes the next shot. Avoid/modify: Use no shot until the fake and dribble are legal. Focus: Best for shot fake control, side dribble, gather balance, and midrange accuracy.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the player to shot fake, take one side dribble, and shoot on balance. It helps against controlled closeouts.
drills.safety: No travel on the fake. Keep the side dribble short.

drills.name: Closeout Read Pull Shot
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: A coach starts several feet away and closes out at half speed with hands up. The shooter catches, reads the space, and shoots if the closeout is late. No contact or block is allowed.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players learning to shoot against controlled closeouts. Triggers: Assign if the player hesitates too long on open shots. Avoid/modify: Use coach hand cue instead of moving closeout if the player rushes. Focus: Best for closeout read, shot timing, confidence, and release speed.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the player to read a short closeout and shoot before the defender arrives. It builds timing and confidence.
drills.safety: Closeout is half speed. Defender cannot jump into the shooter.

drills.name: Closeout Read Side Shot
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: The shooter catches at the wing. A coach closes out with a hand high. If the coach's hand is directly in the shot path, the player takes one side step and shoots. If not, the player shoots immediately.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players learning shoot-or-shift decisions. Triggers: Assign if the player either shoots into the hand or overdribbles. Avoid/modify: Use a cone hand target first if the live closeout is too much. Focus: Best for closeout decision, side-step control, shot window creation, and release consistency.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the player to move one step to the side when the closeout takes away the first shot. It builds controlled decision-making.
drills.safety: No contact. Side step must be controlled.

drills.name: Fly-By Stay Down Shot
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: The shooter catches at a spot. A coach runs by to the side as a controlled fly-by, not toward the shooter's body. The shooter stays balanced, waits a half-count, and shoots.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players who rush against fly-bys. Triggers: Assign if the player rushes or jumps sideways when a defender flies by. Avoid/modify: Use a walking fly-by if the athlete gets nervous. Focus: Best for shot patience, closeout discipline, balance, and release control.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the player to stay balanced while a defender flies past, then shoot. It helps players avoid rushing when the defender runs by.
drills.safety: Defender runs past the side, not into the shooter's landing space.

drills.name: High-Hand Window Shot
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: A coach stands several feet away with one hand high. The shooter catches, sets the feet, and shoots with normal mechanics. The coach does not jump or reach into space.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players who panic when a hand is up. Triggers: Assign if the player changes form when a hand is up. Avoid/modify: Increase distance from the hand if the shooter rushes. Focus: Best for contest awareness, release focus, balance, and confidence.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the player to find a clean shooting window against a high hand without changing the shot too much. It builds calm contest awareness.
drills.safety: Coach must stay out of the landing area.

drills.name: Side Contest Balance Shot
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: The shooter catches on the wing. A coach stands to the side with a hand up. The shooter keeps balance and shoots without leaning away. No contact is allowed.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players who fade away from side contests. Triggers: Assign if the player leans away from side pressure. Avoid/modify: Move the contest farther away if mechanics break down. Focus: Best for side contest awareness, shoulder control, balance, and release consistency.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the player to shoot while a contest comes from the side. It helps the shooter keep the base and shoulders square.
drills.safety: No contact and no landing-space invasion.

drills.name: Late Contest Quick Lift
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: The shooter catches and starts the shot. A coach gives a late hand contest from a safe distance. The shooter focuses on lifting smoothly and holding the finish. No jumping contest.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players who are open but release too slowly. Triggers: Assign if the player is late getting the shot off. Avoid/modify: Use no contest if the player speeds up and loses mechanics. Focus: Best for quick release, shot prep, release smoothness, and confidence.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the player to get the shot up when the contest is late. It helps with quick but clean release.
drills.safety: Contest must stay away from the shooter's body and landing space.

drills.name: Shot Window Pause
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: The shooter catches the ball. The coach says "window" if the shot is open. The shooter pauses briefly, then shoots. If the coach says "hold," the shooter keeps the ball and resets.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players learning shot patience and selection. Triggers: Assign if the player shoots before seeing if the shot is clean. Avoid/modify: Use only "window" calls at first. Focus: Best for shot selection, patience, catch control, and decision-making.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the player to pause for a half-count, confirm the window is open, and shoot. It helps players who rush every catch.
drills.safety: No late panic cues. Keep the decision simple.

drills.name: Shoot-or-Swing Read
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: The shooter catches on the wing. If the coach shows open hands low, the player shoots. If the coach points to the next teammate, the player swings the pass and relocates. Keep the read simple.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players learning when not to shoot. Triggers: Assign if the player shoots every catch or never looks at the next pass. Avoid/modify: Use no shot and only reads if decision-making is slow. Focus: Best for shot selection, team awareness, catch decision, and spacing.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the player to decide between shooting and swinging the ball to a teammate. It helps prevent forced shots.
drills.safety: No rushed pass or shot. Control the catch first.

drills.name: Pump-Fake Read Shot
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: The player catches at the wing. If the coach closes hard, the player pump fakes, takes one side step, and shoots. If the coach stays back, the player shoots immediately. No contact.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players learning when to fake. Triggers: Assign if the player pump fakes every catch or never uses the fake. Avoid/modify: Use slower coach cues if the read is too hard. Focus: Best for closeout read, fake discipline, shot timing, and footwork.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the player to use a pump fake only when the defender is actually closing hard. It helps avoid wasted fakes.
drills.safety: No jumping into the defender after the fake.

drills.name: Dribble or Shoot Coach Read
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: The player catches at the slot. If the coach's hand is down, shoot. If the coach's hand is high, take one controlled dribble into a pull-up. Work both directions.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players learning shoot-or-drive reads. Triggers: Assign if the player shoots into contests or overdribbles open shots. Avoid/modify: Use only one read until the player understands it. Focus: Best for decision shooting, one-dribble control, shot timing, and balance.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the player to choose between a shot and one-dribble pull-up based on a coach cue. It builds simple game decision-making.
drills.safety: No live defense. The coach cue should be clear and early.

drills.name: Read the Under Screen Shot
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: Use a cone as a screen. The player dribbles toward the cone. The coach calls "under," and the player stops behind the cone space and shoots. Start at midrange.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players learning basic screen shooting reads. Triggers: Assign if the player does not shoot when the defender gives space. Avoid/modify: Use no dribble and just the read first. Focus: Best for screen read, pull-up timing, spacing, and shot balance.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the player to shoot when the defender goes under a screen. It helps players recognize when space is available.
drills.safety: No live screen contact. Use cone only.

drills.name: Read the Over Screen Fade Shot
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: Use a cone as a screen. The player moves around the cone. Coach calls "over." The player fades slightly to open space, catches or gathers, and shoots. Keep movement controlled.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players learning screen-read spacing. Triggers: Assign if the player curls into pressure instead of spacing away. Avoid/modify: Use walk-through movement if the player drifts too far. Focus: Best for screen read, fade control, catch balance, and release consistency.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the player to move away from the screen when the defender trails over. It helps with spacing and shot prep.
drills.safety: No live screens at first. Check space behind the shooter.

drills.name: Reject Screen Pull-Up
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: Place a cone as a screen. The player approaches like they will use it, then rejects the screen with one controlled dribble, stops, and shoots from midrange. Work both sides.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players learning reject-screen shooting. Triggers: Assign if the player always uses the screen even when the other lane is open. Avoid/modify: Walk through the reject if direction change is unsafe. Focus: Best for screen rejection, change of direction, pull-up balance, and shot control.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the player to reject a screen and pull up when the defender overplays the screen side. It builds shot control after a change of direction.
drills.safety: No sharp plant if the athlete cannot control the knee and ankle.

drills.name: Curl Screen Stop Shot
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: Place a cone near the elbow or wing as a screen. The player curls around it, catches a pass, stops in balance, and shoots. Work both directions.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players learning curl-screen shooting. Triggers: Assign if the player curls into shots while leaning. Avoid/modify: Widen the curl if the turn is too tight. Focus: Best for curl path, catch timing, stop balance, and release consistency.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the player to curl around a screen cone and stop into a shot without drifting. It helps with balance after tight turns.
drills.safety: No tight turn at full speed. Keep the path safe.

drills.name: Flare Screen Set Shot
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: Use a cone as a screen. The player flares to open space, catches a pass, squares the body, and shoots. The player should not fade backward unless that is a later progression.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players learning flare-screen shooting. Triggers: Assign if the player flares but catches off balance. Avoid/modify: Use shorter flare distance if the athlete drifts. Focus: Best for flare movement, square-up control, catch balance, and shot readiness.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the player to flare away from the ball and shoot after setting the feet. It helps with movement away from pressure.
drills.safety: Check space behind the shooter. No drifting into another player.

drills.name: Screen Away Return Shot
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: The player starts on the wing, jogs to set a screen-away position on a cone, then returns to the wing or slot, catches, and shoots. Keep the screen contact imaginary.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players learning team-action shooting. Triggers: Assign if the player screens or moves but is not ready to shoot afterward. Avoid/modify: Walk the route first. Focus: Best for off-ball movement, return timing, conditioning, and catch shot prep.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the player to screen away, then return to space for a shot. It builds conditioning and off-ball shooting habits.
drills.safety: No live screen contact. Use cones.

drills.name: Ghost Screen Pop Shot
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: The player jogs toward a screen spot, then quickly pops back to open space, catches, and shoots. The movement should be controlled and not a hard jump backward.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players learning pop timing. Triggers: Assign if the player pops too early, too late, or catches off balance. Avoid/modify: Use slower pop movement if balance is poor. Focus: Best for pop timing, footwork, catch readiness, and shot balance.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the player to fake a screen and pop into space for a shot. It helps with timing and shot readiness.
drills.safety: No hard backward jump. Land balanced.

drills.name: Pick-and-Pop Slot Shot
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: The player starts near the top as if setting a screen. The player pops to the slot, catches, and shoots. Use midrange or three-point range only if mechanics are clean.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players learning pick-and-pop shooting. Triggers: Assign if the player pops but is not ready to shoot on the catch. Avoid/modify: Use midrange pop shots if three-point strength is not ready. Focus: Best for pop spacing, catch timing, shot readiness, and range control.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the player to pop from a screen spot to the slot and shoot. It helps players who play as screeners or connectors.
drills.safety: Range must fit strength. No heaving.

drills.name: Slip-to-Short Jumper
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: The player starts near a cone as if setting a screen. The player slips into open short space, catches, and shoots from short midrange. Keep the shot controlled.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players learning slip timing and short shooting. Triggers: Assign if the player slips open but rushes the shot. Avoid/modify: Use a shorter movement path if timing is poor. Focus: Best for slip timing, short jumper touch, catch readiness, and balance.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the player to slip out of a screen early and shoot a short jumper. It helps with timing and soft touch.
drills.safety: No live screen contact. Keep the slip path clear.

drills.name: Handoff Keeper Jumper
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: A coach stands as a handoff partner. The player approaches, receives or keeps the ball in handoff motion, takes one controlled step, and shoots. No defender is used.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players learning handoff shooting actions. Triggers: Assign if the player rushes shots after handoff actions. Avoid/modify: Walk through the handoff path first. Focus: Best for handoff timing, gather control, shot balance, and release consistency.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the player to keep the ball after a simulated handoff and shoot a jumper. It helps with handoff timing and shot balance.
drills.safety: No collision with the handoff partner. Move slowly first.

drills.name: Handoff Turn Corner Shot
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: The player receives a handoff from a coach, turns the corner under control, takes one or two dribbles, and pulls up. Work both directions.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players learning to shoot after turning the corner. Triggers: Assign if the player turns the corner but cannot shoot balanced. Avoid/modify: Use no dribble first if the turn is poor. Focus: Best for turn-corner control, dribble gather, shoulder alignment, and pull-up balance.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the player to turn the corner after a handoff and shoot from midrange or safe range. It helps with shoulder and foot alignment.
drills.safety: No sharp corner at full speed. Keep the path clear.

drills.name: Relocate After Handoff Shot
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: The player hands the ball to a coach or teammate, relocates to the wing or slot, receives the return pass, and shoots. Work both directions.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players learning to move after handoff actions. Triggers: Assign if the player hands off and stands still. Avoid/modify: Walk the relocation route first. Focus: Best for relocation timing, catch readiness, shot prep, and footwork.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the player to give up the ball in a handoff action, relocate, and shoot. It helps with movement after the ball leaves the hands.
drills.safety: No running into the handoff partner. Communicate the route.

drills.name: Baseline Pinch Shot
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: The player starts a step inside the baseline. The passer delivers the ball. The player catches, sets the feet inside the line, and shoots. The coach watches foot placement.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players learning baseline shooting control. Triggers: Assign if the player steps out of bounds or fades from baseline shots. Avoid/modify: Move the player farther from the line if safety space is tight. Focus: Best for baseline awareness, foot placement, tight-space balance, and release consistency.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the player to catch near the baseline, keep feet inbounds, and shoot without drifting. It helps with tight-space shooting.
drills.safety: Check baseline space. No drifting into walls or supports.

drills.name: Corner Baseline Step-In Shot
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: The player starts near the corner baseline. The player steps in toward the wing or short corner, catches, sets, and shoots. The step should create balance and space.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players learning corner baseline footwork. Triggers: Assign if the player catches baseline passes off balance. Avoid/modify: Use shorter step if the athlete drifts. Focus: Best for baseline step-in, catch balance, footwork, and shot control.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the player to step in from the corner baseline area and shoot with balance. It helps with short-space footwork.
drills.safety: Stay inbounds and away from the wall.

drills.name: Short Corner Pop Jumper
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: The player starts near the block, pops to the short corner, catches a pass, and shoots. The player should stop before drifting baseline. Work both sides.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players learning short-corner shooting. Triggers: Assign if the player pops open but rushes the short-corner shot. Avoid/modify: Use stationary short-corner reps first. Focus: Best for short-corner spacing, catch timing, balance, and soft touch.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the player to pop to the short corner and shoot in rhythm. It helps with short-corner spacing and touch.
drills.safety: No baseline drift into support or wall.

drills.name: Dunker Spot Pop Shot
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: The player starts near the dunker spot. On cue, the player pops out to a short midrange spot, catches, and shoots. The player should arrive balanced before release.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players learning short-space relocation. Triggers: Assign if the player stays hidden near the rim instead of popping to space. Avoid/modify: Use a shorter pop if balance is poor. Focus: Best for short relocation, catch readiness, balance, and midrange touch.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the player to move from dunker spot to open short space for a jumper. It helps with spacing near the rim.
drills.safety: Stay clear of the lane and other players.

drills.name: Middle Flash Jumper
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: The player starts on the wing or short corner, flashes to the middle, catches, squares the shoulders, and shoots. Work from both sides.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players learning middle-area catch shooting. Triggers: Assign if the player catches in the middle but rushes the shot. Avoid/modify: Use catch-and-hold before shooting. Focus: Best for flash timing, catch balance, shoulder square, and midrange accuracy.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the player to flash to the middle, catch, and shoot with balance. It helps with shots from the high-post or middle area.
drills.safety: No defender or contact at first.

drills.name: Flash Pivot Jumper
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: The player flashes to the middle and catches. The coach calls "left" or "right." The player pivots that way, squares to the rim, and shoots. Start slow.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players learning pivot shooting after a catch. Triggers: Assign if the player catches in the middle and travels or shoots sideways. Avoid/modify: Use pivot-and-hold before shooting. Focus: Best for pivot control, shoulder square, shot balance, and catch security.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the player to catch in the middle, pivot, and shoot. It helps when the player catches with the body facing away from the rim.
drills.safety: Slow pivot. Protect the knee and ankle.

drills.name: Elbow Reverse Pivot Shot
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: The player starts with back or side to the rim at the elbow. The player catches, reverse pivots to face the basket, and shoots. Work both elbows and pivot directions.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players learning elbow pivot shots. Triggers: Assign if the player catches at the elbow and cannot face the rim cleanly. Avoid/modify: Use no-shot pivot reps first. Focus: Best for reverse pivot, elbow shooting, balance, and release control.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the player to reverse pivot at the elbow and shoot with balance. It helps with shots after catching under pressure.
drills.safety: Do not spin fast. Keep the pivot foot quiet.

drills.name: Elbow Front Pivot Shot
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: The player catches at the elbow with side or back to the rim. The player front pivots, sets the base, and shoots. Work both elbows and both pivot feet if safe.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players learning to square up from the elbow. Triggers: Assign if the player catches at the elbow and shoots before getting square. Avoid/modify: Use pivot-and-freeze first. Focus: Best for front pivot, square-up control, shot base, and release consistency.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the player to front pivot at the elbow and shoot. It helps players square the body before release.
drills.safety: No twisting through the knee. Pivot slowly.

drills.name: Post Kick-Out Catch Shot
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: A coach or teammate starts in the post with the ball. The shooter starts on the wing or slot. The ball is kicked out. The shooter catches with feet ready and shoots. Work both sides.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players learning inside-out shooting rhythm. Triggers: Assign if the player relaxes when the ball enters the post and is late on the kick-out. Avoid/modify: Use midrange if range is not safe. Focus: Best for inside-out readiness, catch timing, shot prep, and spacing.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the player to catch a kick-out pass and shoot with readiness. It helps players prepare for shots after the ball goes inside.
drills.safety: Pass must be controlled. Shooter should not drift into another player.

drills.name: Drive Kick Catch Shot
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: A teammate or coach drives from the slot and passes to the shooter on the wing or corner. The shooter has hands ready, catches, and shoots. Work both sides.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players learning drive-and-kick shooting. Triggers: Assign if the shooter is late or not ready on drive-and-kick passes. Avoid/modify: Use stationary pass first if timing is poor. Focus: Best for kick-out timing, catch readiness, spacing, and release speed.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the player to catch a pass from a driving teammate and shoot in rhythm. It helps with game-like timing.
drills.safety: No passing into the shooter's face or body. Keep spacing clear.

drills.name: Paint Touch Kick Shot
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: The passer drives or dribbles to touch the paint, then passes out. The shooter stays ready, catches, and shoots. The shot can be midrange or three depending on strength.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players learning paint-touch shooting timing. Triggers: Assign if the shooter moves too early or too late after the ball enters the paint. Avoid/modify: Use coach walk-through if timing is confusing. Focus: Best for paint-touch timing, shot readiness, spacing, and catch balance.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the shooter to wait until the ball touches the paint, then get ready for a kick-out shot. It helps timing and patience.
drills.safety: No traffic in the driving lane. Keep the pass safe.

drills.name: Baseline Drive Kick Shot
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: A coach drives baseline under control. The shooter holds spacing in the corner or wing. The coach passes out, and the shooter catches and shoots. Work both sides.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players learning baseline drive kick shots. Triggers: Assign if the shooter cuts too low or is not ready on baseline kick-outs. Avoid/modify: Use stationary kick-out pass first. Focus: Best for baseline kick timing, spacing discipline, catch readiness, and shot balance.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the shooter to prepare for a pass after a baseline drive. It builds corner and wing shot timing.
drills.safety: Passer drives under control. No baseline collisions.

drills.name: Lift After Drive Shot
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: The shooter starts in the corner. As the coach drives toward the baseline, the shooter lifts to the wing, catches a pass, and shoots. Work both sides.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players learning relocation on drives. Triggers: Assign if the shooter stays hidden in the corner during drives. Avoid/modify: Walk through the lift timing first. Focus: Best for lift timing, relocation, catch readiness, and shot prep.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the shooter to lift into space as a teammate drives. It helps players become available for a pass.
drills.safety: Shooter and driver must not run into the same space.

drills.name: Shake Behind Drive Shot
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: The coach drives from the wing. The shooter starts behind or near the slot, shakes into open space behind the drive, catches, and shoots. Start at midrange or safe three range.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players learning behind-drive relocation. Triggers: Assign if the shooter watches the drive instead of relocating. Avoid/modify: Use a cone route if the player does not understand the spacing. Focus: Best for shake timing, spacing awareness, catch balance, and shot readiness.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the shooter to move behind the drive into a passing window. It helps with spacing and open-shot creation.
drills.safety: No crossing into the driver's path.

drills.name: Drift Behind Drive Shot
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: The shooter starts in the corner or wing. The ball handler drives middle or baseline. The shooter drifts a few feet to keep a passing angle, catches, and shoots.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players learning drift timing on drives. Triggers: Assign if the shooter stands still and loses the passing angle. Avoid/modify: Use a shorter drift if the player cannot stop. Focus: Best for drift timing, passing angle, foot control, and shot balance.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the shooter to drift with a drive and stay ready for the pass. It builds timing and foot control.
drills.safety: Check sideline and corner space before drifting.

drills.name: Re-Space Catch Shot
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: Two cones mark a crowded spot and a better shooting spot. The player starts at the crowded cone, re-spaces to the open cone, catches, and shoots. Work both sides.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players learning spacing before shooting. Triggers: Assign if the player catches too close to teammates or in poor spacing. Avoid/modify: Walk the re-space route first. Focus: Best for spacing correction, relocation, catch readiness, and shot balance.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the shooter to move to better spacing before catching. It helps players avoid catching too close to teammates.
drills.safety: Move with eyes up. Do not cut through other players.

drills.name: Partner Relocation Race Shot
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: Two shooters start at different spots. Coach calls a shooting spot. Both players move there, but only the first clean player receives the pass and shoots. The other player clears out. Keep it safe and controlled.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players ready for light competitive shooting movement. Triggers: Assign if the player moves too slowly or gets confused in space. Avoid/modify: Use one player if spacing gets unsafe. Focus: Best for relocation speed, spatial awareness, catch readiness, and competitive focus.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the shooter to relocate quickly, catch, and shoot before a partner reaches the same spot. It adds light competition without contact.
drills.safety: No racing into contact. Clear rules and spacing first.

drills.name: Two-Ball Read Shot
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: A coach holds two basketballs. The coach passes one ball to the shooter. The shooter reacts, catches, sets the feet, and shoots. The second ball stays with the coach.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players learning reaction catch shooting. Triggers: Assign if the player is late reacting to passes. Avoid/modify: Use one ball if the athlete loses focus or flinches. Focus: Best for reaction, catch readiness, focus, and shot prep.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the shooter to react to which ball is passed and prepare quickly. It builds focus and catch readiness.
drills.safety: Coach should not fake throws near the face. Pass safely.

drills.name: Random Spot Coach Pass Shot
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: The coach calls a spot: wing, slot, elbow, or corner. The player moves there, catches a pass, and shoots. The coach should only call spots within the athlete's clean range.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players learning random spot readiness. Triggers: Assign if the player only shoots well from planned spots. Avoid/modify: Use two spots only if too many choices overwhelm the player. Focus: Best for reaction movement, spot recognition, catch balance, and shot consistency.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the player to move to a random shooting spot, catch, and shoot. It builds adaptability.
drills.safety: No sprinting to unsafe spots. Range must fit strength.

drills.name: Make-Then-Move Intermediate
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: Pick 5 intermediate spots. The player must make 1 shot before moving to the next spot. If misses pile up, cap the attempts and move closer. Track form quality.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players building multi-spot consistency. Triggers: Assign if the player loses form across multiple spots. Avoid/modify: Use 3 spots or closer range if fatigue builds. Focus: Best for shot consistency, focus, multi-spot rhythm, and range control.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the player to make a shot before moving to the next spot. It builds focus and controlled volume.
drills.safety: Cap attempts. Do not let misses turn into tired heaves.

drills.name: Two-Make Move On
drills.reps_target: 2 shots
drills.instructions: Choose 4 shooting spots. The player must make 2 shots at each spot before moving. The shots do not have to be in a row unless the coach progresses the drill later.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players building repeatable makes. Triggers: Assign if the player can make one shot but cannot repeat the same mechanics. Avoid/modify: Use one make per spot if the athlete fatigues. Focus: Best for repeatability, focus, form consistency, and spot shooting.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the player to make two clean shots at a spot before moving. It builds repeatability without requiring a huge streak.
drills.safety: Do not stay at one spot until mechanics collapse.

drills.name: Miss Two Reset Shot
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: The player shoots from a spot. If they miss two in a row, they step in one spot, make one clean shot, then return to the original spot. Continue for 8-12 total shots.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players who keep forcing bad shots after misses. Triggers: Assign if the player misses and keeps shooting harder from the same spot. Avoid/modify: Use only close-range reset shots for younger athletes. Focus: Best for self-correction, range discipline, focus, and shot quality.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the player to reset after two misses instead of forcing more rushed shots. It builds awareness and discipline.
drills.safety: Move in after misses. Do not reward heaving.

drills.name: Consecutive Clean Form Challenge
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: The player shoots from a safe spot. The coach counts a rep only if the shot has balanced feet, smooth lift, and held follow-through. The goal is 5 clean reps, makes or misses.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players who chase makes but lose mechanics. Triggers: Assign if the player makes some shots but the form changes every rep. Avoid/modify: Move closer if clean form is not possible. Focus: Best for form consistency, shot discipline, balance, and follow-through.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the player to repeat the same shot form several times in a row. It focuses on clean reps, not just makes.
drills.safety: Clean form matters more than range.

drills.name: Timed Ten-Shot Form Hold
drills.reps_target: 10 shots
drills.instructions: The player takes 10 shots from a safe range within a coach-set time window. The player must hold the follow-through after each shot. If the hold disappears, slow the pace.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players learning pace without rushing form. Triggers: Assign if the player speeds up and loses the finish. Avoid/modify: Use 5 shots if the athlete fatigues quickly. Focus: Best for shooting pace, follow-through discipline, form endurance, and focus.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the player to shoot at a steady pace while still holding the finish. It builds controlled volume.
drills.safety: Stop the clock if mechanics break. Do not chase speed over form.

drills.name: Make Under Mild Fatigue Shot
drills.reps_target: 5-8 shots
drills.instructions: The player performs 10 seconds of light defensive slides or jogging, then shoots from safe range. Repeat for 5-8 shots. The coach watches form quality.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players whose shooting drops when tired. Triggers: Assign if the player shoots well fresh but breaks down after movement. Avoid/modify: Reduce activity if the athlete gets tired too fast. Focus: Best for fatigue shooting, form endurance, lower-body control, and shot confidence.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the player to make shots after a short controlled activity. It builds game-like energy without exhausting the athlete.
drills.safety: No dizziness, no overconditioning, no heaving.

drills.name: Partner Rebound Pace Shot
drills.reps_target: 8-10 shots
drills.instructions: One player shoots from a safe spot while a partner rebounds and passes back. The shooter must be ready but not rushed. After 8-10 shots, switch roles.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players learning practice shooting rhythm with a rebounder. Triggers: Assign if the shooter rushes because the pass comes quickly or relaxes between reps. Avoid/modify: Use fewer shots if fatigue changes mechanics. Focus: Best for shot rhythm, communication, catch readiness, and conditioning.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the shooter to take shots at the pace a rebounder can deliver the ball. It builds communication and realistic rhythm.
drills.safety: Passes must be safe. Shooter should not shoot while off balance.

drills.name: Rebound Own Miss Shoot Again
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: The player shoots from a safe spot. If the shot misses, the player rebounds it, dribbles or passes out to the same spot, resets the feet, and shoots again. The second shot must be balanced.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players learning reset discipline after misses. Triggers: Assign if the player rebounds a miss and rushes the next shot. Avoid/modify: Use a partner rebounder if the player chases misses unsafely. Focus: Best for rebounding effort, reset balance, shot repeatability, and focus.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the player to rebound their own miss, reset, and shoot again without rushing. It builds effort and body control.
drills.safety: No diving for rebounds. Reset before the second shot.

drills.name: Game-Spot Eight-Shot Test
drills.reps_target: 2 shots
drills.instructions: Choose 4 game spots that fit the athlete's role and range. The player takes 2 shots from each spot. Track makes, misses, balance, and whether the shot looked clean. Do not count heaves as good reps.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players ready to test shooting zones. Triggers: Assign if the player needs to identify which shots are actually reliable. Avoid/modify: Use 3 spots or closer range if the player fatigues. Focus: Best for shot zone evaluation, form consistency, range control, and role fit.
drills.statistic: This drill tests whether the player can shoot from real game spots without form breaking down. It helps the AI and coach identify reliable intermediate shooting zones.
drills.safety: Only test shots inside clean range. No forced deep attempts.

drills.name: Advantage Pause Read
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: The player starts at the slot with the ball. A coach stands in the lane as a help defender, and two receivers stand on the wing and corner. The player takes one controlled dribble toward the coach, pauses for half a count, then passes to the receiver the coach points away from. Keep it slow at first.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players learning to make the easy read after drawing help. Triggers: Assign if the player draws help but throws late, panics, or forces the wrong pass. Avoid/modify: Use one receiver first if the athlete cannot process two options. Focus: Best for advantage recognition, pass timing, decision control, and ball security.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the player to pause after gaining an advantage and choose the simple pass instead of rushing. It helps players slow the game down when they draw help.
drills.safety: No live defender reaching. The help defender is a visual read only.

drills.name: Two-on-One Lane Read
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: Two offensive players start on the wings, and one coach or passive defender starts in the lane. The ball handler dribbles toward the lane. If the defender steps up, pass to the teammate. If the defender stays back, keep the dribble and stop at a safe spot. No finish is required.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players learning basic advantage decisions. Triggers: Assign if the player makes the decision before reading the defender. Avoid/modify: Use walking speed if the decision is too fast. Focus: Best for 2-on-1 read, timing, pass accuracy, and dribble control.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the ball handler to attack a 2-on-1 situation and decide whether to pass or keep the ball. It builds simple advantage playmaking.
drills.safety: No collisions with the lane defender. Keep the defender passive.

drills.name: Three-Lane Advantage Pass
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: Set three receivers: left wing, middle lane, and right wing. The ball handler starts at the top. A coach points to one closed lane as the player dribbles. The player must pass to one of the two open lanes. Start at walking speed.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players learning to scan more than one option. Triggers: Assign if the player locks onto one teammate and misses easier options. Avoid/modify: Use two lanes first if three choices overload the athlete. Focus: Best for scanning, lane recognition, passing accuracy, and decision speed.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the player to see three lanes and choose the open one. It helps playmakers avoid staring at only one teammate.
drills.safety: Keep pass distance age-appropriate. No long hard passes.

drills.name: Help Defender Shoulder Read
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: A coach stands in help position with shoulders turned slightly toward one receiver. The ball handler dribbles slowly toward the lane, reads the coach's shoulder angle, and passes away from that direction. Work both sides.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players learning defender body-language reads. Triggers: Assign if the player only reads the ball and not the defender's body. Avoid/modify: Use coach pointing first if shoulder reads are too subtle. Focus: Best for help read, visual processing, pass choice, and timing.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the ball handler to read a help defender's shoulders before passing. It helps players see where the help is moving.
drills.safety: No live steals. Coach gives a clear, safe read.

drills.name: Dribble Probe Kick
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: The player starts at the slot with a receiver on the wing. The player dribbles toward the paint. A coach steps into help. The player stops the drive early and passes out to the wing receiver. Work both sides.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players learning to pass out of controlled paint pressure. Triggers: Assign if the player drives too deep and loses passing vision. Avoid/modify: Use a cone help defender if the coach read is too hard. Focus: Best for drive timing, kick-out pass, dribble control, and help recognition.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the player to probe the paint with a controlled dribble and kick the ball out when help appears. It builds drive-and-kick timing.
drills.safety: No full-speed drive. Stop before the help defender.

drills.name: Middle Drive Spray Pass
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: The player starts at the top. Receivers stand on both wings. The player dribbles middle, and the coach calls left or right before the gather. The player passes to that receiver with control.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players learning middle-drive passing. Triggers: Assign if the player drives middle but cannot pass to the side on time. Avoid/modify: Use one receiver if two-sided passing is too hard. Focus: Best for middle-drive vision, pass timing, body control, and passing accuracy.
