drills.statistic: This drill teaches the player to drive middle and spray the pass to a side receiver. It helps with passing on time before the lane gets crowded.
drills.safety: No jump passes. Stop under control before passing if needed.

drills.name: Baseline Drive Lift Pass
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: The ball handler starts on the wing. A receiver starts in the corner and lifts to the wing as the ball handler drives baseline. The ball handler stops before the baseline gets crowded and passes to the lifting receiver.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players learning baseline drive passing. Triggers: Assign if the player drives baseline and throws unsafe passes under the rim. Avoid/modify: Walk through the lift timing before adding the dribble. Focus: Best for baseline vision, receiver timing, pass accuracy, and ball security.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the player to drive baseline and pass to a lifting receiver instead of getting stuck under the basket. It builds baseline passing vision.
drills.safety: Stay away from the backboard support and baseline traffic.

drills.name: Drive Stop Behind Pass
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: The player drives from the slot. A coach steps in front as help. A trailing receiver follows behind. The ball handler stops, pivots safely, and passes back to the trailer. No jump pass.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players learning to pass back out of stopped drives. Triggers: Assign if the player gets stopped and throws the ball into traffic. Avoid/modify: Use no defender first if the stop-pivot is poor. Focus: Best for drive stop control, trailer awareness, pivot pass, and ball security.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the ball handler to stop a drive and pass back behind to a trailing teammate. It helps when the defense cuts off the forward pass.
drills.safety: No jump passing. Stop and pivot first.

drills.name: Retreat Reset Pass
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: The player dribbles toward a cone or coach. When the coach says "reset," the player takes one retreat dribble, protects the ball, and passes to a safety receiver. Work both hands.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players learning to escape pressure without forcing the ball. Triggers: Assign if the player gets crowded and throws panic passes. Avoid/modify: Use a cone instead of live pressure if the player loses control. Focus: Best for retreat control, pressure escape, ball security, and safe passing.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the player to retreat one dribble, regain space, and pass safely. It helps players who panic when pressure cuts off the drive.
drills.safety: Check space behind the player. No fast backpedaling.

drills.name: Retreat Re-Attack Pass
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: The player dribbles at a cone. The coach calls "retreat," then "go." The player retreats one dribble, re-attacks under control, and passes to a receiver. Keep the distance short.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players learning second-read playmaking. Triggers: Assign if the player gives up or forces a pass after the first read closes. Avoid/modify: Use no re-attack if the retreat is not controlled. Focus: Best for retreat control, re-attack timing, second read, and pass accuracy.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the player to retreat away from pressure, then re-attack and pass when the lane opens. It helps with patience and second reads.
drills.safety: No sudden sprint. Control the retreat and re-attack.

drills.name: Pressure Side Pocket Pass
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: A coach stands in front with hands up but no reach. A receiver stands to the side. The ball handler keeps the ball on the outside hip, steps slightly, and passes from the side pocket to the receiver.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players learning to pass around front pressure. Triggers: Assign if the player brings the ball to the middle of pressure before passing. Avoid/modify: Use a cone pressure target if live coach pressure is too much. Focus: Best for ball protection, side-pocket passing, pressure control, and pass accuracy.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the player to pass from the side pocket of the body when front pressure is present. It helps protect the ball and make a short safe pass.
drills.safety: No defender swiping. Coach is a visual obstacle only.

drills.name: Hip-to-Hip Pass Window
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: Place a cone as a defender in front of the ball handler. A receiver stands slightly to the side. The passer shifts the ball to the outside hip and passes through the side window to the receiver.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players learning side-window passing. Triggers: Assign if the player keeps throwing into the defender's body line. Avoid/modify: Widen the passing window if accuracy is poor. Focus: Best for passing window awareness, hip-level control, ball security, and pass placement.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the passer to find a small passing window beside the body. It helps players avoid throwing through the defender's chest.
drills.safety: Keep pass speed controlled. No hard passes at close range.

drills.name: One-Hand Pocket Feed
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: A receiver shows a target near the lane. The passer starts at the slot, takes one controlled dribble, and gives a short one-hand feed to the receiver's pocket. Keep the pass soft and close.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players learning quick short feeds. Triggers: Assign if the player needs a quick short pass but throws too hard or late. Avoid/modify: Use two-hand feeds if one-hand control is unsafe. Focus: Best for short-feed timing, one-hand control, touch, and receiver accuracy.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the player to deliver a short one-hand feed into a teammate's target pocket. It helps when two-hand passing is too slow in a tight space.
drills.safety: No hard one-hand passes. Receiver must show ready hands.

drills.name: Touch Pass Redirect
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: Three players form a short triangle. Player A passes to Player B. Player B catches softly and redirects quickly to Player C. Player B should not slap the ball; they must control and redirect. Rotate roles.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players learning quick ball movement. Triggers: Assign if the player catches and holds too long or redirects without control. Avoid/modify: Use catch-pause-pass first if control is poor. Focus: Best for quick decision, touch passing, hand control, and passing rhythm.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the player to redirect the ball quickly without holding it too long. It helps with ball movement and fast decisions.
drills.safety: Soft passes only. No one-touch slaps at close range.

drills.name: One-More Corner Read
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: The player catches on the wing. A receiver is in the corner. The coach raises a hand as a closeout. If the hand is high, the wing player passes one more to the corner. If no hand, hold and reset.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players learning extra-pass decisions. Triggers: Assign if the player forces the wing play and misses the open corner. Avoid/modify: Use a fixed "pass every time" version first. Focus: Best for extra-pass timing, corner vision, closeout read, and pass accuracy.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the player to make the extra pass from wing to corner when the corner is open. It helps players move the ball instead of forcing a shot or drive.
drills.safety: Keep pass distance safe. No hard corner passes to young players.

drills.name: One-More Slot Read
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: The player catches on the wing. A slot receiver shows hands. A coach shades the lane. The player reads the coach and passes back to the slot when the lane is closed. Work both sides.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players learning reversal decisions. Triggers: Assign if the player keeps attacking a closed lane instead of reversing the ball. Avoid/modify: Use no coach first if the read is too much. Focus: Best for reversal timing, slot vision, pass accuracy, and decision control.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the player to make the extra pass from wing back to the slot when the slot is open. It helps with reversal timing.
drills.safety: Pivot under control. No blind backward throws.

drills.name: Second-Side Swing Read
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: Set receivers at top, wing, and opposite wing. The ball starts on one side. The player in the middle catches, reads the coach's help position, and swings the ball to the second side if help is loaded.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players learning second-side ball movement. Triggers: Assign if the player stops the ball and misses the open second side. Avoid/modify: Use two-player reversal first. Focus: Best for second-side vision, ball movement, timing, and team awareness.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the player to keep the ball moving to the second side when the first side is crowded. It helps with team spacing and patience.
drills.safety: No long skip passes unless the player has safe strength and accuracy.

drills.name: Slot-to-Slot Reversal Under Pressure
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: Two slot receivers stand on opposite sides. The passer starts at one slot. A coach stands nearby with hands up but does not reach. The passer pivots, protects the ball, and passes to the opposite slot.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players learning calm reversals under visual pressure. Triggers: Assign if the player turns the ball over under light pressure. Avoid/modify: Remove coach pressure if the pass is unsafe. Focus: Best for pressure passing, reversal accuracy, pivot control, and ball security.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the player to reverse the ball across the top while a coach applies light visual pressure. It helps with calm ball movement.
drills.safety: No reaching defender. Keep the pressure light and controlled.

drills.name: Skip Pass Read Short Court
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: Use a shortened court width. The passer starts on one wing, and the receiver stands opposite wing. A coach stands in the middle. If the coach steps toward the ball, the passer throws a controlled skip to the opposite receiver.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players learning weak-side vision. Triggers: Assign if the player never sees weak-side teammates or forces short-side passes. Avoid/modify: Shorten the distance or use a smaller ball if strength is low. Focus: Best for weak-side vision, skip timing, passing strength, and decision-making.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the player to read a skip pass across a short court distance. It helps players see weak-side options without forcing long passes.
drills.safety: No long hard skip passes for athletes without strength.

drills.name: Skip Fake to Swing Pass
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: The passer starts on the wing. A weak-side receiver and top receiver are available. The passer shows a controlled skip fake, then passes to the top receiver for reversal. Keep the fake tight.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players learning safer alternatives to skip passes. Triggers: Assign if the player forces long skip passes when the reversal is safer. Avoid/modify: Remove the fake if the player travels or swings wide. Focus: Best for ball fake control, shot-side patience, reversal decision, and pass safety.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the player to fake the skip pass and make the safer swing pass. It helps players avoid risky cross-court throws.
drills.safety: No wide ball swing. Keep the fake controlled.

drills.name: Skip Pass Window Hold
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: The passer starts on one side. A coach stands in the middle and moves one step left or right. The passer must wait until the coach clears the lane, then pass to the opposite receiver. Use short distance.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players learning skip timing. Triggers: Assign if the player throws skip passes before the lane is open. Avoid/modify: Use a shorter pass if strength or accuracy is low. Focus: Best for passing patience, skip timing, lane awareness, and ball security.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the player to wait until the skip pass window is actually open. It helps players stop throwing cross-court passes too early.
drills.safety: No hard pass if the receiver is not ready.

drills.name: Corner Lift Skip Catch Pass
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: The receiver starts in the corner. On the passer's dribble, the receiver lifts to the wing. The passer delivers a controlled pass as the receiver arrives. The receiver catches and secures, then resets.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players learning skip or swing timing with a moving receiver. Triggers: Assign if the receiver lifts late or the passer throws before the receiver is ready. Avoid/modify: Use short swing pass distance first. Focus: Best for receiver timing, passing accuracy, catch control, and spacing.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the receiver to lift from the corner and receive a skip or swing pass safely. It helps both the passer and receiver time the window.
drills.safety: No long skip if distance is too much. Use short court spacing.

drills.name: Corner Drift Pass Read
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: The ball handler drives from the wing. The corner receiver drifts a few steps along the baseline or sideline to maintain the angle. The ball handler passes only when the receiver shows hands. Work both sides.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players learning drive-and-drift reads. Triggers: Assign if the ball handler drives and misses the drifting receiver. Avoid/modify: Walk through the receiver drift first. Focus: Best for drive vision, receiver drift timing, pass placement, and spacing.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the ball handler to see a corner teammate drifting with the drive. It helps players pass to the moving corner receiver at the right time.
drills.safety: Receiver must stay away from baseline obstacles.

drills.name: Lift-Replace Passing Pair
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: Two receivers start at corner and wing. As the wing lifts, the corner replaces to the wing area. The passer waits, reads who shows first, and passes to the open target. Rotate roles.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players learning coordinated receiver movement. Triggers: Assign if receivers crowd the same spot or the passer throws late. Avoid/modify: Use walk-speed and no defense first. Focus: Best for spacing movement, receiver timing, communication, and pass choice.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches two receivers to lift and replace each other while the passer reads the open target. It builds spacing and timing.
drills.safety: No crossing into each other. Keep routes clear.

drills.name: Replace After Drive Pass
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: The ball handler drives from the slot. A receiver starts on the wing, replaces up or behind the drive, shows hands, and catches the pass. The ball handler passes out under control.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players learning drive-replace spacing. Triggers: Assign if the receiver stands still and the ball handler loses the passing option. Avoid/modify: Use cone route first if replacement timing is confusing. Focus: Best for replacement timing, drive vision, catch readiness, and spacing.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the receiver to replace open space behind a drive and receive a pass. It helps the ball handler see the replacement option.
drills.safety: No running into the driver's path.

drills.name: Fill Behind Ball Pass
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: The ball handler dribbles toward the wing and stops. A teammate fills behind to the slot. The ball handler pivots and passes back to the filler. Work both sides.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players learning support spacing behind the ball. Triggers: Assign if the ball handler gets stuck and no teammate fills behind. Avoid/modify: Walk the fill timing first. Focus: Best for support spacing, pivot pass, receiver timing, and ball security.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches a teammate to fill behind the ball and receive a safe pass when the ball handler is cut off. It builds support spacing.
drills.safety: No blind back pass. Pivot and see the receiver.

drills.name: Slot Exchange Catch Pass
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: Two players start at opposite slots. They exchange spots at a jog. The passer hits the receiver as they arrive at the new slot. The receiver catches, secures, and passes back or swings to a coach.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players learning slot exchange timing. Triggers: Assign if players exchange but arrive late or pass off target. Avoid/modify: Walk the exchange first. Focus: Best for exchange timing, catch readiness, passing rhythm, and spacing.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches two players to exchange slot spots and move the ball on time. It helps with spacing and communication.
drills.safety: Players must not collide during the exchange.

drills.name: Wing Exchange Pass
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: One receiver starts on the wing and one in the corner. They exchange spots. The passer waits for the new wing player to show hands and passes. Rotate after each rep.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players learning wing-corner exchange timing. Triggers: Assign if receivers cross paths or the passer throws too early. Avoid/modify: Use no pass until the exchange route is clean. Focus: Best for off-ball timing, spacing discipline, catch readiness, and pass accuracy.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches players to exchange wing and corner spots while keeping a clear passing lane. It builds timing and off-ball communication.
drills.safety: No crossing into the same spot. Talk early.

drills.name: Backdoor Read Pass
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: The receiver starts on the wing. The coach denies the wing pass with a hand. The receiver backdoor cuts at controlled speed. The passer reads the denial and passes to the cutter's safe target. No finish is required.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players learning backdoor passing timing. Triggers: Assign if the passer keeps forcing denied wing passes. Avoid/modify: Walk the cut first if timing is poor. Focus: Best for denial read, cutter timing, pass placement, and court vision.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the passer to read when a receiver backdoor cuts and deliver the pass safely. It helps with timing and vision.
drills.safety: No blind passes. Cutter must show hands.

drills.name: Face-Cut Timing Pass
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: The receiver starts on one wing and face cuts across the lane. The passer waits until the receiver shows a clear target, then passes. The receiver catches and secures. Work both directions.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players learning moving target timing. Triggers: Assign if the passer throws before the cutter is ready. Avoid/modify: Use walking cuts first. Focus: Best for cutter timing, moving pass accuracy, target recognition, and communication.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the passer to hit a face cut at the right time. It helps players pass to moving teammates without throwing too early or late.
drills.safety: No pass into the cutter's face or body. Target hands first.

drills.name: Curl Cut Hit Pass
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: A cone marks the curl point. The receiver curls around the cone and shows hands. The passer waits until the receiver clears the cone, then passes to the target. The receiver catches and stops.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players learning pass timing to curl cuts. Triggers: Assign if the passer throws behind the curl or too early. Avoid/modify: Widen the curl if the turn is too tight. Focus: Best for curl timing, pass angle, receiver tracking, and catch control.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the passer to deliver the ball to a teammate curling into space. It helps with timing around off-ball movement.
drills.safety: No sharp full-speed curl until the route is safe.

drills.name: Flare Cut Timing Pass
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: The receiver starts near the lane, flares out to the wing or corner, and shows hands. The passer delivers a controlled pass as the receiver arrives. Use shorter distance first.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players learning to pass to flare movement. Triggers: Assign if the passer throws late or the receiver flares beyond safe range. Avoid/modify: Use midrange spacing before longer perimeter spacing. Focus: Best for flare timing, pass strength, spacing, and catch readiness.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the passer to hit a teammate moving away into space. It helps with flare timing and pass strength.
drills.safety: Distance must match strength. No long forced passes.

drills.name: Slip Cut Feed
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: A receiver walks toward a cone as if setting a screen, then slips toward open space. The passer reads the slip and gives a short controlled pass. No defender is used at first.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players learning slip timing. Triggers: Assign if the passer misses the slip or passes late. Avoid/modify: Walk through the slip before adding speed. Focus: Best for slip read, short pass timing, receiver movement, and accuracy.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the passer to feed a teammate who slips out of a screen action. It helps with timing and short passing decisions.
drills.safety: No live screen contact. Use cone only.

drills.name: Ghost Screen Return Pass
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: The receiver approaches as if setting a screen, then pops back to space. The ball handler waits, protects the ball, and passes to the popping receiver. Work both sides.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players learning ghost-screen timing. Triggers: Assign if the ball handler passes too early or misses the pop. Avoid/modify: Use a slower pop if timing is poor. Focus: Best for ghost-screen read, timing, spacing, and pass accuracy.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the ball handler to pass back to a teammate who fakes a screen and pops out. It helps with timing and spacing.
drills.safety: Keep the pop path clear. No body contact.

drills.name: Handoff Keep-or-Give Read
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: The ball handler meets a teammate for a handoff. The coach calls "give" or "keep" early. If give, hand the ball safely. If keep, the ball handler turns the corner under control and passes to a receiver.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players learning handoff decisions. Triggers: Assign if the player fumbles handoffs or keeps when the give is open. Avoid/modify: Use give-only reps first if ball security is poor. Focus: Best for handoff timing, decision-making, ball security, and communication.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the ball handler to decide whether to keep the ball or give it on a handoff. It builds simple two-player decision-making.
drills.safety: No collision at the handoff point. Slow first.

drills.name: Handoff Flip Pass
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: The receiver cuts past the ball handler. The ball handler gives a short soft flip pass into the receiver's hands. The receiver catches and stops. Keep the pass close and controlled.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players learning soft handoff passes. Triggers: Assign if the player throws handoff passes too hard or late. Avoid/modify: Use a hand-to-hand exchange if the flip pass is unsafe. Focus: Best for handoff touch, receiver timing, pass softness, and ball control.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the player to make a short flip-style handoff pass to a teammate moving past. It helps with timing and soft touch.
drills.safety: Keep the receiver close. No hard flip passes.

drills.name: Handoff Reject Pass
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: A handoff partner approaches. The coach steps into the handoff path as visual pressure. The ball handler keeps the ball and passes to a safety receiver. No live steal.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players learning handoff counters. Triggers: Assign if the player forces handoffs into pressure. Avoid/modify: Use coach cue only before adding movement pressure. Focus: Best for handoff read, counter decision, ball security, and safety pass.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the ball handler to fake the handoff and pass to a different receiver when the handoff path is crowded. It helps with counter decisions.
drills.safety: No live trap. Coach is a visual cue only.

drills.name: Pick-and-Roll Hit Roll Man
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: Use a cone as the screen. The receiver starts near the cone, then rolls toward the lane. The ball handler dribbles off the cone and passes to the roll. No live defense at first.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players learning basic roll-man timing. Triggers: Assign if the player misses the roll or passes late. Avoid/modify: Walk the roll path first. Focus: Best for pick-and-roll timing, roll pass accuracy, court vision, and ball control.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the ball handler to pass to a rolling teammate after a screen action. It helps with timing and short passing.
drills.safety: No live screen contact. Keep the roll path open.

drills.name: Pick-and-Roll Hit Pop Man
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: The receiver starts near a cone as the screen. After the ball handler dribbles off the cone, the receiver pops to space. The ball handler passes when the receiver shows hands.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players learning pop timing. Triggers: Assign if the ball handler only looks at the roll and misses the pop. Avoid/modify: Use a stationary pop first. Focus: Best for pop read, pass timing, spacing, and receiver communication.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the ball handler to pass to a popping teammate after a screen action. It helps with spacing and reading the screener.
drills.safety: Receiver must stop in safe space before catching.

drills.name: Screen Angle Pocket Read
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: A cone marks the screen. The receiver rolls at a slight angle. The ball handler dribbles off the screen cone and passes through the open pocket between cone and coach. Keep the pass short.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players learning screen-angle passing. Triggers: Assign if the player passes into the screen body line or misses the rolling target. Avoid/modify: Use no coach obstacle first. Focus: Best for screen angle read, pocket timing, pass placement, and ball control.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the ball handler to read the angle of a screen and make the pass through the open pocket. It helps with timing and ball placement.
drills.safety: Short pass only. No hard pass into a moving receiver.

drills.name: Short Roll Read Pass
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: A passer gives the ball to a player around the free throw line area. Two receivers stand corner and dunker spot. The short-roll player catches, reads the coach's point, and passes to the open receiver.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players learning short-roll decisions. Triggers: Assign if the player catches short roll and freezes. Avoid/modify: Use one receiver first if the read is too hard. Focus: Best for short-roll vision, catch security, pass choice, and timing.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the player receiving in the short roll to catch and make the next pass. It helps bigs and connectors make simple reads.
drills.safety: No live defender at first. Catch and see before passing.

drills.name: Short Roll Corner or Cutter
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: The short-roll player catches near the nail. One teammate starts in the corner, and one cuts slowly toward the rim. The coach points to the closed option. The player passes to the open option.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players ready for two-option short-roll reads. Triggers: Assign if the player pre-decides and misses the open teammate. Avoid/modify: Use stationary receivers before adding cutter movement. Focus: Best for two-option read, cutter timing, corner vision, and pass accuracy.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the short-roll player to choose between a corner receiver and a cutter. It builds timing and decision-making.
drills.safety: Cutter moves at controlled speed. No blind passes.

drills.name: Roll Replace Pass
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: One teammate rolls toward the rim, and another teammate replaces to the top or slot. The ball handler dribbles off a cone screen, looks at the roll, then passes to the replacing teammate when the coach takes away the roll.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players learning second-option screen reads. Triggers: Assign if the player only sees the roll and misses the replace option. Avoid/modify: Use no roll first and just replace timing. Focus: Best for second read, replacement timing, ball screen vision, and pass accuracy.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the passer to hit the player replacing behind a roll. It helps the ball handler see the second action after the screen.
drills.safety: Keep all routes spaced. No collisions.

drills.name: Pocket Fake Skip Pass
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: The ball handler dribbles off a cone screen. A coach steps toward the short receiver. The ball handler shows a short pass fake, then passes to the weak-side receiver. Use short-court spacing first.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players learning pass-fake reads. Triggers: Assign if the player forces the short pass into help. Avoid/modify: Use a shorter skip distance if strength is limited. Focus: Best for pass fake control, weak-side vision, timing, and ball security.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the ball handler to fake a short inside pass and skip to the weak side when help collapses. It helps with eye control and timing.
drills.safety: No long skip if the athlete has to throw the ball.

drills.name: Snake Dribble Pass Read
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: Use a cone as the screen. The player dribbles around it, snakes back toward the middle, and reads a receiver lifting or cutting. The coach calls the receiver early. The player passes under control.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players learning controlled snake-dribble passing. Triggers: Assign if the player snakes the dribble but loses vision. Avoid/modify: Use no pass until dribble path is controlled. Focus: Best for snake dribble control, middle vision, receiver read, and pass timing.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the ball handler to snake the dribble into the middle and pass when a receiver opens. It builds patience and court vision.
drills.safety: No live trap. Keep the path controlled.

drills.name: Reject Drive Kick Read
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: A cone marks a screen. The player starts as if using it, then rejects away from the cone. A coach steps into help, and the player kicks to the open receiver. Work both sides.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players learning reject-screen passing. Triggers: Assign if the player rejects the screen but drives into help. Avoid/modify: Walk the reject step first. Focus: Best for reject read, change direction, help recognition, and kick-out accuracy.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the ball handler to reject a screen and pass when help steps up. It helps with change-of-direction playmaking.
drills.safety: No hard plant at full speed. Protect knees and ankles.

drills.name: Split Gap Keep-or-Pass
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: Two cones create a gap. The ball handler dribbles toward the gap. If the coach closes the gap, pass to the receiver. If the coach leaves it open, dribble through and stop. No finish required.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players learning gap decisions. Triggers: Assign if the player forces tight gaps or passes too early. Avoid/modify: Widen the gap or remove the coach if control is poor. Focus: Best for gap read, dribble control, pass decision, and body control.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the player to attack a small gap and decide whether to keep the ball or pass. It helps with controlled aggression.
drills.safety: No squeezing between people. Cones only at first.

drills.name: Split Gap Safety Outlet
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: The player attacks a cone gap. A coach steps into the gap. The player stops, protects the ball, and passes to a safety outlet behind or beside them. Work both directions.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players who need a safe escape when gaps close. Triggers: Assign if the player forces the ball into a closed gap. Avoid/modify: Use no dribble and pivot only if stop control is poor. Focus: Best for safety outlet vision, stop control, ball protection, and pressure decision.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the player to find a safety outlet when the split gap closes. It helps avoid turnovers.
drills.safety: No live body gap. Use cones and controlled coach cues.

drills.name: Trap Split Pivot Pass
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: Two coaches stand near the ball handler with hands up but no reaching. The player keeps the ball tight, uses one or two pivots, and passes to the open receiver. The trap is visual only.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players learning to pass out of trap pressure. Triggers: Assign if the player panics in traps or throws over defenders blindly. Avoid/modify: Use one coach pressure first. Focus: Best for trap composure, pivot control, ball security, and passing vision.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the player to pivot through light trap pressure and find a pass. It helps with calm ball security.
drills.safety: No reaching, bumping, or trapping the athlete's arms.

drills.name: Trap Middle Flash Pass
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: Two coaches show soft trap pressure on the sideline. A receiver flashes to the middle. The ball handler pivots, waits for the middle target, and passes with control. Rotate roles.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players learning the middle flash escape pass. Triggers: Assign if the player gets trapped and never sees the middle. Avoid/modify: Remove one pressure coach if the athlete panics. Focus: Best for trap escape, middle vision, receiver timing, and pass accuracy.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the trapped ball handler to pass to a teammate flashing to the middle. It builds escape timing.
drills.safety: Trap pressure must stay light. No grabbing or crowding.

drills.name: Trap Sideline Reverse Pass
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: The ball handler starts near the sideline. A coach shades the sideline forward pass. The player pivots away from the sideline and passes back to a reverse receiver. Work both sides.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players learning sideline pressure escape. Triggers: Assign if the player gets stuck on the sideline and throws risky passes. Avoid/modify: Use no pressure first if pivot control is poor. Focus: Best for sideline awareness, reverse passing, pivot control, and ball security.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the player to reverse the ball out of sideline pressure instead of forcing a pass down the sideline.
drills.safety: Stay away from walls and benches. No hard trap.

drills.name: Corner Trap Release Pass
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: The ball handler starts in the corner. Two receivers are available: one on the wing and one at the safety slot. A coach shades one receiver. The ball handler pivots and passes to the open outlet.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players who panic in corners. Triggers: Assign if the player traps themselves in the corner and throws wild passes. Avoid/modify: Use one receiver first. Focus: Best for corner pressure, outlet vision, pivot control, and decision-making.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the player to pass out of the corner before panic sets in. It helps with ball security and safe outlets.
drills.safety: No live double team. Keep corner space clear.

drills.name: Pressure Turnout Pass
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: A coach stands on one side as pressure. The ball handler pivots or turns away from the coach, keeps the ball tight, and passes to a receiver. Work both directions.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players learning safe pressure turnouts. Triggers: Assign if the player turns into pressure or exposes the ball. Avoid/modify: Use cone pressure if the player is nervous. Focus: Best for pressure turnout, ball protection, pivot control, and pass accuracy.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the player to turn out of pressure and pass without exposing the ball. It helps players avoid turning into the defender.
drills.safety: No body contact. Turn slow first.

drills.name: Contact-Free Bump Read Pass
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: A coach holds a soft pad near the ball handler but does not hit. The player dribbles slowly, sees the pad on one side, and passes away from that pressure to a receiver.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players learning to pass away from pressure. Triggers: Assign if the player dribbles into pressure or passes toward the pad. Avoid/modify: Use a cone instead of a pad if the athlete is contact-averse. Focus: Best for pressure read, pass-away decision, body control, and ball security.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the player to read body pressure without being bumped. It helps prepare for contact decisions safely.
drills.safety: Pad is a visual cue only. No bumping.

drills.name: Two-Touch Swing Under Pressure
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: Three players line up around the perimeter. A coach stands near the middle player with hands up but no reach. The middle player catches, takes one control touch, and swings the ball to the next player.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players learning quick but controlled ball movement. Triggers: Assign if the player rushes passes or freezes under light pressure. Avoid/modify: Remove coach pressure if the player cannot catch safely. Focus: Best for pressure rhythm, catch control, swing passing, and composure.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the player to catch, secure, and swing the ball quickly while feeling light pressure nearby. It builds calm passing rhythm.
drills.safety: No swiping from coach. Passes stay controlled.

drills.name: One-Second Ball Reversal
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: Three players stand top, wing, and opposite wing. The middle player catches and has one second to pass to the next receiver. Start with no defender, then add a coach point cue.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players learning faster ball movement. Triggers: Assign if the player holds the ball too long after catching. Avoid/modify: Use two seconds if one second causes bad passes. Focus: Best for quick processing, reversal speed, catch readiness, and pass accuracy.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the player to reverse the ball within one second after catching. It builds quick processing without forcing panic.
drills.safety: Speed cannot replace control. Bad passes do not count.

drills.name: Two-Second Scan Pass
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: The player catches at the top. The coach counts "one, two." During the count, the player scans left, middle, and right while protecting the ball. After the count, the player passes to the receiver the coach calls.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players who need better scanning patience. Triggers: Assign if the player passes to the first target without seeing other options. Avoid/modify: Use two receivers only if scanning three is too much. Focus: Best for scanning, patience, ball security, and pass selection.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the player to scan for two seconds before choosing the pass. It helps players who pass too quickly without seeing the floor.
drills.safety: Protect the ball during the scan. No defender reaching.

drills.name: Eyes-Only Fake Pass
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: Two receivers stand left and right. The player looks at one receiver, then passes to the other. The ball stays tight until the pass. Start slowly and focus on eye control.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players learning simple passing deception. Triggers: Assign if the player telegraphs every pass with eyes and body. Avoid/modify: Use no fake if the player loses the real target. Focus: Best for eye discipline, pass deception, ball security, and target control.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the player to move a defender with the eyes before passing elsewhere. It helps with deception without swinging the ball.
drills.safety: No blind pass. The passer must still see the final target.

drills.name: Shoulder Fake Swing Pass
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: The player catches on the wing. The player gives a small shoulder fake toward the baseline, then swings the ball back to the slot. Keep the fake small and the pass accurate.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players learning controlled deception. Triggers: Assign if the player telegraphs passes or uses big unsafe fakes. Avoid/modify: Remove fake if the player travels or over-rotates. Focus: Best for shoulder fake control, reversal timing, pass accuracy, and ball security.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the player to use a small shoulder fake before swinging the ball. It helps move defenders without using a risky ball fake.
drills.safety: No big twist through the knees or back.

drills.name: Ball Fake Freeze Defender
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: A coach stands between two receivers. The player ball fakes to one receiver, waits for the coach to shift, then passes to the other receiver. The fake should stay close to the body.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players learning ball fake timing. Triggers: Assign if the player makes big loose fakes or passes into pressure. Avoid/modify: Use eye fake first if ball fake is unsafe. Focus: Best for ball fake control, defender manipulation, timing, and pass placement.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the player to use a tight ball fake, freeze the defender, and pass to the open receiver. It helps with passing under light pressure.
drills.safety: No wide ball swing. Keep the fake tight.

drills.name: Pass Fake Dribble Reposition
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: A receiver stands on the wing. A cone blocks the straight pass. The passer fakes the pass, takes one side dribble to open the lane, and passes. Work both directions.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players learning to improve passing angles after a fake. Triggers: Assign if the player tries to pass through a blocked lane. Avoid/modify: Use no dribble first if ball control is poor. Focus: Best for pass angle, ball fake, dribble reposition, and pass accuracy.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the player to fake a pass, take one dribble to a better angle, and then pass. It helps avoid forcing bad lanes.
drills.safety: One controlled dribble only. No rushing.

drills.name: Inside Pivot Skip Look
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: The player catches at the wing. The player inside pivots, looks across the court, and passes to either the safety receiver or weak-side receiver based on the coach's cue.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players learning vision off the catch. Triggers: Assign if the player catches and only sees the nearest teammate. Avoid/modify: Use one receiver until the pivot is safe. Focus: Best for pivot vision, weak-side awareness, pass decision, and balance.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the player to pivot inside and look weak side before deciding the pass. It helps with court vision after a catch.
drills.safety: Pivot slowly. No twisting through the knee.

drills.name: Outside Pivot Safety Read
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: The player catches near the sideline. A coach shades forward pressure. The player outside pivots away and passes to the safety receiver or middle receiver based on the coach's hand cue.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players learning safe pivot reads. Triggers: Assign if the player turns into pressure or panics near sideline. Avoid/modify: Use no pressure first if pivot control is poor. Focus: Best for outside pivot, safety read, ball security, and passing accuracy.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the player to outside pivot away from pressure and choose the safe pass. It builds calm decisions after a catch.
drills.safety: No live reach. Keep sideline space safe.

drills.name: Reverse Pivot Middle Pass
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: The player catches on the wing with back or side to the middle. The player reverse pivots toward the court, sees the middle receiver, and passes. Work both sides.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players learning to find the middle after pressure. Triggers: Assign if the player stays turned toward the sideline and misses middle options. Avoid/modify: Use pivot-and-freeze before adding the pass. Focus: Best for reverse pivot, middle vision, passing angle, and ball protection.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the player to reverse pivot and pass to the middle. It helps players who get trapped facing the sideline.
drills.safety: Keep the pivot controlled. No spinning into another player.

drills.name: Drop Pivot Pass Away
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: A coach shades one side of the ball handler. The ball handler drop pivots away, keeps the ball tight, and passes to the receiver on the open side. Work both directions.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players learning to pass away from pressure. Triggers: Assign if the player pivots into pressure or exposes the ball. Avoid/modify: Use cone pressure if live coach cue is too hard. Focus: Best for drop pivot, pressure escape, ball security, and pass accuracy.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the player to drop pivot away from pressure and pass to a teammate. It helps with safe pressure escape.
drills.safety: No contact pressure. Keep the ball close.

drills.name: Pivot Count Escape
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: The player catches the ball. The coach calls "one" or "two." On one, the player pivots once and passes. On two, the player pivots twice before passing. Receivers show hands.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players who pass too early under pressure. Triggers: Assign if the player panics after the first pivot. Avoid/modify: Use one pivot only if footwork is poor. Focus: Best for pivot patience, ball security, decision timing, and pass accuracy.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the player to stay calm and pivot more than once before passing. It helps when the first passing lane is closed.
drills.safety: No travel. Keep the pivot foot legal.

drills.name: Dribble Freeze Defender Read
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: The ball handler dribbles at a coach. The coach shifts left or right. The player waits until the shift is clear, then passes to the opposite receiver. Start at slow speed.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players learning to manipulate help with the dribble. Triggers: Assign if the player passes before moving the defender. Avoid/modify: Use a stationary ball fake if dribble control is poor. Focus: Best for dribble manipulation, defender read, pass timing, and patience.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the player to freeze a defender with a controlled dribble, then pass when the defender shifts. It builds timing and patience.
drills.safety: No live steal. Coach shifts only.

drills.name: Hesitation Pass Read
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: The player dribbles from the slot, gives a small hesitation, reads the coach's movement, and passes to the receiver who opens. Work both hands and sides.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players learning change-of-pace passing. Triggers: Assign if the player hesitates but does not create a passing read. Avoid/modify: Use no pass first if hesitation control is poor. Focus: Best for hesitation control, timing, deception, and pass accuracy.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the player to use a hesitation to make the defender pause, then pass. It helps with timing and deception.
drills.safety: No high-speed hesitation until the ball is controlled.

drills.name: Change-Speed Kick Pass
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: The player dribbles slowly, then speeds up for one or two steps. When the coach steps toward the ball, the player kicks to the receiver. Keep the pass controlled.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players learning speed-change playmaking. Triggers: Assign if the player drives at one speed and misses help. Avoid/modify: Use no speed-up if the athlete loses control. Focus: Best for change speed, help reaction, kick timing, and passing control.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the player to change speed on the drive and pass when help reacts. It helps with drive-and-kick rhythm.
drills.safety: Speed change should be short. No full-speed crash into help.

drills.name: Stop-Start Draw Pass
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: The ball handler dribbles toward the paint, stops briefly, then starts again. A coach steps toward the ball on the second start. The player passes to the receiver the help leaves.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players learning to create help reactions. Triggers: Assign if the player cannot change rhythm before passing. Avoid/modify: Use a walk-through if stop-start control is poor. Focus: Best for stop-start control, help draw, pass timing, and body control.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the player to stop, start again, draw help, and pass. It helps players create the pass instead of waiting for it.
drills.safety: No hard stop that hurts knees or ankles.

drills.name: Crossover Draw Kick
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: The player starts at the top. A coach shades one side. The player crosses over away from the shade, draws the coach, and passes to the receiver on the open side. Work both directions.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players learning purposeful crossover passing. Triggers: Assign if the player uses crossovers without seeing teammates. Avoid/modify: Use a slower crossover if the ball gets loose. Focus: Best for crossover control, defender shift, kick pass, and timing.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the player to use a crossover to shift the defense and pass to the open side. It builds ball handling with purpose.
drills.safety: No hard plant at full speed. Keep the crossover controlled.

drills.name: Between-Legs Reset Pass
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: The player dribbles toward a cone, uses one controlled between-the-legs dribble to reset direction, then passes to a receiver. Keep the move slow and clean.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players with safe intermediate ball handling. Triggers: Assign if the player can use the move but cannot pass after it. Avoid/modify: Avoid if the between-the-legs dribble is not controlled. Focus: Best for reset dribble, body control, pass timing, and ball security.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the player to use a between-the-legs dribble to reset the body and pass. It helps when the first lane closes.
drills.safety: No advanced dribble move if control is poor.

drills.name: Behind-Back Escape Pass
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: The player dribbles toward a cone pressure point, uses one behind-the-back dribble away from it, then passes to a receiver. Start slow and close.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Older intermediate players with safe ball control. Triggers: Assign if the player can do the move but loses vision after it. Avoid/modify: Use retreat reset pass if the behind-the-back dribble is loose. Focus: Best for escape dribble, pressure control, pass timing, and ball security.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the player to use a controlled behind-the-back dribble to escape pressure and pass. It is for players who already own the move safely.
drills.safety: No speed until the move and pass are clean.

drills.name: Spin Out Safety Pass
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: A cone marks pressure on one side. The player dribbles toward it, uses a slow controlled spin away, keeps the ball tight, and passes to a safety receiver. Work both directions.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players learning safe spin decisions. Triggers: Assign if the player spins into trouble or loses the ball after spinning. Avoid/modify: Use a pivot escape instead if spin control is unsafe. Focus: Best for spin control, safety pass, ball security, and body balance.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the player to spin away from pressure and pass to safety. It helps players who spin without a plan.
drills.safety: No fast spin near other players. Stop if dizziness or balance loss appears.

drills.name: Pullback Pass Window
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: The player dribbles toward a cone. The player pulls the dribble back one step, sees the receiver on the side, and passes. The pullback should create space, not a deep retreat.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players learning pass windows after pullback dribbles. Triggers: Assign if the player keeps driving into a closed lane. Avoid/modify: Use retreat reset pass if pullback control is poor. Focus: Best for pullback control, space creation, passing window, and ball security.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the player to pull the ball back to create space and pass through a new window. It helps against pressure without forcing contact.
drills.safety: Check space behind the player. No hard backward jump.

drills.name: Double Retreat Reset Pass
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: The player dribbles toward a coach. The coach calls "one" or "two." The player takes that many retreat dribbles, protects the ball, and passes to a receiver. Work both hands.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players learning controlled patience under pressure. Triggers: Assign if the player panics after one retreat or backs up too far. Avoid/modify: Use one retreat only if the athlete loses space. Focus: Best for retreat patience, pressure control, ball security, and pass timing.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the player to retreat twice only when needed, then pass safely. It helps with patience against pressure.
drills.safety: No retreating into traffic or walls.

drills.name: Live Dribble Count Pass
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: The coach calls "two" or "three." The player dribbles that many times, scans the floor, and passes to the receiver. The receiver must show hands before the pass.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players learning dribble rhythm into passing. Triggers: Assign if the player dribbles without purpose or passes randomly. Avoid/modify: Use one count only if the athlete struggles. Focus: Best for dribble rhythm, timing, eyes-up control, and pass readiness.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the player to pass after a specific dribble count while keeping eyes up. It builds rhythm and control.
drills.safety: No speed dribbling. Count and control first.

drills.name: Pass on Coach Clap
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: The player dribbles in place or slowly forward. The coach claps once. On the clap, the player picks the ball up and passes to the receiver. The receiver must be ready.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players learning reaction timing. Triggers: Assign if the player is late reacting or fumbles when picking up the dribble. Avoid/modify: Use stationary ball hold if dribble pick-up is poor. Focus: Best for reaction timing, dribble control, pick-up control, and pass accuracy.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the player to keep the dribble alive and pass on a reaction cue. It helps with timing and focus.
drills.safety: No surprise hard pass. Receiver must show hands.

drills.name: Pass on Color Call
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: Place colored cones or jerseys with two or three receivers. The player dribbles under control. The coach calls a color, and the player passes to the matching receiver.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players learning quick visual decisions. Triggers: Assign if the player is slow to identify targets under a simple cue. Avoid/modify: Use two colors before three. Focus: Best for reaction processing, receiver recognition, pass accuracy, and dribble control.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the player to react to a color call and pass to the matching receiver. It builds quick processing.
drills.safety: Use short passes. No hard throws to surprised receivers.

drills.name: Pass on Number Call
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: Three receivers are numbered one, two, and three. The player dribbles. The coach calls a number, and the player passes to that receiver. Rotate receivers after several reps.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players learning multi-target scanning. Triggers: Assign if the player loses track of receivers while dribbling. Avoid/modify: Use two receivers if three is too much. Focus: Best for scanning, working memory, pass accuracy, and dribble control.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the player to pass to the correct numbered receiver while keeping the dribble under control. It builds scanning and memory.
drills.safety: Keep the dribble slow enough for control.

drills.name: Coach Points Receiver Cut
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: Two receivers stand on the wing and corner. The coach points to one receiver, and that receiver cuts to open space. The passer reads the cut and passes when the receiver shows hands.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players learning to pass to moving receivers. Triggers: Assign if the passer throws late or misses moving teammates. Avoid/modify: Use one receiver until timing improves. Focus: Best for receiver tracking, pass timing, moving accuracy, and decision speed.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the passer to see which receiver is moving and pass on time. It helps with timing moving targets.
drills.safety: Receiver must show hands before the pass.

drills.name: Receiver Decoy Read
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: Two receivers start on the perimeter. One receiver makes a quick decoy step, while the other shows hands. The passer must ignore the decoy and pass to the ready target.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players learning to read target readiness. Triggers: Assign if the passer throws to movement instead of readiness. Avoid/modify: Use slow decoys first. Focus: Best for target readiness, patience, visual discipline, and pass choice.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the passer not to throw to the first movement if it is a decoy. It helps with patience and reading the real target.
drills.safety: No surprise pass to a receiver without hands ready.

drills.name: Receiver Screen-Then-Pop Pass
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: A receiver walks to a cone as if setting an off-ball screen, then pops to open space. The passer waits until the receiver arrives, then passes. The receiver catches and secures.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players learning to pass after off-ball screens. Triggers: Assign if the passer throws before the receiver clears the screen action. Avoid/modify: Walk the action first. Focus: Best for screen-pop timing, receiver tracking, pass accuracy, and spacing.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the passer to hit a teammate after that teammate screens and pops open. It builds timing around off-ball actions.
drills.safety: No live screen contact. Cone only.

drills.name: Receiver Seal Feed
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: A receiver seals a cone or passive coach near the lane with no contact. The passer waits for the receiver to show a hand target, then delivers a controlled feed to that side.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players learning interior feed timing. Triggers: Assign if the passer throws inside before the receiver has position. Avoid/modify: Use cone-only seal if contact is not safe. Focus: Best for seal recognition, interior passing, target placement, and patience.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the passer to feed a receiver who seals a position safely. It helps with timing and target placement inside.
drills.safety: No pushing or wrestling. Receiver shows a safe target.

drills.name: Receiver Re-Seal Feed
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: The receiver first shows a target, then loses it, then re-seals on the opposite side of the cone. The passer waits for the second target and feeds the ball safely.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players learning patience on interior passes. Triggers: Assign if the passer forces the first covered target. Avoid/modify: Use slow re-seal movement until timing improves. Focus: Best for re-seal timing, patience, interior vision, and pass accuracy.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the passer to wait for a receiver to re-seal instead of forcing the first inside pass. It builds patience.
drills.safety: No live contact seal. Use cone or passive body only.

drills.name: High-Low Feed Read
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: A passer starts near the elbow or high post. A receiver starts near the block. A coach shades one side. The passer reads the shade and feeds the receiver on the open side.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players learning high-low passing. Triggers: Assign if the passer throws high-low feeds into the defender's side. Avoid/modify: Use no coach first if angle is confusing. Focus: Best for high-low vision, passing angle, target placement, and timing.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the high player to feed a low receiver when the lane is open. It helps with timing and angle.
drills.safety: No hard interior passes at close range.

drills.name: Low-to-High Kick Pass
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: The receiver catches near the block or short corner. A coach shows light pressure. The player secures the ball, pivots, and passes out to a high receiver.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players learning inside-out passing. Triggers: Assign if the player catches inside and forces a bad finish or turnover. Avoid/modify: Use no pressure if pivot control is poor. Focus: Best for inside-out vision, pivot control, ball security, and pass accuracy.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the low player to pass back out to the high player when pressure comes inside. It helps with inside-out playmaking.
drills.safety: No elbows or contact. Secure first, pass second.

drills.name: Elbow Catch Split Read
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: The player catches at the elbow. One receiver cuts, and one receiver spaces out. The coach points to the covered option. The elbow player passes to the open option.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players learning elbow decision-making. Triggers: Assign if the player catches at the elbow and freezes or pre-decides. Avoid/modify: Use stationary receivers first. Focus: Best for elbow vision, split read, passing accuracy, and timing.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the player to catch at the elbow and choose between two passing options. It builds high-post playmaking.
drills.safety: No contact cuts. Receiver routes stay clear.

drills.name: Nail Catch Corner Read
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: The player catches at the nail. A coach stands in help. A corner receiver shows hands. When the coach steps toward the player, the player passes to the corner. Work both corners.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players learning nail playmaking. Triggers: Assign if the player catches at the nail and misses the corner option. Avoid/modify: Use a closer receiver if the corner pass is too long. Focus: Best for nail vision, corner pass, help read, and pass timing.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the player to catch at the nail and pass to the corner when help steps in. It builds middle-floor vision.
drills.safety: Corner distance must match strength.

drills.name: Nail Catch Dunker Read
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: The player catches at the nail. A receiver waits in the dunker spot. If the coach lifts toward the ball, the player passes down to the dunker spot receiver. Keep the pass soft and short.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players learning short interior reads from the nail. Triggers: Assign if the player catches middle and cannot see short passing options. Avoid/modify: Use a closer target if pass touch is poor. Focus: Best for interior vision, short-pass touch, help read, and target accuracy.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the player to pass from the nail to a receiver near the dunker spot when the defense lifts. It builds short interior vision.
drills.safety: No hard pass into the lane. Receiver must show hands.

drills.name: Free Throw Line Flash Pass
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: The receiver starts on the wing and flashes to the free throw line. The passer waits until the receiver shows hands, then passes. The receiver catches, secures, and returns the ball.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players learning flash timing. Triggers: Assign if the passer throws before the flash target is ready. Avoid/modify: Walk the flash first. Focus: Best for flash timing, pass placement, receiver tracking, and communication.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the player to pass to a teammate flashing to the free throw line. It helps with timing and middle access.
drills.safety: No pass into a receiver who has not shown hands.

drills.name: Flash Catch Backdoor Hit
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: A player flashes to the middle and catches. A teammate cuts behind a cone defender. The middle player turns, sees the cutter, and passes. Keep the cutter controlled and the pass safe.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players learning second-pass reads. Triggers: Assign if the middle player catches and never sees cutters. Avoid/modify: Use stationary cutter target first. Focus: Best for second-pass vision, cutter timing, target accuracy, and ball security.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the player who catches in the middle to hit a teammate cutting behind the defense. It builds second-pass awareness.
drills.safety: Cutter must show hands. No blind pass.

drills.name: Flash Catch Skip Read
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: The player flashes to the middle and catches. A weak-side receiver lifts. The coach shades the strong side. The middle player passes to the weak-side receiver.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players learning weak-side reads after a middle catch. Triggers: Assign if the player catches middle and only looks strong side. Avoid/modify: Shorten the weak-side pass if strength is limited. Focus: Best for middle scan, weak-side vision, pass timing, and receiver awareness.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the middle receiver to catch, scan, and pass to the weak side. It helps with middle-floor playmaking.
drills.safety: No long pass if the athlete has to throw with poor form.

drills.name: Top Catch Corner Skip
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: The player catches at the top. Receivers stand wing and corner. A coach shifts toward the wing. The passer reads the shift and skips or swings to the corner if open. Use short-court spacing first.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players learning top-of-key weak-side passing. Triggers: Assign if the player misses the weak-side corner or forces the wing pass. Avoid/modify: Use a swing pass instead of skip if distance is too hard. Focus: Best for top vision, corner skip timing, pass strength, and decision-making.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the player at the top to find the weak-side corner when help is loaded. It builds skip vision.
drills.safety: Use short-court distance until pass strength is safe.

drills.name: Top Catch Drive-or-Swing
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: The player catches at the top. If the coach backs up, the player takes one controlled drive dribble. If the coach steps up, the player swings to the wing receiver. Work both sides.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players learning top-of-key decisions. Triggers: Assign if the player dribbles every catch without reading. Avoid/modify: Use one cue at a time if decision is slow. Focus: Best for catch decision, drive read, swing pass, and ball control.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the player at the top to decide between driving and swinging the ball. It helps prevent automatic dribbles.
drills.safety: No live drive into coach. Keep the read controlled.

drills.name: Top Catch Delay Pass
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: The player catches at the top. The receiver starts covered by a cone or coach hand, then pops open after one second. The passer holds the ball safely and passes when the receiver shows hands.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players learning delayed passing timing. Triggers: Assign if the player passes too early or gives up on the receiver. Avoid/modify: Use a shorter delay if the athlete gets anxious. Focus: Best for timing patience, receiver read, ball security, and pass accuracy.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the player to delay a pass until the receiver gets open. It helps with timing and patience.
drills.safety: No defender reaching during the delay.

drills.name: Trailer Catch Reverse Read
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: The trailer runs to the top and catches. One receiver is on each wing. Coach points to the side that is closed. The trailer passes to the open side. Start with jog speed.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players learning transition trailer decisions. Triggers: Assign if the trailer catches and immediately throws to the wrong side. Avoid/modify: Use standing trailer catch first if running catch is poor. Focus: Best for trailer vision, transition decision, pass timing, and catch balance.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the trailer to catch in transition and decide whether to reverse the ball or hit the side. It builds transition playmaking.
drills.safety: Jog before sprinting. Catch balanced before passing.

drills.name: Transition Middle Advance Pass
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: The ball handler starts in the backcourt or near half court. A middle receiver runs ahead under control. The ball handler passes ahead to the receiver's chest or outside target. Use shorter distance first.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players learning transition advance passing. Triggers: Assign if the player overdribbles instead of advancing the ball. Avoid/modify: Shorten the pass if strength or accuracy is low. Focus: Best for transition vision, advance pass timing, passing strength, and receiver lead.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the player to advance the ball through the middle with a safe pass. It helps players avoid overdribbling in transition.
drills.safety: No full-court hard passes for younger or low-strength athletes.

drills.name: Transition Wing Advance Pass
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: The ball handler dribbles up the middle. A wing receiver runs wide. The ball handler passes ahead to the wing before the receiver reaches the corner. Work both sides.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players learning wing advance timing. Triggers: Assign if the player passes too late or misses the wide runner. Avoid/modify: Use half-court distance if full-court passing is too much. Focus: Best for wing vision, transition timing, pass placement, and spacing.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the player to advance the ball to a wing runner on time. It helps with transition spacing and pass timing.
drills.safety: Receiver must look back and show hands before the pass.

drills.name: Transition Drag Pass
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: The ball handler dribbles into the frontcourt. A trailer follows behind. A coach shades the forward receiver. The ball handler stops under control and passes back to the drag trailer.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players learning trailer usage in transition. Triggers: Assign if the player forces transition passes forward when the trailer is open. Avoid/modify: Use half-speed transition if the stop is unsafe. Focus: Best for trailer awareness, transition patience, stop control, and reverse passing.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the ball handler to find a drag trailer behind the play when the front options are covered. It helps players use late-arriving teammates.
drills.safety: No sudden stop at full speed. Control the body before passing.

drills.name: Closeout Chop Contain
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: The defender starts 10-12 feet away from a coach with the ball. The defender closes out under control, chops the feet, then slides one step in the direction the coach points. The defender freezes balanced with hands active. Work both directions.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players who can close out but get beat right after the closeout. Triggers: Assign if the player contests but cannot contain the next move. Avoid/modify: Use walking closeout if the athlete cannot stop safely. Focus: Best for closeout control, first-slide containment, stop balance, and hand activity.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the player to close out, chop the feet, then stay in front for one controlled slide. It builds the link between contesting and containing.
drills.safety: No live drive. Coach points only. Defender must not run into the coach.

drills.name: Long Closeout Brake and Box
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: The defender starts near the paint. A shooter or coach stands on the wing. The defender closes out under control. The coach calls "shot," and the defender turns to box out a cone or passive partner, then holds for one count.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players learning closeout-to-rebound habits. Triggers: Assign if the player flies by the shooter or forgets to rebound after closing out. Avoid/modify: Use a cone-only box-out if contact readiness is low. Focus: Best for long closeout control, braking, box-out reaction, and possession finish habits.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the player to close out from a longer distance, brake safely, then turn into a box-out shape. It builds the full defensive possession sequence.
drills.safety: No full-speed fly-bys. Use cones before partner contact.

drills.name: Closeout Read: Shoot or Drive
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: The defender closes out to a coach or partner with the ball. If the coach raises the ball, the defender contests with hands high. If the coach drops the ball to dribble position, the defender chops feet and slides one step to contain. Keep it half speed.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players who guess during closeouts. Triggers: Assign if the player jumps at drives or stays flat-footed on shots. Avoid/modify: Use verbal calls before visual reads if the player reacts late. Focus: Best for closeout read, reaction control, contest discipline, and contain footwork.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the defender to read whether the offensive player is shooting or putting the ball down. It builds defensive reaction after the closeout.
drills.safety: No live blow-by. Offensive player shows the cue only.

drills.name: Closeout High-Hand Low-Hand Read
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
