drills.instructions: The defender closes out to a coach. If the ball is above the shoulders, the defender shows a high hand. If the ball is at the hip, the defender shows a low hand and stays down. The defender freezes after each cue.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players who reach or jump on every closeout. Triggers: Assign if the player swipes down or jumps at shot fakes. Avoid/modify: Use stationary reads before adding the closeout. Focus: Best for hand discipline, contest control, reaction timing, and foul prevention.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the defender to choose the correct hand position after a closeout. It helps the player contest shots without reaching at the ball.
drills.safety: No swiping. Defender stays out of the shooter's landing space.

drills.name: Closeout Baseline Cutoff
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: The offensive player or coach starts on the wing. The defender closes out from the paint and shades the baseline side. The offensive player points baseline or middle, and the defender takes one controlled containment step. No live drive.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players who give up baseline after closeouts. Triggers: Assign if the player closes out square and gives up easy baseline drives. Avoid/modify: Use cones to show the baseline path first. Focus: Best for closeout angle, baseline containment, foot placement, and balance.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the defender to close out and take away the baseline path without over-running the play. It builds closeout angle control.
drills.safety: No live drive until the defender can stop without contact.

drills.name: Closeout Middle Shade
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: The defender closes out to the wing. The coach calls "no middle." The defender lands slightly angled, with the top foot placed to discourage the middle drive. Hold one second, then reset. Work both wings.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players who close out flat and give up the middle. Triggers: Assign if the player lets the ball drive middle after every closeout. Avoid/modify: Use no ball and foot-angle checks first. Focus: Best for no-middle positioning, closeout balance, foot angle, and stance discipline.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the defender to close out and shade the ball away from the middle. It helps players control driving angles.
drills.safety: No lunging into the ball handler. Angle with feet, not contact.

drills.name: Closeout Pump Fake Stay Down
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: The defender closes out to a coach with the ball. The coach gives a slow pump fake. The defender keeps feet down, hands high, and then resets into stance. Add one slide only after the athlete stays down consistently.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players who jump at pump fakes. Triggers: Assign if the player leaves the floor on every fake. Avoid/modify: Use stationary pump-fake discipline before closeouts. Focus: Best for pump-fake discipline, foul prevention, closeout control, and balance.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the defender to stay down on a pump fake, then recover into contest position. It helps reduce fouls.
drills.safety: No jumping into the shooter. Stay down and balanced.

drills.name: Closeout Rebound Locate
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: The defender closes out to a coach. On "shot," the defender turns to find a partner or cone behind them, makes a safe box-out shape, then releases to catch a soft rebound toss. Work both sides.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players who ball-watch after a closeout. Triggers: Assign if the player contests and then watches the ball without finding anyone. Avoid/modify: Use cone-only locate if contact readiness is low. Focus: Best for closeout recovery, locate habit, box-out timing, and rebound security.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the defender to close out, hear "shot," and immediately locate a player before looking for the rebound. It builds the find-before-ball habit.
drills.safety: No pushing. Locate, hold space, then get the ball.

drills.name: Closeout Shot-Long Rebound
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: The defender closes out to a coach on the wing. The coach calls "shot" and tosses the ball toward the free throw line or opposite elbow area. The defender turns, tracks, moves to the ball, and secures it.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players who close out and then stay frozen. Triggers: Assign if the player expects every rebound to fall near the rim. Avoid/modify: Use shorter tosses if tracking or movement is poor. Focus: Best for long-rebound tracking, closeout recovery, movement to ball, and secure catch.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the defender that a closeout can lead to a long rebound. It helps players step out instead of standing under the rim.
drills.safety: One player at a time. No diving for the ball.

drills.name: Closeout Weak-Side Crash Read
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: The defender closes out from the paint to the wing. The coach tosses the ball off the backboard or into the air toward the weak side. The defender turns, crosses the lane under control, and secures the ball.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players learning weak-side rebound movement after a closeout. Triggers: Assign if the player closes out and never moves to the weak side rebound. Avoid/modify: Use a soft air toss before backboard tosses. Focus: Best for weak-side tracking, closeout-to-board transition, body control, and catch security.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the defender to close out, then read a weak-side rebound angle. It builds awareness that misses often move away from the shot side.
drills.safety: No sprinting across crowded lanes. Clear the space first.

drills.name: Stunt Recover Box Out
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: The defender starts one pass away. The coach with the ball shows a drive cue. The defender takes one short stunt step, recovers to their cone or partner, then boxes out on "shot." No live drive.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players learning to help and still rebound. Triggers: Assign if the player helps but loses their rebounding matchup. Avoid/modify: Use no box-out contact if the athlete cannot recover safely. Focus: Best for stunt control, recovery timing, box-out reaction, and possession finish.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the defender to stunt toward the ball, recover, then box out when the shot goes up. It connects help defense with rebounding.
drills.safety: No live drive. Stunt is one short step.

drills.name: Gap Help Recover Contest
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: The defender starts between a ball coach and a wing shooter. On "help," the defender steps toward the ball. On "recover," the defender closes out to the wing shooter and contests hands high. No shot block.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players learning help-and-recover timing. Triggers: Assign if the player helps too far or recovers out of control. Avoid/modify: Use walking pace before adding speed. Focus: Best for gap help, recovery closeout, contest control, and court awareness.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the defender to help in the gap, recover to the shooter, and contest under control. It builds team defense footwork.
drills.safety: No running into the shooter. Recover under control.

drills.name: Help Recover Rebound
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: The defender starts in help position. The coach calls "recover," and the defender closes to a shooter cone. Coach calls "shot," and the defender turns to locate a cone or passive partner, boxes out, then secures a soft toss.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players who recover but forget to rebound. Triggers: Assign if the player moves well on defense but watches rebounds. Avoid/modify: Remove rebound toss until the sequence is clean. Focus: Best for help recovery, box-out reaction, rebound tracking, and finish-possession habits.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the defender to help, recover, and rebound after the shot. It keeps the athlete from thinking the rep ends at recovery.
drills.safety: No contact battle. Sequence first, speed second.

drills.name: Nail Help X-Out
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: Two defenders and two offensive spots are set on the perimeter. One defender helps toward the nail. Coach passes to the opposite spot. The two defenders communicate and X-out to cover both shooters. Walk first.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players learning two-player recovery rotations. Triggers: Assign if defenders both run to the same shooter or fail to talk. Avoid/modify: Use cone spots before live offensive players. Focus: Best for rotation timing, communication, closeout control, and team defense awareness.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the defender to help at the nail, then X-out to recover to the open shooter. It builds intermediate rotation timing.
drills.safety: Walk first. No crossing paths at high speed.

drills.name: Corner Help X-Out
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: Set one offensive player in the corner and one on the wing. The corner defender steps into help. The coach passes to the wing or corner. The defenders call "mine" and "yours," then close out to the correct player.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players learning corner help rotations. Triggers: Assign if the corner helper gets stuck and leaves a shooter open. Avoid/modify: Use cones and coach calls before live passes. Focus: Best for corner help, X-out timing, communication, and closeout angle.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches a corner defender to help, then recover through an X-out rotation. It builds corner-to-wing communication.
drills.safety: No sprinting into the same closeout lane. Talk early.

drills.name: Baseline Help Rotate
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: A coach starts on the wing with the ball. The defender starts in help near the lane. Coach shows a baseline drive cue. The defender steps to stop the lane, then recovers to the receiver the coach passes to.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players learning baseline help responsibilities. Triggers: Assign if the player watches baseline drives without helping or overhelps and cannot recover. Avoid/modify: Use no pass first if the help step is poor. Focus: Best for baseline help, rotation timing, closeout recovery, and communication.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the defender to help on a baseline drive and rotate to cover the next pass. It builds intermediate help defense.
drills.safety: No live baseline drive. Coach cues only.

drills.name: Sink and Fill Rebound
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: The defender starts on the weak side. Coach moves the ball to the opposite wing. The defender sinks toward the lane. On "shot," the defender steps into rebounding space and catches a soft toss.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players learning weak-side defensive rebounding. Triggers: Assign if the player stays too wide and misses weak-side rebounds. Avoid/modify: Use no toss first if positioning is confusing. Focus: Best for weak-side positioning, help sink, rebound space, and ball tracking.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the defender to sink into help position, then fill the rebounding space when the shot goes up. It helps weak-side players rebound.
drills.safety: No crowding under the rim. One rebounder at a time.

drills.name: Low-Man Tag and Rebound
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: A cone or passive teammate rolls toward the paint. The low defender takes one tag step, then coach calls "shot." The defender turns to box out a cone or partner and secures a soft rebound toss.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players learning low-man responsibility. Triggers: Assign if the player tags the roller but forgets the rebound. Avoid/modify: Use cone-only roller if contact or timing is unsafe. Focus: Best for low-man tag, recover timing, box-out reaction, and rebound security.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the low defender to tag a cutter or roller, then turn and rebound. It connects help responsibility with possession finish.
drills.safety: No body collision with the roller. Tag is a step, not a hit.

drills.name: Weak-Side Corner Crack Back Box
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: The defender starts in the weak-side corner. Coach calls "shot" from the opposite wing. The defender steps inside, finds a cone or passive partner, boxes out, then releases to secure a soft toss.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players who stay in the corner during rebounds. Triggers: Assign if the player watches from the corner instead of entering the rebound. Avoid/modify: Use cone-only box-out if contact is not safe. Focus: Best for weak-side crack back, box-out angle, rebound timing, and ball security.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches a weak-side corner defender to crack back and box out when the shot comes from the opposite side. It helps with weak-side rebounding habits.
drills.safety: No blind contact from behind. Defender must see the space before moving.

drills.name: Split-Rebound Read
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: The coach tosses the ball either short near the lane or long toward the elbow. The player starts in rebounding position, reads the toss, moves to the ball, catches with two hands, and secures.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players learning rebound direction reads. Triggers: Assign if the player guesses before reading the ball. Avoid/modify: Use verbal short/long calls first. Focus: Best for rebound read, first-step reaction, ball tracking, and secure catch.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the player to read whether the rebound is short or long and move to the right space. It builds reaction and tracking.
drills.safety: One rebounder only. No diving.

drills.name: High-Point Rebound and Land
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: Coach tosses the ball slightly above the athlete's comfortable reach. The player jumps only if safe, catches with two hands, lands balanced, and freezes. Use reach-only reps if jumping mechanics are not ready.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players with safe landing control who need better high-point timing. Triggers: Assign if the player waits too long and catches rebounds low. Avoid/modify: Use no-jump reaches if the athlete lands poorly. Focus: Best for high-point timing, two-hand catch, landing control, and rebound confidence.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the player to catch the ball at a higher point and land under control. It helps players avoid waiting for the ball to fall too low.
drills.safety: No max jumps. Stop if knees, ankles, or back hurt.

drills.name: Second-Jump Rebound Control
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: Coach tosses the ball off the backboard. The player reaches for the first rebound. If the coach taps or redirects the ball softly, the player resets the feet and catches the second toss. No contact.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players learning second-effort rebounding without chaos. Triggers: Assign if the player gives up after missing the first rebound. Avoid/modify: Use no-jump second catch if landing control is poor. Focus: Best for second-jump timing, reset balance, reaction, and catch security.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the player to recover after missing the first rebound and secure the second bounce. It builds controlled second effort.
drills.safety: No repeated max jumping. Short sets only.

drills.name: Rebound Tap-Control Catch
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: Coach tosses the ball slightly away from the player. The player taps it softly upward or toward their own space, then catches with two hands and secures. Start low and slow.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players who bat rebounds away instead of controlling them. Triggers: Assign if the player slaps rebounds randomly. Avoid/modify: Use direct two-hand catches if tap control is unsafe. Focus: Best for tap control, hand touch, rebound tracking, and ball security.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the player to control a ball they cannot fully grab, then secure it. It helps with tipped rebounds without slapping the ball away.
drills.safety: No tipping over other players. One athlete at a time.

drills.name: Rebound Tip-Out Read
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: Coach tosses the ball slightly outside the player's clean catch range. A teammate stands in a safe outlet spot. If the player can catch, they secure. If not, they tip softly to the teammate. Coach grades the decision.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players learning controlled team rebounding. Triggers: Assign if the player tips every ball or tries to grab impossible rebounds. Avoid/modify: Use catch-only reps if the player cannot control tips. Focus: Best for rebound decision, tip direction, teammate awareness, and hand control.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the player to tip the ball to a teammate only when they cannot secure it. It builds rebound decision-making.
drills.safety: No hard slaps. Teammate must be ready.

drills.name: Rebound Tip-Back to Self
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: The player stands near the rim with the ball. They toss or tap the ball lightly off the backboard, move one step, catch with two hands, land balanced, and secure. Keep reps short.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players learning controlled rebound touch. Triggers: Assign if the player cannot control rebounds off the board. Avoid/modify: Use coach toss instead of self tap if timing is poor. Focus: Best for rebound touch, backboard control, tracking, and landing balance.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the player to tip the ball off the backboard or into the air and then secure it. It helps with body control and touch.
drills.safety: No crowded rim. No repeated high jumps.

drills.name: Rebound Through Hands
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: The player catches a soft rebound toss. A coach lightly taps the ball with open hands for one second while the player holds it tight. The player then pivots and outlets. Pressure is light.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players who lose the ball after rebounds. Triggers: Assign if the player catches the rebound but loses it to light pressure. Avoid/modify: Use no taps if the athlete has finger or wrist pain. Focus: Best for rebound strength, ball security, pivot control, and outlet readiness.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the player to secure the ball through light hand pressure without swinging elbows. It builds ball strength after the rebound.
drills.safety: Light taps only. No ripping, grabbing, or elbow swinging.

drills.name: Rebound Chin Pivot Outlet
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: Coach tosses a rebound. The player catches, chins the ball, pivots away from a cone pressure marker, and passes to an outlet target. Work both pivot directions.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players who rebound but rush the outlet. Triggers: Assign if the player travels, drops the ball, or throws blind outlets. Avoid/modify: Use no outlet pass until pivot control is safe. Focus: Best for rebound security, pivot control, outlet timing, and pass accuracy.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the player to secure the rebound, chin it, pivot, and make a clean outlet pass. It builds calm possession control.
drills.safety: No swinging elbows. Pivot before passing.

drills.name: Rebound Outlet Pressure Read
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: The player catches a rebound toss. Two outlet targets show hands. A coach shades one target. The rebounder pivots away from pressure and passes to the open outlet.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players learning outlet decisions. Triggers: Assign if the player always outlets to the same side even when covered. Avoid/modify: Use one outlet first if the read is too hard. Focus: Best for outlet read, rebound protection, pivot awareness, and pass accuracy.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the rebounder to choose the safe outlet when one target is covered. It builds decision-making after the board.
drills.safety: No defender grabbing at the rebounder. Coach shades only.

drills.name: Rebound Push Outlet
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: The player catches a rebound. A receiver sprints or jogs to the sideline outlet spot. The rebounder pivots, sees the target, and throws a controlled outlet pass. Use shorter distance first.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players learning transition outlet passing. Triggers: Assign if the player secures the rebound but cannot start transition safely. Avoid/modify: Shorten the outlet if pass strength is low. Focus: Best for outlet distance, passing strength, rebound security, and transition awareness.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the rebounder to secure the ball and make a controlled push outlet to start transition. It helps players connect rebounding to offense.
drills.safety: No long hard outlets beyond the athlete's strength.

drills.name: Rebound Fake Outlet Pivot
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: The player catches a rebound toss. A coach shades the first outlet. The player gives a tight outlet fake, pivots, and passes to the second outlet. Keep the fake controlled.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players who force the first outlet pass. Triggers: Assign if the player throws outlets into pressure. Avoid/modify: Use no fake if the player swings the ball wide. Focus: Best for outlet fake, pivot control, ball security, and decision-making.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the rebounder to fake one outlet and pivot to the safer outlet. It helps against pressure after rebounds.
drills.safety: No elbow swing on the fake. Keep the ball tight.

drills.name: Rebound Turn Up Floor
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: The player catches a rebound toss, pivots to face upcourt, and either outlets to a receiver or holds if the coach says "stop." The decision is controlled and simple.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players learning what to do after defensive rebounds. Triggers: Assign if the player rebounds and looks down or panics. Avoid/modify: Use turn-and-hold before outlet passes. Focus: Best for upcourt vision, rebound security, pivot speed, and outlet decision.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the player to secure the rebound, turn up the floor, and make a controlled first decision. It builds transition awareness.
drills.safety: No blind outlet. Eyes up before pass.

drills.name: Outlet to Trailer Read
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: The player rebounds a soft toss. One outlet is on the sideline, and one trailer is behind or middle. The coach shades the sideline outlet. The rebounder pivots and passes to the trailer.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players learning second outlet options. Triggers: Assign if the player only sees the sideline outlet and misses the trailer. Avoid/modify: Use stationary trailer target first. Focus: Best for trailer vision, outlet decision, pivot control, and pass accuracy.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the rebounder to outlet to a trailing teammate when the sideline outlet is covered. It builds second-option outlet vision.
drills.safety: No blind backward outlet. Turn and see the trailer.

drills.name: Box-Out Swim Resistance
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: The defender boxes out a partner. The partner gives a slow light swim move to one side. The defender moves feet to keep position for 2 seconds, then releases. No wrestling.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players ready for light box-out contact. Triggers: Assign if the player loses box-out position against light movement. Avoid/modify: Use cone box-outs if contact readiness is low. Focus: Best for box-out contact, foot adjustment, balance, and discipline.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the rebounder to hold box-out position against a light swim move without pushing or grabbing. It builds contact control.
drills.safety: Light resistance only. No grabbing, pushing, or wrestling.

drills.name: Box-Out Spin Seal
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: The defender boxes out a passive partner. The partner slowly spins to one side. The defender steps and re-seals without holding or pushing. Hold for one count, then reset.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players who lose box-outs when opponents move around them. Triggers: Assign if the player boxes out once but cannot adjust when the opponent moves. Avoid/modify: Use cone movement first if contact is unsafe. Focus: Best for re-seal footwork, box-out balance, contact awareness, and hip position.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the defender to recover box-out position when the offensive player tries to spin around. It builds footwork and balance.
drills.safety: No holding the partner. Move the feet.

drills.name: Box-Out Reverse Seal
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: The defender starts boxing out. The partner slowly moves from one shoulder to the other. The defender turns the hips, re-seals, and holds position. Then reset.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players learning to adjust box-out angle. Triggers: Assign if the player loses position after first contact. Avoid/modify: Use a cone walkthrough if partner movement is too much. Focus: Best for box-out adjustment, hip turn, balance, and position recovery.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the player to reverse the box-out angle when the opponent moves across the back. It helps with rebounding position recovery.
drills.safety: No pushing backward. Re-seal with feet and hips.

drills.name: Box-Out Release Timing
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: The defender boxes out a cone or passive partner. Coach tosses the ball. The defender holds for one count, then releases to the ball, catches with two hands, and secures. Vary the toss direction.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players who either leave early or hold too long. Triggers: Assign if the player boxes out but never gets the ball, or leaves too early. Avoid/modify: Use cone-only box-out if contact is not safe. Focus: Best for release timing, box-out discipline, rebound tracking, and secure catch.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the player when to stop holding the box out and go get the rebound. It builds timing and possession finish.
drills.safety: No pushing off to release. Step to the ball.

drills.name: Hit-Get-Outlet Sequence
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: The defender turns to a cone or passive partner, makes safe box-out position for one count, releases to catch a soft toss, chins the ball, pivots, and outlets to a teammate. Work both sides.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players who know parts of rebounding but not the full sequence. Triggers: Assign if the player boxes out but forgets the ball, or rebounds but forgets the outlet. Avoid/modify: Remove outlet until the box-out and catch are safe. Focus: Best for sequence memory, box-out timing, ball security, and outlet accuracy.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the player the full sequence: make contact safely, get the ball, and outlet. It builds a complete rebounding habit.
drills.safety: No live battle. Learn the order first.

drills.name: Box-Out Across Lane
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: The defender starts on one block. On "shot," the defender crosses the lane under control, finds a cone or passive partner on the opposite block, boxes out, then catches a soft toss.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players learning rotation rebounding. Triggers: Assign if the player rotates on defense but does not rebound from the new position. Avoid/modify: Walk across first if body control is poor. Focus: Best for lane-crossing control, rotation rebound, box-out angle, and ball security.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the player to cross the lane, find a body, and box out from a new angle. It helps with rebounding after rotations.
drills.safety: No sprinting across traffic. Clear the lane.

drills.name: Free Throw Box-Out Read
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: Players line up in free throw rebounding spots or use cones. On the shot cue, the defender waits until release, steps into legal box-out position, then tracks a soft rebound toss. No live wrestling.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players learning free throw rebounding discipline. Triggers: Assign if the player steps early or forgets to box out on free throws. Avoid/modify: Use cone spots before live players. Focus: Best for free throw timing, lane discipline, box-out angle, and rebound tracking.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the player to read the free throw shot and box out without stepping early. It builds lane discipline.
drills.safety: No early stepping, pushing, or lane contact battles.

drills.name: Free Throw Opposite-Side Board
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: The player starts in a legal lane rebounding spot. Coach tosses or shoots a soft miss toward the opposite side. The player boxes out the cone or passive partner, then moves to secure the ball.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players who freeze in free throw rebound spots. Triggers: Assign if the player watches free throw misses instead of moving to the ball. Avoid/modify: Use slow tosses before real misses. Focus: Best for free throw tracking, opposite-side movement, box-out discipline, and secure catch.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the player that free throw rebounds can come to the opposite side. It helps with tracking and movement from lane spots.
drills.safety: One active rebounder at first. No lane collisions.

drills.name: Free Throw Outlet After Board
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: The player starts in a lane spot. Coach tosses a soft free throw-style miss. The player boxes out a cone or partner, secures the rebound, pivots, and outlets to a guard target.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players learning free throw rebound outlet habits. Triggers: Assign if the player rebounds free throws and immediately travels or throws wild passes. Avoid/modify: Use no outlet until rebound security improves. Focus: Best for free throw rebound security, pivot control, outlet timing, and pass accuracy.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the player to secure a free throw rebound and outlet without rushing. It connects lane rebounding to possession control.
drills.safety: No swinging elbows in lane spots.

drills.name: Back-Tap Rebound Save
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: Coach tosses the ball just beyond the player's secure catch range. A teammate stands behind. The player back-taps softly to the teammate, then lands or resets balanced. Use no jump first if needed.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players learning controlled rebound saves. Triggers: Assign if the player tips rebounds randomly or tries unsafe catches. Avoid/modify: Use regular two-hand rebound catch if tap control is poor. Focus: Best for back-tap control, teammate awareness, rebound decision, and landing safety.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the player to back-tap a rebound to a teammate when they cannot secure it safely. It builds controlled save decisions.
drills.safety: No jumping into other players. Teammate must be ready.

drills.name: Save and Balance Rebound
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: Coach tosses the ball near a sideline or baseline marker with plenty of space. The player moves to the ball, catches or controls it, lands inbounds if possible, and passes safely to a teammate. No diving.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players learning safe boundary rebound decisions. Triggers: Assign if the player throws wild saves or steps out without control. Avoid/modify: Move farther from boundary if safety space is limited. Focus: Best for boundary awareness, save decision, body control, and pass accuracy.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the player to save a rebound near a boundary while staying balanced and safe. It helps avoid wild saves.
drills.safety: No diving, sliding, or saving into walls or benches.

drills.name: Sideline Rebound Save Outlet
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: Coach tosses the ball toward the sideline. The player moves under control, secures or saves the ball inbounds, then passes to an outlet target. The coach grades control, not speed.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players who panic near the sideline. Triggers: Assign if the player saves the ball blindly to the other team. Avoid/modify: Use a cone boundary first if the real sideline is too tight. Focus: Best for sideline awareness, rebound save, outlet vision, and pass control.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the player to secure or save a sideline rebound and find a calm outlet. It builds decision control near the line.
drills.safety: No diving. Check sideline space before starting.

drills.name: Baseline Rebound Save Read
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: Coach tosses the ball near the baseline with safe space. If the ball is clearly playable, the player saves to a teammate. If not, the coach says "leave," and the player lets it go. No diving.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players learning boundary decision-making. Triggers: Assign if the player saves every ball blindly or gives up on playable balls. Avoid/modify: Use coach calls before independent reads. Focus: Best for baseline awareness, save judgment, teammate vision, and body control.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the player to read whether to save a baseline rebound or let it go. It builds smarter possession decisions.
drills.safety: No diving or twisting into the stanchion.

drills.name: Loose Ball Sweep and Outlet
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: Coach rolls the ball across the lane. The player moves to it, sweeps it into two hands, secures at the chest, pivots, and outlets to a teammate. Work both directions.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players learning controlled loose-ball recovery. Triggers: Assign if the player kicks, slaps, or panics around loose balls. Avoid/modify: Use a still ball first if rolling pickup is unsafe. Focus: Best for loose-ball pickup, body control, pivot control, and outlet accuracy.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the player to sweep a loose ball into two hands and make a safe outlet. It builds loose-ball control without diving.
drills.safety: No diving. Bend knees and secure first.

drills.name: Loose Ball Race Control
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: Two players start 6-8 feet from a slowly rolled ball. On "go," both move toward it. The first player to arrive must secure with two hands and pivot away. The second player stops short. No diving or grabbing.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players ready for controlled loose-ball competition. Triggers: Assign if the player avoids loose balls or attacks them recklessly. Avoid/modify: Use one-player loose-ball drills if safety is poor. Focus: Best for loose-ball reaction, body control, ball security, and competitive discipline.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the player to compete for a loose ball while staying safe and under control. It adds light competition without diving.
drills.safety: No diving, sliding, pushing, or grabbing.

drills.name: Loose Ball Shoulder Check
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: Coach rolls the ball. The player secures it, performs a quick shoulder check to the coach's side cue, then pivots away and outlets. Start slow.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players who secure loose balls but turn into pressure. Triggers: Assign if the player picks up loose balls and immediately turns into defenders. Avoid/modify: Use verbal "left/right" before shoulder checks. Focus: Best for loose-ball awareness, shoulder check, pivot decision, and outlet pass.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the player to check surroundings before turning with a loose ball. It helps avoid turning into pressure.
drills.safety: Secure first. Do not twist quickly with the ball low.

drills.name: Loose Ball to Jump Ball Tie-Up
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: The player secures a rolled ball. A coach places hands lightly on the ball for one second. The player holds tight with two hands, keeps elbows safe, and waits for the whistle cue. No ripping or twisting.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players who lose loose balls when someone reaches in. Triggers: Assign if the player secures the ball but gives it up under light pressure. Avoid/modify: Avoid if wrist, finger, or shoulder pain appears. Focus: Best for loose-ball strength, two-hand security, composure, and elbow safety.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the player to secure a loose ball and protect it when a defender arrives. It builds safe tie-up strength without wrestling.
drills.safety: No pulling, twisting, or wrestling. Coach pressure is light.

drills.name: Transition Stop the Ball
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: A ball handler dribbles slowly up the middle. The defender starts back and angles in to stop the ball near a cone. Defender shows hands and contains for one count. No live drive past the defender.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players learning transition ball-stopping responsibility. Triggers: Assign if the player retreats too far or fouls trying to stop transition. Avoid/modify: Use walking speed first. Focus: Best for transition angle, contain stance, stop control, and foul prevention.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the defender to stop the ball in transition without fouling. It helps players slow the drive and buy time for teammates.
drills.safety: No charges or collisions. Ball handler stays controlled.

drills.name: Transition Wall-Up
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: A ball handler dribbles toward the lane at half speed. The defender retreats, stops in legal position, raises both hands straight up, and holds. No contact finish is allowed.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players learning safe transition contesting. Triggers: Assign if the player swipes down or jumps into drivers. Avoid/modify: Use no ball handler and a cone drive line first. Focus: Best for wall-up control, verticality, stop balance, and foul prevention.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the defender to retreat, stop, and wall up without jumping into the offensive player. It builds vertical contest discipline.
drills.safety: No body contact. Offensive player stops before contact.

drills.name: Transition Match-Up Talk
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: Three offensive players jog into the frontcourt. Three defenders retreat. Coach calls "match." Defenders point, call a matchup, and stop in stance. No live offense at first.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players learning transition communication. Triggers: Assign if defenders are quiet or double-team the same player in transition. Avoid/modify: Use three cones instead of offensive players first. Focus: Best for transition communication, matchup recognition, spacing, and stance reset.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches defenders to talk and match up in transition. It helps teams avoid guarding the same player.
drills.safety: Jog speed only. No live transition until matchups are clear.

drills.name: Transition Box-Out Trailer
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: One offensive trailer jogs in behind the play. The defender starts in the paint, locates the trailer on "shot," boxes out safely, then secures a soft rebound toss. Work both sides.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players who forget trailers on rebounds. Triggers: Assign if the player watches the ball and lets trailers rebound. Avoid/modify: Use a cone trailer before live movement. Focus: Best for trailer awareness, transition box-out, locate habit, and rebound security.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the defender to find a trailer after transition defense and box out before the shot. It helps with late-arriving rebounders.
drills.safety: No blind contact. Defender must see the trailer.

drills.name: Transition Find Nearest Body
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: Three offensive players spread out. Coach calls "shot." Each defender finds the nearest offensive player, makes safe box-out position, and holds for one count. Add a soft rebound after clean reps.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players learning transition rebounding matchups. Triggers: Assign if players stand still after transition shots. Avoid/modify: Use cones instead of players if contact is unsafe. Focus: Best for nearest-body recognition, transition rebounding, communication, and box-out angle.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the defender to find the closest offensive player after a transition shot. It builds fast rebounding awareness.
drills.safety: No hard contact. Find and hold only.

drills.name: Two-on-Two Closeout Rebound
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: Two offensive players stand wing and corner. Two defenders start in help positions. Coach passes to one offensive player. Both defenders close out or help appropriately. Coach calls "shot," and defenders box out and rebound. No live scoring at first.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players learning paired closeout and rebounding. Triggers: Assign if two defenders both close to the ball or leave rebounders free. Avoid/modify: Use cone offensive spots first. Focus: Best for two-player communication, closeout assignment, help positioning, and rebound finish.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches two defenders to close out, contain, and rebound together. It builds communication in a small-sided setting.
drills.safety: No live drives until closeout and rebound jobs are clear.

drills.name: Two-on-Two Box-Out Advantage
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: Two offensive players move slowly around the lane and wing area. Coach calls "shot." The two defenders find the nearest player, box out safely, and secure a soft toss. Rotate roles.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players learning rebounding communication with movement. Triggers: Assign if defenders lose moving rebounders. Avoid/modify: Use cones or walking speed if movement is too hard. Focus: Best for box-out communication, nearest-player recognition, movement rebounding, and ball security.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches two defenders to box out when the offense has movement. It helps players communicate and find bodies.
drills.safety: Walking movement first. No pushing.

drills.name: Three-on-Three Shell Rebound Freeze
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: Three offensive players move the ball around the perimeter. Three defenders adjust in shell position at walking or jog speed. Coach calls "shot." Defenders freeze, identify matchups, box out, then reset.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players learning shell-to-rebound habits. Triggers: Assign if defenders move in shell but forget rebounding assignments. Avoid/modify: Use 2-on-2 if three-player shell is too much. Focus: Best for shell positioning, matchup recognition, communication, and box-out readiness.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches three defenders to move in shell position, then freeze into rebounding matchups when the shot is called. It builds team awareness.
drills.safety: No live crash at first. Freeze and identify before contact.

drills.name: Three-on-Three Help Rotate Board
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: Three offensive players space around the perimeter. Coach dribbles or passes to create a help cue. Defenders rotate at half speed. Coach calls "shot," and each defender finds a body and rebounds.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players learning rotation-to-rebound responsibility. Triggers: Assign if players rotate but leave offensive rebounders free. Avoid/modify: Use walk-through rotations before adding rebound toss. Focus: Best for help rotation, communication, box-out assignment, and rebound finish.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches three defenders to help, rotate, and rebound after the rotation. It builds possession-finish habits in team defense.
drills.safety: No full-speed rotations until players can talk and stop safely.

drills.name: Three-on-Two Scramble Board
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: Three offensive players space around the arc. Two defenders start in the paint. Coach passes the ball around. Defenders close out and help at half speed. On "shot," defenders find the two most dangerous rebounders and secure the toss.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players learning scramble defense and rebounding. Triggers: Assign if defenders panic when outnumbered. Avoid/modify: Use 2-on-2 before 3-on-2. Focus: Best for scramble communication, closeout recovery, rebound priority, and decision-making.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches outnumbered defenders to scramble, contest, and rebound. It builds communication and calm recovery.
drills.safety: Half speed only. No live contact rebounding until safe.

drills.name: Four-Spot Closeout Call
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: Four cones or offensive players are placed around the perimeter. Defenders start inside. Coach calls a spot number or name. The defender closes out, calls the spot, contests, and resets. Add rebound call later.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players learning multi-spot closeout reactions. Triggers: Assign if the player is slow to identify and close out to the correct spot. Avoid/modify: Use two spots first. Focus: Best for closeout reaction, communication, spot recognition, and stop balance.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches defenders to close out to different spots based on a coach call. It builds reaction and team communication.
drills.safety: No sprinting into cones or players. Control the stop.

drills.name: Four-Spot Closeout to Board
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: Four spots are marked around the perimeter. Coach calls one spot. Defender closes out there. Coach calls "shot" and tosses the ball to a realistic rebound area. Defender tracks and secures it.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players who need closeout-to-rebound range. Triggers: Assign if the player closes out but does not rebound from the new location. Avoid/modify: Use shorter closeouts and softer tosses first. Focus: Best for closeout range, rebound tracking, movement to ball, and possession finish.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches defenders to close out to a called spot and then rebound from that new position. It builds game-like possession habits.
drills.safety: One defender at a time until space is safe.

drills.name: Defensive Slide Sprint Recover
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: The defender slides between two cones, then coach calls "recover." The defender opens the hips, sprints three controlled steps to a recovery cone, and stops in stance. Work both directions.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players learning to recover without fouling. Triggers: Assign if the player gives up after getting beat or recovers out of control. Avoid/modify: Use jog recovery if sprint stop is unsafe. Focus: Best for hip turn, recovery sprint, stop control, and stance reset.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the player to slide, turn, recover, and stop in stance. It builds recovery control after being beaten.
drills.safety: No hard stop if ankles or knees are unstable.

drills.name: Defensive Turn and Chase Angle
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: A partner jogs from wing to lane line. The defender starts slightly behind, opens the hips, and runs to cut off the angle at a cone. The defender stops short and does not bump.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players learning recovery angles. Triggers: Assign if the player chases from behind and fouls. Avoid/modify: Use cone path only if partner movement is too hard. Focus: Best for chase angle, hip turn, body control, and stop distance.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the defender to turn and chase at an angle instead of running behind the offensive player. It helps with recovery positioning.
drills.safety: No bumping from behind. Defender stops short.

drills.name: Cut-Off Sprint to Wall-Up
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: The defender starts on the wing. Coach points to the lane. Defender sprints under control to a cone, stops, raises hands straight up, and holds. Add a controlled ball handler only after clean reps.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players who foul after late recoveries. Triggers: Assign if the player recovers late and jumps into the driver. Avoid/modify: Use jog speed if the stop is unsafe. Focus: Best for recovery speed, stop control, verticality, and foul prevention.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the defender to recover to the lane, stop, and wall up. It helps prevent chase fouls near the rim.
drills.safety: No collision at the cone. Stop before hands go up.

drills.name: Chase-Down Stay Down
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: A ball handler jogs to the rim or a cone finish area. The defender trails one step behind, runs to the side, shows hands, and stays down. No block attempt is allowed. The offensive player stops before contact.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players who foul on chase-down attempts. Triggers: Assign if the player swipes from behind or jumps into the driver. Avoid/modify: Use cone runner if live movement is unsafe. Focus: Best for chase discipline, hand control, foul prevention, and body control.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the defender to chase from behind but stay down instead of swiping or jumping into the offensive player. It builds discipline.
drills.safety: No blocks, no swipes, no contact from behind.

drills.name: Trail Contest to Rebound
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: The defender starts behind a coach or partner. The offensive player stops for a controlled shot fake or soft shot cue. Defender contests from the side without contact, then turns to rebound a soft toss.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players learning recovery contest plus rebound. Triggers: Assign if the player contests from behind but forgets to rebound. Avoid/modify: Use no shot cue if trailing contest is unsafe. Focus: Best for trail contest, recovery balance, rebound reaction, and possession finish.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches a trailing defender to contest safely, then rebound. It helps players finish the possession after recovering.
drills.safety: Defender must not run into the shooter. Contest from the side.

drills.name: Trail Rebound Locate
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: The defender trails into the play. Coach calls "shot." The defender points to the nearest offensive player or cone, boxes out safely, and then secures a soft rebound toss.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players who trail the play and ball-watch. Triggers: Assign if the player arrives late and watches instead of finding a body. Avoid/modify: Use cones first. Focus: Best for late-arrival awareness, locate habit, transition box-out, and rebound security.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches a trailing defender to locate the nearest rebounder after arriving late. It helps with transition rebounding.
drills.safety: No blind contact into a player. Locate first.

drills.name: Stance Hold to Burst Closeout
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: The defender holds a comfortable stance for 4 seconds. Coach points to a cone or wing spot. Defender bursts at controlled speed, chops feet, and stops in closeout position.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players who lose stance energy before moving. Triggers: Assign if the player stands upright before closing out. Avoid/modify: Shorten stance hold if legs or knees struggle. Focus: Best for stance endurance, burst control, closeout stop, and lower-body strength.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the player to hold a stance briefly, then burst into a controlled closeout. It builds leg strength and transition from stance to movement.
drills.safety: No long stance holds. Stop if knee or back pain appears.

drills.name: Slide-to-Closeout Combo
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: The defender starts at a cone, slides three steps to the side, then closes out to a coach or cone on the wing. The defender chops feet, raises hands, and freezes. Work both directions.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players ready to combine slide and closeout mechanics. Triggers: Assign if the player can slide and close out separately but not together. Avoid/modify: Reduce slide distance if form breaks. Focus: Best for footwork combination, lateral control, closeout balance, and hand activity.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the player to slide, then close out to a shooter. It combines two defensive movements in one rep.
drills.safety: No speed until both movements stay clean.

drills.name: Backpedal Closeout Combo
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: The defender backpedals 3 controlled steps, coach points to a wing spot, and the defender turns into a closeout. Finish with hands high and feet choppy.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players learning recovery-to-closeout movement. Triggers: Assign if the player backpedals well but cannot recover to the shooter. Avoid/modify: Use a jog turn instead of speed if balance is poor. Focus: Best for backpedal control, hip turn, closeout balance, and recovery speed.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the player to backpedal, turn, and close out under control. It helps with defensive recovery after retreating.
drills.safety: Check space behind the player. No backpedaling into traffic.

drills.name: Slide-Slide-Rebound
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: The defender slides right, slides left, then coach calls "shot." The defender turns to find a cone or partner, boxes out safely, and catches a soft rebound toss.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players who defend laterally but forget to rebound. Triggers: Assign if the player slides well but ball-watches on the shot. Avoid/modify: Use one slide each way if conditioning is low. Focus: Best for lateral endurance, shot reaction, box-out timing, and rebound security.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the player to slide twice, then turn and rebound. It connects lateral defense to finishing the possession.
drills.safety: No long slide sets. Quality over fatigue.

drills.name: Zig-Zag Contain Rebound
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: Use three cones in a zig-zag. A ball handler or coach walks/jogs the path. Defender contains without reaching. At the final cone, coach calls "shot," and defender locates and rebounds a soft toss.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players ready for short containment sequences. Triggers: Assign if the player defends the dribble but relaxes before the rebound. Avoid/modify: Use walking pace first. Focus: Best for containment, lateral stamina, rebound reaction, and ball tracking.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the defender to contain through a short zig-zag, then rebound when the shot goes up. It builds defensive stamina and awareness.
drills.safety: No full-speed live 1-on-1. Keep it controlled.

drills.name: Mirror Drive Cutoff
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: A ball handler dribbles slowly from wing to lane line. Defender mirrors the drive, keeps chest in front, and cuts off at a cone. The ball handler stops before contact. Work both sides.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players learning controlled on-ball defense. Triggers: Assign if the defender reaches instead of moving feet. Avoid/modify: Use no dribble and walking first. Focus: Best for on-ball containment, mirror control, angle cutoff, and reach discipline.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the defender to mirror a controlled drive and cut off the lane without reaching. It builds on-ball containment.
drills.safety: No contact drive. Ball handler stops before collision.

drills.name: One-on-One Contain No Reach
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: Offense starts on the wing with the ball. Defender guards for 4 seconds. Offense can use two controlled dribbles but cannot shoot. Defender's goal is to stay in front with hands out and no reach.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players ready for short live containment. Triggers: Assign if the defender reaches or fouls during short on-ball reps. Avoid/modify: Use shadow containment if live dribble is too much. Focus: Best for containment discipline, body control, hand discipline, and focus.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the defender to guard for a short time without reaching. It builds discipline and body control.
drills.safety: Short rep. No aggressive contact or reach-ins.

drills.name: One-on-One Shot Contest Board
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: Offense starts at the wing. Defender guards for one or two dribbles. Offense takes a controlled jumper or coach calls "shot." Defender contests without contact, then boxes out and rebounds.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players ready for short on-ball shot-contest reps. Triggers: Assign if the defender contests but forgets to box out. Avoid/modify: Use coach-shot cue instead of live shot first. Focus: Best for contest control, box-out reaction, rebound tracking, and foul prevention.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the defender to contest a controlled shot and then rebound. It connects on-ball defense to possession finish.
drills.safety: No landing-space contact. Defender boxes out after the shot.

drills.name: One-on-One Cutoff to Wall
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: Offense starts at the wing with two controlled dribbles. Defender shades the drive to a cone near the lane. When offense reaches the cone, defender stops and walls up. No contact finish.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players learning legal paint containment. Triggers: Assign if the defender cuts off drives but fouls at the end. Avoid/modify: Use walking speed if drive cutoff is unsafe. Focus: Best for drive cutoff, wall-up control, foul prevention, and stop balance.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the defender to cut off a drive and wall up without fouling. It helps with on-ball discipline near the paint.
drills.safety: No body collision. Offensive player stops at cone.

drills.name: One-on-One Baseline No Middle
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: Offense starts on the wing. Defender shades no middle. Offense can take two controlled dribbles toward baseline. Defender slides to contain and stop at a cone. No shot is required.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players learning defensive angle rules. Triggers: Assign if the player gives up the middle or reaches on baseline drives. Avoid/modify: Use coach as offense before live partner. Focus: Best for no-middle angle, baseline containment, lateral control, and hand discipline.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the defender to force the ball away from the middle and contain a short baseline path. It builds angle discipline.
drills.safety: No baseline sprinting into walls or stanchions.

drills.name: One-on-One Middle Cutoff
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: Offense starts at the wing and tries to take one or two controlled dribbles middle. Defender works to slide and cut off the path at a cone. The rep ends at the cone.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players who get beaten middle. Triggers: Assign if the defender opens the middle or reaches across the body. Avoid/modify: Use walking pace first. Focus: Best for middle containment, slide timing, body position, and foul prevention.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the defender to stop a middle drive with feet and chest position. It helps reduce reaching fouls.
drills.safety: No shoulder bumping. Stop the rep at the cone.

drills.name: One-on-One Late Clock Stop
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: Offense starts on the wing. Coach counts down from 5. Offense can use controlled dribbles but cannot initiate contact. Defender must stay in front, contest at the end, and then box out if shot is called.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players who foul late in possessions. Triggers: Assign if the defender plays well then fouls at the end. Avoid/modify: Use 3-second reps first. Focus: Best for late-clock discipline, containment focus, contest control, and box-out reaction.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the defender to guard for a short countdown without fouling. It helps players stay disciplined late in a possession.
drills.safety: No aggressive contact. Short reps only.

drills.name: Two-Shot Rebound Sprint
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: Coach tosses or shoots a soft miss. Player rebounds, outlets to coach, then immediately tracks a second soft miss from another angle. Do two rebounds per rep, then rest.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players ready for short rebound conditioning. Triggers: Assign if the player gets the first board but loses focus on the second. Avoid/modify: Use one rebound per rep if fatigue changes form. Focus: Best for rebound endurance, tracking consistency, outlet reset, and landing control.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the player to rebound two shots in a row while keeping tracking and landing control. It builds controlled rebounding endurance.
drills.safety: Two rebounds only, then rest. No fatigue jumping.

drills.name: Three-Angle Rebound Read
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: Coach tosses from wing, top, and corner angles. The player starts in the lane, reads the ball, moves to it, catches with two hands, and secures. Rotate angles every rep.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players learning shot-angle rebound reads. Triggers: Assign if the player moves before reading the ball or guesses wrong. Avoid/modify: Use two angles first. Focus: Best for angle tracking, first-step reaction, catch security, and rebound awareness.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the player to track rebounds from three shot angles. It helps players stop guessing where the ball will go.
drills.safety: One rebounder at a time. No diving.

drills.name: Rim Bounce High-Low Read
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: Coach softly tosses the ball onto the rim or near the rim. Some rebounds come high, some drop low. The player tracks, waits, moves, and secures with two hands.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players learning rim-bounce timing. Triggers: Assign if the player jumps early or reaches late on rim rebounds. Avoid/modify: Use air tosses if rim bounces are too unpredictable. Focus: Best for rim read, timing, patience, and secure catch.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the player to read whether the ball comes off high or low after a rim bounce. It builds timing and patience.
drills.safety: No crowd under rim. Keep tosses soft.

drills.name: Backboard Side Read
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: Coach tosses the ball off different spots on the backboard. The player starts centered, reads left or right, steps to the ball, catches, and secures. Work both sides.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players who misread backboard rebounds. Triggers: Assign if the player freezes or moves the wrong way off the backboard. Avoid/modify: Use predictable side calls first. Focus: Best for backboard read, lateral reaction, ball tracking, and catch security.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the player to read which side the ball leaves the backboard. It helps with lateral rebound reaction.
drills.safety: No crowded paint. One player at a time.

drills.name: Backboard Long-Carom Read
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: Coach tosses the ball hard enough to create a controlled long carom, but not dangerously. The player starts inside, reads the bounce, steps out, catches with two hands, and secures.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players who stay under the rim on long caroms. Triggers: Assign if the player watches long rebounds bounce away. Avoid/modify: Use softer caroms if tracking is poor. Focus: Best for long-carom read, step-out reaction, tracking, and ball security.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the player to read a long carom off the backboard and step out to secure it. It helps with rebounds that bounce away.
drills.safety: No chasing into other players. Clear the area.

drills.name: Rebound Over Shoulder Track
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: The player starts facing the coach. Coach tosses the ball gently over one shoulder. The player turns, tracks, catches with two hands, and lands balanced. Work both shoulders.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players learning over-shoulder rebound tracking. Triggers: Assign if the player loses balls that go behind them. Avoid/modify: Use lower tosses if tracking is difficult. Focus: Best for shoulder tracking, turn control, catch security, and balance.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the player to turn, track over the shoulder, and secure a rebound. It helps with balls that go behind the player.
drills.safety: No backpedaling into traffic. Turn first, then move.

drills.name: Rebound Spin Locate
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: The player starts facing away from the rim. Coach says "turn," and the player turns over the called shoulder, locates the ball toss, catches with two hands, and secures. Keep the turn controlled.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players who lose the ball after rotating. Triggers: Assign if the player rotates defensively and cannot find the rebound. Avoid/modify: Use slower turn and lower toss first. Focus: Best for body control, ball locate, rotation recovery, and catch security.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the player to turn from a spin or rotation and locate the rebound. It helps after defensive rotations.
drills.safety: No fast spinning if balance is poor or dizziness appears.

drills.name: Rebound Land Pivot Pass
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: Coach tosses a rebound. The player catches, lands balanced, pivots on the coach's left or right call, and outlets. The pass happens only after the feet are stable.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players who land from rebounds and rush. Triggers: Assign if the player travels or throws wild outlets after landing. Avoid/modify: Use no-jump catch if landing control is poor. Focus: Best for landing balance, pivot speed, outlet accuracy, and ball security.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the player to land from a rebound and immediately pivot into a safe outlet. It builds control after the catch.
drills.safety: Feet stable before pass. No swinging elbows.

drills.name: Rebound Land Contact Hold
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: The player catches a soft rebound toss and lands. A coach gives a light pad touch to the side after the landing. The player holds the ball tight for one second, then resets.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players ready for light post-rebound contact. Triggers: Assign if the player catches rebounds but loses balance from light pressure. Avoid/modify: Avoid if the athlete is not contact-ready or landing is poor. Focus: Best for post-rebound stability, contact readiness, ball security, and landing control.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the player to land with the rebound and hold balance through light body pressure. It builds contact readiness.
drills.safety: Pad touch after landing only. No airborne contact.

drills.name: Rebound Strong Base Partner Tap
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: The player holds the rebound at the chest or chin. A partner lightly taps the player's shoulder or forearm area with open hands while the player keeps base and ball secure. Then switch.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players who need stronger rebound base. Triggers: Assign if the player gets knocked off balance by light pressure. Avoid/modify: Use coach pad only if partner control is poor. Focus: Best for strong base, ball protection, contact balance, and composure.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the player to secure a rebound while staying strong through light partner taps. It builds lower-body base and ball protection.
drills.safety: Light taps only. No pushing, ripping, or wrestling.

drills.name: Rebound Contact Turn Away
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: Player catches a soft rebound toss. Coach steps to one side with hands up. Player pivots away from the coach, keeps the ball tight, and holds. Add outlet pass if safe.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players who expose the ball after rebounds. Triggers: Assign if the player turns into pressure after securing the ball. Avoid/modify: Use cone pressure first. Focus: Best for rebound protection, pressure awareness, pivot control, and ball security.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the player to turn away from pressure after securing a rebound. It helps protect the ball against nearby defenders.
drills.safety: No elbow swing. Pivot away under control.

drills.name: Box-Out to Second Ball
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: The player boxes out a cone or passive partner. Coach tosses the first ball fake or points one way, then tosses the real ball another way. The player releases and secures the real rebound.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players who lose focus after first contact. Triggers: Assign if the player boxes out but stops tracking the ball. Avoid/modify: Use one clear toss before adding a fake. Focus: Best for box-out focus, second reaction, rebound tracking, and ball security.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the player to box out one target, then react to a second ball direction. It builds focus and rebound tracking.
drills.safety: No sudden hard toss. Keep the fake simple.

drills.name: Rebound Read: Catch or Let Go
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: Coach tosses balls at different distances. If the ball is in safe range, the player calls "mine" and catches. If it is outside safe range, the player calls "yours" and lets the teammate secure it.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players learning rebound judgment. Triggers: Assign if the player overreaches or collides with teammates for rebounds. Avoid/modify: Use verbal coach calls first. Focus: Best for rebound judgment, communication, spatial awareness, and safety decision.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the player to decide whether a rebound is safe to catch or should be left to a teammate. It builds judgment and communication.
drills.safety: No diving or colliding. Communication wins.

drills.name: Two-Rebounder Communication
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: Two defenders start in the lane. Coach tosses a rebound. One player calls "ball," the other calls "box" and finds a cone or partner. Rotate roles. Keep tosses soft.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players learning team rebounding roles. Triggers: Assign if teammates collide or both watch the ball. Avoid/modify: Use one rebounder and one cone first. Focus: Best for rebound communication, role clarity, collision avoidance, and ball security.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches two rebounders to communicate who gets the ball and who boxes out. It reduces teammate collisions.
drills.safety: No two-player jumping until calls are clear.

drills.name: Three-Rebounder Zone Call
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: Three rebounders take left, middle, and right zones. Coach tosses the ball to one zone. The player in that zone calls "mine," secures the ball, and the other two hold box-out shapes. Rotate zones.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Teams learning organized rebounding coverage. Triggers: Assign if all players chase the same ball or no one covers weak-side space. Avoid/modify: Use two zones first. Focus: Best for zone awareness, communication, rebound coverage, and role discipline.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches three players to cover rebound zones and call the ball. It builds team rebounding organization.
drills.safety: No crossing zones at full speed. Call early.

drills.name: Rebound Outlet Under Call
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: The player catches a rebound toss. Two outlet receivers call "left" or "right," but only one shows hands. The rebounder listens, sees hands, pivots, and passes to the correct target.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players learning outlet communication. Triggers: Assign if the player outlets without listening or seeing the target. Avoid/modify: Use one outlet until control improves. Focus: Best for listening, outlet vision, pivot control, and passing accuracy.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the rebounder to outlet based on a teammate's call. It helps the player listen while protecting the ball.
drills.safety: Receiver must show hands. No blind outlet.

drills.name: Rebound Outlet Fake to Keep
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: The player secures a rebound. Coach shades the outlet target. The player shows a tight outlet fake, keeps the ball protected, and pivots away. Add a second outlet only after control improves.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players who force outlets into coverage. Triggers: Assign if the player throws to a covered outlet. Avoid/modify: Remove fake if the player swings elbows or travels. Focus: Best for outlet decision, fake control, ball security, and patience.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches the rebounder to fake the outlet and keep the ball when the outlet is covered. It prevents forced passes.
drills.safety: No wide fake or elbow swing. Keep ball tight.

drills.name: Defensive Communication Chain
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: Three defenders start in shell positions. Coach moves the ball. The on-ball defender calls "ball," help defender calls "help," coach calls "shot," and everyone calls "box" while finding their matchup. Reset after each rep.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Teams that are quiet on defense. Triggers: Assign if players know the movements but do not talk. Avoid/modify: Use two defenders first. Focus: Best for defensive communication, shell awareness, box-out reaction, and team discipline.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches players to communicate through a defensive sequence: ball, help, shot, box. It builds team language.
drills.safety: No live contact. Talk and position first.

drills.name: Call the Rotation
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: Three defenders stand in help positions. Coach passes to a new spot. The defender who rotates must call "I got ball," and the next defender calls "help." Freeze after each call to check spacing.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players learning rotation language. Triggers: Assign if players rotate silently or cover the same player. Avoid/modify: Use cones before offensive players. Focus: Best for rotation communication, help chain, spacing, and decision timing.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches defenders to call the rotation before they move. It helps avoid two players rotating to the same spot.
drills.safety: Freeze after rotations. No speed until calls are clear.

drills.name: Call the Box-Out Matchup
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: Three offensive players stand around the lane. Three defenders start in help positions. Coach calls "shot." Each defender points and calls their matchup, boxes out safely, then releases to the ball if it comes to them.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Teams that lose rebound matchups. Triggers: Assign if players all chase the ball and nobody claims a matchup. Avoid/modify: Use cones instead of offensive players first. Focus: Best for matchup ownership, box-out communication, rebound organization, and possession finish.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches each defender to call who they are boxing out before the rebound. It builds ownership and prevents confusion.
drills.safety: No pushing. Claim the matchup early.

drills.name: Finish Possession Scoreboard
drills.reps_target: Short, controlled sets; quality over volume
drills.instructions: Run a short 2-on-2 or 3-on-3 defensive rep at half speed. The defense earns 1 point for a controlled stop and 1 extra point for securing the rebound or loose ball. Offense earns 1 point for an offensive rebound. Keep reps short.
drills.coaching_notes: Best for: Players ready to connect defense and rebounding in small-sided reps. Triggers: Assign if the team plays defense but gives up second chances. Avoid/modify: Use no live scoring if players are not ready for contact or decision speed. Focus: Best for possession finish, defensive accountability, rebound effort, and communication.
drills.statistic: This drill teaches defenders that the possession is not over until the rebound is secured or the ball is controlled. It builds accountability.
drills.safety: Half speed first. No hard crashes, dives, or unsafe rebound battles.
